title: Brazil Regulator Warns That 30% of Crypto Exchanges Fail New Capital Rules
summary: Nearly one-third of the 120 cryptocurrency exchanges that filed to continue operating in Brazil as VASPs fail to reach the share capital required to operate in compliance with Central Bank regulations, meaning they could have their applications rejected after review.   Central Bank of Brazil Warns T...
content:
Nearly one-third of the 120 cryptocurrency exchanges that filed to continue operating in Brazil as VASPs fail to reach the share capital required to operate in compliance with Central Bank regulations, meaning they could have their applications rejected after review.

Key Takeaways

  • About 30% of 120 Brazilian crypto license applicants missed capital rules, risking mass operational rejections.
  • Many applicants also omitted required audited financials, raising fears of reduced market access for users.
  • Analysts suspect flawed filings are stalling tactics to delay a Nov. 6 banking blockade on unlicensed firms.

Central Bank of Brazil Warns That 30% of VASPs Fail to Comply With Capital Requirements

The virtual assets service provider market is facing a reconfiguration in Brazil, after the deadline for exchanges to file the requirements to become licensed and keep operating expired on Oct. 30.

While the central bank disclosed a list of 120 entities that applied, central bank officials reported that nearly one-third of these companies have submitted flawed applications that might affect their continued operation.

Livecoins reported that Ailton Aquino, the Central Bank of Brazil’s inspection director, commented on the issue recently while giving a keynote at a conference. Aquino said that at least 30% of cryptocurrency exchanges did not have the share capital to comply with the regulator’s resolution, affecting the viability of their operations.

Aquino refers to the new capital requirements issued by the bank that establish that each institution would have to hold up to $7.2 million in capital, depending on its classification, according to Resolutions 519 and 520.

Earlier reports indicate that these measures have already triggered the exit of numerous companies from the Brazilian market, including Bitnuvem, NovaDAX, Digitra, and Coinext.

Furthermore, Aquino also stressed that a large number of the firms that filed their applications did not include an audited financial statement, an element requested by regulation.

Aquino’s statements raised alarms in the cryptocurrency ecosystem, as this might bring a reduction in the options Brazilian institutions and customers have to access digital asset financial markets.

João Paulo Oliveira, founder of NoxPay, a crypto-enabled payment service provider, estimated that a good number of these institutions might be rejected by the central bank even after submitting their applications.

“Judging by the tone of his talk, I think half of the 120 VASPs on the list are going to get rejected in this first round,” he declared on social media.

Some have suggested that institutions might have applied knowing they would be rejected to buy time and avoid being blocked by banks, which, since Nov. 6, have been banned from providing services to institutions that did not submit applications. Furthermore, companies that did not apply have until Nov. 30 to wind down their operations.

While companies can file applications to enter the Brazilian market, going forward, the central bank has established a period of up to two years to consider these requests, during which time the exchange will not be able to operate until the application is approved.

title: Ethlabs Calls for Ethereum Quantum Protection in 2027 as Upgrade Priorities Shift
summary: Ethlabs wants Ethereum to prioritise quantum protection in 2027, opening a debate over the scope of its next upgrades.
content:
TL;DR: Ethlabs proposes quantum readiness in 2027 and plans to withdraw its quick-slots work from Hegotá. Developers still need to agree on the network's priorities.

Ethereum's next upgrade debate is becoming a question of how much engineering effort should move toward long-term security. In a November 11 proposal, Ethlabs argues for making quantum protection and resilience against advanced AI-assisted attacks the priority for 2027.

The practical question is which improvements can share an upgrade without slowing the security work. That trade-off deserves attention even from readers who never run a validator: protocol roadmaps influence the software that wallets, exchanges and applications must eventually support.

A timetable that still needs agreement

Ethlabs distinguishes basic readiness from full performance: keeping Ethereum operational with quantum-safe options is the main objective, while matching full network capacity is the more ambitious goal. Its proposed reshuffle includes withdrawing quick slots from Hegotá and reconsidering work outside that security objective.

This is a contribution to Ethereum's development process. A research group's preferred date does not establish an activation date, and an architectural direction still needs specifications, implementations and testing. The useful evidence from here will be what client teams agree to build and what they can demonstrate together.

NewsBTC's earlier coverage of Ethereum's proposed base-layer reconstruction helps explain why changes to speed, security and account design have become closely connected.

Why changing account signatures matters

One relevant building block is EIP-8141, the frame-transaction proposal. It would let a transaction contain separate steps for validation, fee approval and execution. The design gives accounts more flexibility over how they authorise activity, including a path away from today's elliptic-curve signatures.

It also provides for key rotation, batched operations and alternative fee payment. Those features matter because a cryptographic migration is easier to manage when an account's identity can survive a change in its authorisation method.

That creates an important implementation question. An upgrade can enable a safer signature scheme, but wallet developers still have to expose it clearly, exchanges have to recognise it, and users need a recovery path that they understand. Flexibility in the protocol only becomes useful protection when the surrounding software makes it usable.

Several parts of Ethereum need preparation

Ethereum's quantum-security overview identifies multiple areas of exposure: ordinary account signatures, validator signatures, data commitments and some proof systems. Each has a different role, so replacing one component would leave other migration work outstanding.

The same overview says present-day quantum computers cannot break Ethereum's cryptography. Preparation is being undertaken because a transition across a large network takes time, while future hardware capability is uncertain. Hash-based approaches are among the routes being researched, with different efficiency and deployment challenges from current systems.

The distinction between a future cryptographic threat and an active compromise is essential. Readers should not interpret a more ambitious research timetable as evidence that current Ethereum accounts have suddenly been broken. NewsBTC has previously examined Justin Drake's view of quantum migration as a broader redesign opportunity.

The next test is coordinated delivery

Our reading is that the proposal's significance lies in resource allocation. Every additional feature creates implementation and review work, while concentrating on security can defer improvements that other users want sooner. Neither choice is costless.

A credible programme therefore needs measurable milestones: working clients, agreement on migration behaviour and evidence about performance under the new cryptography. It also needs a clear account of which guarantees are available at each stage.

For ETH holders, those milestones will be more informative than a calendar target alone. The debate now asks developers to turn an ambitious security objective into a sequence that the wider Ethereum ecosystem can actually deliver.

written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Trump nominates Hester Peirce successor among SEC, CFTC picks
summary: The White House also named a former CFTC commissioner and two CLARITY Act veterans as nominees to fill vacancies at the SEC and CFTC.
content:
US President Donald Trump has nominated Steven Levine to replace former Securities and Exchange Commission Commissioner Hester Peirce, one of the agency’s most prominent crypto advocates, as part of four nominations to fill vacancies at the SEC and Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

The White House’s latest announcement on Thursday named two nominees each for the SEC and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, agencies whose decisions help shape US cryptocurrency regulation, among other functions. All four nominations require Senate confirmation.

The nominations would replenish several commissioner roles. The SEC currently has only two of its five commissioner seats filled, while CFTC Chairman Michael Selig is the sole member of his agency’s five-seat commission.

The nominations come weeks before Democrats are set to take control of the Senate in January, giving a narrow window for Republicans to confirm Trump’s picks.

Related: House Finance panel chair says regulator actions on crypto ‘fall short’ of CLARITY bill

Levine, a Republican, was nominated for an SEC term ending June 5, 2030, replacing Peirce, who left the agency in October. Peirce was a leading advocate for clearer crypto rules at the SEC, helping shape its approach to digital assets as the former head of its Crypto Task Force, while Levine’s views on crypto regulation are less publicly established.

Trump also nominated Democrat Kristin Johnson, a former CFTC commissioner, for the SEC seat held by Caroline Crenshaw, whose term has also expired. Johnson’s proposed term ends June 5, 2029. Johnson has advocated for stronger customer protections and conflict-of-interest rules for crypto firms in her time at the CFTC.

For the CFTC, Trump nominated Republican Nathan Anonick and Democrat Matthew Rowland, both of whom worked on the Clarity Act. CFTC Chairman Mike Selig called them “two strong bipartisan picks” for CFTC commissioners and said he looked forward to working with them upon their confirmation.

The nominees would typically appear before the Senate Banking Committee for the SEC positions and the Senate Agriculture Committee for the CFTC roles. Following committee consideration, their nominations would go to the full Senate, where confirmation requires a majority vote.

Binance Web3 Wallet Review – What Is It?

Binance Web3 Wallet is a self-custody cryptocurrency wallet built right into the main Binance app. Hence, you have complete control over your own private keys and money with the Web3 Wallet, in contrast to the standard Binance exchange wallet, where Binance stores your digital assets on your behalf.

The wallet is designed to make it simpler for users to enter the Web3 world, regardless of their level of experience with cryptocurrencies. It uses Multi-Party Computation (MPC), a unique security technology. The MPC technology splits your private key into three separate parts, which are then stored in different places: one part is secured by Binance, another is on your device, and the third is encrypted by your recovery password and saved to your personal cloud storage like Google Drive or iCloud. Hence, to access your wallet, you need at least two of these key parts.

You can do a lot of things with the Binance Web3 Wallet. To start with, transferring money between your Web3 Wallet and your standard Binance exchange account is really simple. Additionally, you can exchange tokens using Binance Bridge and other decentralized exchanges (DEXs) to find the best prices across various blockchain networks, such as Ethereum and BNB Chain.

You can connect to various decentralized applications (dApps) for trading, lending, or exploring NFTs. The wallet also includes built-in safety features such as warnings for incorrect addresses and alerts for potentially malicious smart contracts, which help protect your funds.

Download the Binance app now and unlock the full power of Web3 with built-in wallet features, multi-chain support, and easy access to DeFi and NFT platforms.

What Are the Pros & Cons of Binance Web3 Wallet?

Pros of Binance Web3 Wallet

The pros of the Binance Web3 Wallet are ease of use, enhanced MPC technology, no seed phrase to remember, access to dApps, cross-chain swaps, and good customer support.

  • Easy to Use and Access: The wallet is built right into the main Binance app, which makes it super easy to set up and manage. You don’t need to download a separate app or go through a complicated process, and this integration also means you can quickly move your crypto between your regular Binance exchange account and your Web3 Wallet with just a few taps.
  • Enhanced Security with MPC Technology: Instead of a traditional seed phrase, Binance Web3 Wallet uses Multi-Party Computation (MPC). Here, your private key is split into three parts, stored in different places (on your device, with Binance, and in your cloud storage with a recovery password). So, this makes it harder for someone to steal all your keys at once.
  • No Seed Phrase to Remember: For many, managing a long, complicated seed phrase is always a big worry because if you lose it, you lose your crypto forever. However, the MPC technology removes the need to remember a seed phrase, which simplifies the whole process and reduces the risk of human error.
  • Access to Decentralized Applications (dApps): The wallet gives you a direct way to connect with various dApps, like decentralized exchanges (DEXs), NFT marketplaces, and DeFi protocols.
  • Cross-Chain Swaps and Optimized Transactions: It lets you swap tokens across many different blockchain networks, like Ethereum and BNB Chain, without needing to use complex “bridges” that can sometimes be tricky. The wallet even tries to find the best routes and fees for your transactions.
  • Integrated Customer Support: As we see with many self-custody wallets, you’re mostly on your own if something goes wrong, but here, Binance Web3 Wallet offers 24/7 customer support.

Cons of Binance Web3 Wallet

The cons of the Binance Web3 Wallet include no desktop app or browser extension, user responsibility for security, and dependency on the Binance app.

  • No Desktop or Browser Extension Version: The Binance Web3 Wallet can only be accessed through the mobile app at this time. Hence, as a user, you can’t manage your crypto or interact with dApps from a computer using a browser extension.
  • User Responsibility for Security: Even with MPC, you are still in charge of your device’s and cloud’s key share and recovery password. Since Binance Web3 is a self-custody wallet, it is unable to assist you in recovering your money if you misplace your device and forget your recovery password.
  • Dependency on the Binance App: Because it’s integrated into the Binance app, accessing your Web3 Wallet may be challenging if you are unable to access your Binance account or the app for any reason.

What Are the Differences Between Binance Web3 Wallet and Binance Wallet?

The Binance Web3 Wallet is a self-custody wallet that gives you full control over your private keys and digital assets within the Binance app. The Binance Wallet (or exchange wallet) is where Binance holds your cryptocurrencies for you on their centralized exchange. The main difference is who controls your private keys: with the Web3 Wallet, you do, but with the exchange wallet, Binance does.

CriteriaBinance Web3 WalletBinance Wallet (Exchange Wallet)

Web3/dApp AccessYes, allows direct interaction with decentralized appsNo, primarily for trading on the centralized exchange

Use CasesInteracting with DeFi, NFTs, and other Web3 applicationsTrading, buying/selling crypto, holding for convenience

Is Binance Web3 Wallet Legit or Safe to Use?

Yes, the Binance Web3 Wallet is considered legitimate and safe to use. It is directly integrated into the main Binance app, which is obviously a well-known and regulated cryptocurrency exchange globally. The exchange is trusted by over 275M users globally. 

As discussed above, for safety, the wallet uses Multi-Party Computation technology. Hence, this design reduces common risks like losing your seed phrase or having it stolen, and Binance also includes built-in risk controls, such as alerts for suspicious addresses, and provides 24/7 customer support.

What Are Binance Web3 Wallet’s Supported and Restricted Countries?

Binance Web3 Wallet is generally available in most countries where the main Binance.com exchange operates, which serves over 100 countries globally. This includes large parts of Europe, Asia (like India, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Japan, Philippines, Taiwan, Vietnam), the Middle East (like UAE, Saudi Arabia, Egypt), and parts of the Americas (like Brazil, Argentina, Mexico, Colombia).

Also, there are certain countries and regions where Binance, and consequently the Web3 Wallet, are restricted or not available due to international sanctions, regulatory issues, or other compliance reasons. These include countries like the United States, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, and the Crimea region. Canada has also experienced restrictions on Binance’s services.

Is Binance Web3 Wallet Available in the US?

No, the Binance Web3 Wallet is not available in the United States. Mainly, users in the U.S. are directed to use the Binance U.S. It’s a separate and independently operated platform designed to comply with U.S. regulations. So, the integrated Web3 Wallet feature is not yet available on Binance.US, compared to the global Binance platform.

 What Are The Unique Features of Binance Web3 Wallet?

The unique features of Binance Web3 Wallet are self-custody with MPC, multi-chain support, DeFi access, advanced security measures, a unified wallet interface, and an airdrop zone.

Self-Custody With MPC (Multi-Party Computation)

You control your crypto fully. Binance uses MPC to split your private key into three parts: one held by Binance, one on your device, and one encrypted in your cloud storage. Hence, to access your wallet, two of the three key shares are needed, and that means no single point can lose control. 

Plus, you do not need a seed phrase. This means you must back up the third share in your iCloud or Google Drive before use. So, if one key share is lost, the other two still let you sign transactions. In this case, Binance cannot access your assets without your permission, and this setup improves security and retains self-custody.

Multi-Chain Support

In a single Binance Web3 Wallet, you can manage cryptocurrencies from more than 60 public blockchains. To start with, this includes well-known ones like the Move ecosystem, Ethereum, Bitcoin, BNB Chain, Solana, Polygon, Arbitrum, Tron, and Cosmos. 

All of the chains are visible in one location, and within the wallet, you can bridge assets across chains and exchange tokens. On top of that, token prices and gas fees are optimized by the Binance Bridge and internal DEX routing. Hence, this facilitates seamless and intuitive cross-chain operations.

dApp & DeFi Integration

The Binance Web3 Wallet’s design allows easy integration with decentralized finance (DeFi) and applications (dApps). You can directly explore and engage with a variety of dApps, including DeFi platforms for lending or borrowing cryptocurrency, NFT marketplaces, and decentralized exchanges (DEXs) like PancakeSwap and Uniswap. 

Because of the smooth integration, you can use these services directly from the Binance app without requiring complicated setups or third-party browsers. It greatly simplifies user participation in the broader Web3 ecosystem.

Advanced Security

The wallet uses built‑in risk controls. It warns if you try to send to the wrong addresses or interact with known malicious contracts. Again, the MPC key system avoids a single point of failure, and face ID, fingerprint, or password lock helps protect on-device access. 

Binance cannot access or revoke your key shares without your approval, and all sensitive data stays encrypted. No seed phrase is used, reducing the risk of phishing or misplacing recovery information. These elements combine to offer high security across setup, signing, and use.

Unified Wallet Interface

The wallet is a part of the main Binance app and has a single, user-friendly interface. It also means that all of your digital assets are displayed in one location, including those on various blockchain networks. Without navigating between screens or complex menus, you can view your balances, manage your portfolio, and complete transactions. 

By placing all crucial features in the most visible location, this cohesive approach greatly simplifies and streamlines the user experience, especially for individuals who may be unfamiliar with Web3.

Airdrop Zone & Reward Center

The Binance Web3 Wallet has a modified Reward Center and Airdrop Zone. You can participate in Web3 projects’ exclusive airdrops. Some use lucky draws, while others offer first-come, first-served spots. Also, staking BNB (for 30, 60, 90, or 120 days) and finishing Web3 quests are additional ways to earn Megadrop. 

Your score from staking and quests boosts your rewards. Here, many users earn at least $10 to $30 per campaign. All tasks, reward status, and pending tokens are shown in one Reward Center screen, and Binance also offers early access via Alpha to new token launches before public listing.

What Are the Fees of Binance Web3 Wallet?

The fees of Binance Web3 Wallet include only network fees (gas fees) and swap fees. Other fees like withdrawal, deposit, or staking fees follow Binance’s general fee schedule and are separate from wallet fees.

Network Fees (Gas Fees)

Network fees, often called “gas fees,” are a cost that applies whenever you perform a transaction on a blockchain network. Also, these fees are not charged by Binance, but by the blockchain network itself. So, every time you send cryptocurrency, interact with a decentralized application (dApp), or make a swap within the Web3 Wallet, you’re performing an action on a blockchain, and that requires computational effort from the network’s validators or miners.

The amount of the network fee can change a lot, and it depends on several things: how busy the network is at that moment (high traffic means higher fees), the complexity of your transaction (a simple transfer costs less than interacting with a complicated smart contract), and the specific blockchain you are using. So, Ethereum gas fees can be much higher than those on BNB Chain.

Swap Fees

Swap means exchanging one cryptocurrency for another (e.g., swapping ETH for USDT), and here, you will generally encounter swap fees. As of now, Binance has been offering promotions where trading fees for swaps conducted through its integrated Swap and Bridge features in the Web3 Wallet are waived. But remember, you still pay gas fees as usual.

Note: Using Binance Connect to buy crypto using bank accounts may involve a platform fee of up to 2%.

How to Create and Use a Binance Web3 Wallet?

Getting started with Binance Web3 Wallet is easy: You first install the Binance app, create an account, and verify your identity. Then, set a recovery password and back up your wallet securely. After that, you can send, receive, swap tokens, and access dApps—all in one place. Let’s explore each step.

Step 1: Install the App and Access Web3 Wallet

First, you must install the official Binance crypto exchange mobile app from the App Store or Google Play. Now, you need to sign in or create a Binance account using a valid email or phone number. Here, you can also use our Binance referral code to get a $100 free crypto welcome bonus. And also, you have to complete identity verification (KYC) before you can access the Web3 Wallet feature. 

Once you have completed these steps, you can open the app and go to the Wallets tab. You will see a choice to “Create Wallet” or “Import Wallet.” Here, you should tap “Create Wallet” to begin.

Create your Binance Web3 Wallet today to explore thousands of dApps, earn rewards, and manage your crypto securely without ever needing a seed phrase or browser extension.

Step 2: Set Your Recovery Password

Next, you will be asked to set a strong recovery password, and you have to strictly remember this password because it will encrypt one share of the private key. Also, please note: Binance cannot see or reset this password. Now, after the password is set, the wallet automatically generates three shares of the private key using MPC (Multi‑Party Computation). Hence, one share stays with Binance, one share is stored on your device, and one encrypted share is backed up to your cloud if chosen.

Step 3: Backup Your Wallet

Then, you must back up your wallet. You have to select either Cloud Backup or QR Code Backup, or both. If you choose Cloud Backup, you must link a Google Drive or iCloud account and confirm encryption with the recovery password.

Step 4: Start Using Your Binance Web3 Wallet

After that, you can use the wallet. You see the dashboard showing balances across all chains, NFTs, and transaction history, and you need to have a native token for each chain to pay network gas fees. You can send tokens by tapping Send, choosing the token and network, entering the destination address, entering the amount, and confirming with the recovery password or biometric lock. 

Similar to this, you can receive tokens by tapping Receive and sharing or copying the address or QR code. You can transfer tokens from the Binance exchange wallet to the Web3 Wallet by selecting Transfer, selecting from and to accounts, entering the amount, and confirming. 

Also, you can swap tokens inside the wallet by choosing tokens, approving the transaction, and paying only the gas fee. You can also access dApps by tapping DApps, selecting a dApp, and connecting via the wallet to interact directly without leaving the app. You can read our full Binance review for more info about the exchange.

How to Recover a Binance Web3 Wallet?

Recovering your Binance Web3 Wallet is simple. Start by importing your wallet using your cloud backup or QR code and recovery password. Make sure to use the same device type linked to your backup. If you don’t have a backup, you can try the Quick Reset option with Binance support’s help. Let’s break down each step.

Step 1: Start Wallet Import

First, you must open the Binance app and go to Wallets. Then, tap “Import Wallet.” If you have a cloud backup, you have to sign in to the same Google or iCloud account that was used to back up. You then have to enter the recovery password to decrypt the backup. 

The wallet will then restore automatically, and if you used QR Code Backup, you must select the QR Code method and scan the code, and enter the recovery password. Hence, once validated, the wallet restores, including balances, assets, NFTs, and history.

Step 2: Use the Correct Device Type

Next, you can recover on any supported device. You must choose the same cloud platform or scan the QR code backup and enter the recovery password. If you used iCloud, you must restore on an iOS device. If you used Google Drive, you can restore it on an Android device. You only need the recovery password and the backup. No seed phrase is required. The process will bring back the private key shares, and the wallet will reopen with full access.

Step 3: Reset if No Backup Exists

Then, if you did not back up at all and lost access, you can attempt to use the Quick Reset option. You will see Quick Reset on the recovery screen if the app detects a wallet without backup, and you must contact the Binance support team, prove your identity, and request a reset link. You must wait for support confirmation. Once support authorizes, you get temporary access to recreate the wallet, but previous assets are lost unless backed up.

How to Withdraw From Binance Web3 Wallet?

To withdraw from your Binance Web3 Wallet. First, open the app and prepare by ensuring you have enough tokens to cover network fees. Next, pick the token, destination, and amount you want to withdraw. Finally, confirm the details, authorize the transaction, and wait for the blockchain to process it. Let’s walk through each step.

Step 1: Prepare for Withdrawal

First, you must open the Binance app and switch to the Web3 wallet. You must ensure that you have sufficient native tokens on the blockchain to pay network gas fees for withdrawal. Now, tap Transfer, choose Web3 Wallet as the from account, and choose either Binance spot wallet or external wallet address as the destination, depending on whether you want to move to Binance spot or to another wallet.

Step 2: Select Token and Destination

Next, you have to choose the token and chain you want to withdraw to. Then, specify the desired amount. So, if you move to the Binance spot wallet, you follow internal transfer steps, and the gas fee is only on the network transfer into a Web3 address. If you send it to an external wallet, you must confirm the destination address carefully. You may be required to add the address as a new beneficiary address and confirm it via email or 2FA.

Step 3: Confirm and Execute Transfer

Then, you must confirm the transaction. You will see the estimated network fee and total, and double‑check the network and fee details. You have to enter the recovery password or use biometric authentication to sign in. Then tap Confirm. Here, you can view the pending withdrawal in the transaction history. Now, wait for blockchain confirmations before the tokens arrive at their destination.

How to Delete a Binance Web3 Wallet?

To delete your Binance Web3 Wallet, you need to first understand that it’s a self-custody wallet, meaning your assets are controlled by your private keys, not by Binance. Therefore, deleting the wallet within the Binance app doesn’t actually delete the wallet itself, it removes the connection between the wallet and your Binance account. 

To truly “delete” it, you need to export your private keys (or seed phrase if applicable) and stop using the wallet. If you don’t have the seed phrase or private keys, you won’t be able to restore the wallet. This is similar to most non-custodial wallets like Trust Wallet.

  1. To remove your Binance Web3 Wallet, you need to open the Binance app and go to the Wallets section, then tap the Web3 tab. Inside the wallet, open the settings or options menu and select “Remove Wallet.”
  2. After that, you must confirm your identity by entering your recovery password or using biometric authentication. Once verified, the app will show a warning about deleting the wallet and removing local key shares.
  3. You will then need to decide if you want to keep or revoke your cloud backup. Keeping the backup lets you restore the wallet later. If you revoke it, recovery will not be possible.
  4. Once you confirm your choice, the wallet will be deleted from your device. If you still have a backup, you can import the wallet again anytime.

title: Peter Schiff Questions Strategy’s 12% Yield as Bitcoin Drops 19% This Year
summary: Peter Schiff questioned whether expected bitcoin gains could sustain Strategy’s preferred-stock payments after losses he cited over two consecutive years. His criticism targeted Stretch, the bitcoin treasury giant’s income-paying security traded as STRC, which carries a variable dividend rate. Schif...
content:
Peter Schiff questioned whether expected bitcoin gains could sustain Strategy’s preferred-stock payments after losses he cited over two consecutive years. His criticism targeted Stretch, the bitcoin treasury giant’s income-paying security traded as STRC, which carries a variable dividend rate.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin fell 18.93% year to date, extending the decline Schiff cited.
  • STRC’s 12% dividend rate is variable and calculated on a $100 amount.
  • Strategy disclosed bitcoin sales to help fund dividends and buybacks.

Schiff Challenges the Bitcoin Growth Assumption

Economist Peter Schiff challenged the bitcoin return assumptions behind Strategy Inc.’s (Nasdaq: MSTR) preferred-stock financing model. Writing on Nov. 12 on X, he argued that recent losses undermined expectations of sustained appreciation supporting its payments. MSTR is the company’s common-stock ticker, distinct from its income-paying STRC shares.

Addressing the economics behind STRC, Schiff stated:

“The strategy behind STRC is that because the bitcoin MSTR owns will appreciate by 30% per year, MSTR can afford to pay STRC shareholders a 12% annual yield and still make money. But last year bitcoin lost 6.5%. So far this year it’s losing 17%. There’s no basis to assume 30%.”

Michael Saylor, Strategy’s founder and executive chairman, projected average annual bitcoin appreciation of approximately 30% over 20 years in a June 2025 CNBC interview. More recently, he forecast annual growth of 20% to 30% over the next two decades during an Oct. 13 Bloomberg interview. Both projections described long-term price appreciation.

As of this writing, bitcoin traded near $70,900, down 18.93% year to date, extending the 17% decline Schiff cited. The price had fallen 3.74% over 24 hours, 6.53% over seven days, and 14.52% over a month. It was also 30.10% below its level a year earlier.

Saylor had outlined the company’s bitcoin income framework on Nov. 7. That model combines bitcoin holdings with preferred shares, securities issuance, and corporate cash management.

What STRC’s 12% Rate Represents

Strategy’s variable STRC dividend rate stood at 12% annually, based on a $100 stated amount per share, the reference value for dividend calculations. At that rate, payments total $12 a year; effective yield expresses annual dividend income as a percentage of the purchase price. Management evaluates the rate monthly to encourage trading around $100.

Shareholders approved daily STRC dividend accrual in October, allowing dividends to accumulate each calendar day starting Nov. 1. Accrual includes weekends and holidays, with associated payments processed on business days. More frequent distributions change the timing of payments rather than increase the annualized rate.

Owning STRC gives investors a claim on the issuing company, while direct bitcoin ownership gives the holder the cryptocurrency itself. Bitcoin price appreciation can increase Strategy’s asset value, but unrealized gains do not automatically produce dollars for dividends. Payments require corporate cash, which can come from financing or asset sales.

Bitcoin Sales and Buybacks Shape the Funding Picture

The company’s third-quarter financial results disclosed approximately $431.8 million in bitcoin sales during 2026 to fund part of its preferred dividends and STRC repurchases. It also reported $5.07 billion in dollar assets as of Oct. 25, which it said covered approximately 3.4 years of dividend and interest obligations. Buybacks involve purchasing shares from investors, reducing the number carrying future dividend claims.

Charles Schwab, a brokerage and financial services company, identified earnings volatility and potential liquidity pressure in its assessment of bitcoin treasury risks. Liquidity pressure means difficulty meeting cash obligations when cryptocurrency holdings lose value. Under market-value accounting, changes in those holdings can also produce unrealized gains or losses in reported earnings.

During Nov. 2-8, Strategy’s latest bitcoin purchases and STRC buybacks included $81.9 million for 1,036 BTC and $188.3 million for preferred shares, both financed through common-stock sales. Holdings reached 850,364 BTC, acquired for $64.16 billion. As of Nov. 8, its designated dollar reserve, set aside for preferred dividends and debt interest, totaled $4.77 billion, alongside $146.2 million in separate cash.

title: ASA Presses Court to Halt Stock Perpetuals, Putting Retail Risk at Center of Fight
summary: The American Securities Association is backing a halt to single-stock perpetuals, arguing that retail-investor harm strengthens the case for interim relief.
content:
TL;DR: The American Securities Association is asking a federal court to consider retail-investor harm in the challenge to single-stock perpetuals. Its November 10 submission, publicised on November 12, supports interim relief. The CFTC has defended the products as a regulated domestic alternative to offshore trading.

The legal battle over US single-stock perpetuals is gaining another angle: what happens to ordinary investors while the court decides whether the products were properly authorised? The American Securities Association put that question at the centre of a submission supporting the Capital Markets Alliance’s challenge to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

ASA announced its intervention on November 12. The accompanying court-stamped documents show that its motion and proposed friend-of-the-court brief were filed on November 10, an important distinction between the announcement date and the legal event.

ASA focuses on harm while the case proceeds

In its filed motion and brief, ASA says it represents a perspective different from the exchange and trading firms arguing about competitive injury. It focuses on retail investors and the wider equity market.

The association contends that leverage, forced liquidation and trading during thinner sessions could expose customers to substantial losses and transmit stress into underlying shares. Those are arguments advanced by an interested participant, not findings that the predicted harm has occurred.

ASA is asking for a halt while the dispute proceeds. Its submission itself neither grants that relief nor settles the legal classification of perpetual contracts.

The CFTC makes the case for domestic access

The regulator’s position is set out in Chairman Michael Selig’s November 3 statement. The CFTC says the pathway involves designated contract markets that are also notice-registered with the SEC for security-futures products.

Selig argues that bringing perpetual contracts into regulated US markets gives participants a domestic route to instruments used for risk management and price discovery. He also describes cooperation between the CFTC and SEC as central to the framework.

That position and ASA’s objections address different sides of the same policy trade-off. Supporters emphasise regulated availability; opponents dispute whether the chosen legal category preserves the protections the law requires. Describing the debate simply as regulation versus no regulation misses that disagreement.

NewsBTC previously covered the crypto and trading firms supporting the CFTC. ASA’s intervention adds an opposing retail-investor argument to that wider dispute.

The earlier order explains why harm matters

In the November 3 temporary-restraining-order decision, Judge Valerie Caproni denied emergency relief because the plaintiff had not demonstrated the required imminent, irreparable harm. The judge nevertheless considered the plaintiff likely to succeed on its statutory-authority argument at that stage.

The result was therefore narrower than a final endorsement of the approvals. ASA’s emphasis on retail harm is relevant to the interim-relief question, but the court must determine what weight that submission deserves.

Contract design remains part of the dispute

An example appears in the SEC’s September notice of Nadex contract specifications: the proposed perpetual products have no fixed expiry, are cash-settled and do not convey ownership of the underlying security. That document describes a particular venue’s filing rather than every contract involved in the lawsuit.

NewsBTC’s coverage of Kalshi’s separate security-futures listing standards also shows why individual filings need to be read carefully. Similar product names do not make all terms or regulatory questions identical.

The next decisive development is judicial treatment of the requested relief. Another party’s argument can sharpen the dispute, but only the court’s orders establish what the litigation changes for the affected products. Any restrictions would depend on the terms and effective timing of a court order, which an advocacy announcement cannot establish.

written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Former Nvidia CEO Huang had third alleged affair: Reuters

content:

Reuters reported that Jensen Huang had a relationship with another Nvidia employee, hours after he resigned as CEO.

Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second company employee, Reuters reported, bringing the number of alleged extramarital affairs to three.

title: PNC’s Coinbase Pilot Turns Incoming USDC Into Business Bank Deposits
summary: PNC’s limited pilot lets eligible corporate clients receive Ethereum-based USDC payments that automatically convert into dollars in their bank accounts.
content:
TL;DR: PNC’s limited pilot lets eligible businesses receive Ethereum-based USDC, automatically converted into dollars. Coinbase supplies the payment infrastructure.

PNC’s new stablecoin pilot addresses a practical business question: can a company accept a digital-dollar payment without deciding to hold digital assets? In its November 9 announcement, the bank says eligible Corporate & Institutional Banking clients can receive USDC and have it converted one-for-one into US dollars.

The service initially operates on a limited pilot basis. PNC identifies Ethereum as the supported blockchain for incoming payments. That detail matters because the name of a stablecoin alone is not enough to identify a valid payment route.

The receiving business ends with dollars

The converted funds go into a designated PNC deposit account. That means the service’s commercial purpose is payment acceptance rather than encouraging the recipient to maintain a crypto treasury.

For a supplier that invoices in dollars, such a structure could let a customer use a different payment method without changing the currency in which the supplier manages its business. The operational appeal would be a completed receivable that fits its existing accounting and banking relationship.

NewsBTC has examined a comparable separation between payment method and settlement currency in SAT Japan’s stablecoin arrangement with Triple-A. The parties and implementation differ, but the basic commercial question is familiar: what usable balance does the seller receive?

Coinbase provides the connection

In its own description of the expanded partnership, Coinbase identifies its Payment APIs as the underlying infrastructure. PNC contributes banking and treasury-management services. Coinbase also places the pilot after an earlier collaboration that gave eligible PNC Private Bank clients access to digital-asset trading.

Those are different services. A trading arrangement helps a customer acquire or sell an asset; payment acceptance helps a business complete a commercial transaction. Treating them as interchangeable would obscure the reason a corporate finance team might be interested in the latest pilot.

NewsBTC’s coverage of Circle and ACI’s settlement demonstration examines a related effort to connect USDC with established payment infrastructure. That remains a separate project, with its own implementation and availability.

Citi has announced a similar payment model

Coinbase’s banking integrations extend beyond PNC. A September 28 Citi announcement described plans for institutional stablecoin acceptance through Spring by Citi, including automatic conversion into fiat and settlement by Citi.

The Citi collaboration also outlined the reverse flow: using Citi’s Virtual Account Wallet infrastructure for Coinbase Virtual Accounts, so incoming fiat could be converted into stablecoins. These opposite directions show why the complete payment journey matters more than a broad claim that a bank has adopted crypto.

That earlier announcement is context for the business model. It does not establish PNC’s pricing, eligibility or processing times, which must be assessed on their own terms.

What the pilot still needs to demonstrate

The useful performance measures are the time until dollars are available, the full cost to sender and recipient, and the quality of payment information that reaches the business. Exception handling matters too: a transfer that fails a check or arrives with incomplete details still needs a clear resolution process.

The public PNC and Coinbase announcements do not provide a comprehensive fee schedule or an end-to-end service guarantee. The one-for-one conversion description should therefore not be expanded into a claim that every part of the payment is free.

The pilot gives eligible businesses a defined way to test stablecoin acceptance within a familiar banking relationship. Its wider significance will depend on whether customers choose it repeatedly because it makes getting paid easier.

written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Visa Adds Western Union’s USDPT for Stablecoin Settlement via Anchorage
summary: Anchorage Digital is partnering with Visa to allow select stablecoins issued by its federally regulated bank, starting with Western Union’s USDPT, to be used as native settlement assets on Visanet. Rapid Growth in Stablecoin Settlement Anchorage Digital announced Thursday, Nov. 12, that it is collab...
content:
Anchorage Digital is partnering with Visa to allow select stablecoins issued by its federally regulated bank, starting with Western Union’s USDPT, to be used as native settlement assets on Visanet.

Key Takeaways

  • Anchorage Digital partnered with Visa to support Western Union’s USDPT as a native settlement asset on VisaNet.
  • Visa’s stablecoin settlement run rate jumped 10x to $25 billion annually alongside 225+ card programs.
  • Visa and Anchorage plan to evaluate and add more 1:1 dollar-backed stablecoins to the network next.

Rapid Growth in Stablecoin Settlement

Anchorage Digital announced Thursday, Nov. 12, that it is collaborating with Visa to support select stablecoins issued by its federally regulated bank as native settlement assets on the Visa network, beginning with Western Union’s USDPT token.

Under the agreement, Visa and eligible partners can use USDPT to settle their obligations on Visanet. USDPT is the first stablecoin issued by Anchorage Digital Bank to receive support on the network, although the partnership establishes a framework for evaluating and adding other Anchorage-issued stablecoins in the future.

The announcement comes amid rapid expansion of Visa’s stablecoin settlement infrastructure. As of September, Visa reported an annualized stablecoin settlement run rate of $25 billion and more than 225 active stablecoin-linked card programs globally. Traditional card settlement typically operates on a five-business-day schedule through conventional banking systems, while blockchain-based settlement allows funds to move continuously, including on weekends and holidays.

Earlier this week, the Monad Foundation announced that Visa had added support for Monad, an Ethereum-compatible Layer 1 blockchain, as a stablecoin settlement network. The integration gives participating Visa issuers and acquirers another blockchain option offering subsecond finality and planned privacy features designed to keep commercially sensitive transaction details confidential, while allowing access for auditors and regulators.

Bridging Regulation and Blockchain Speed

Anchorage Digital said its collaboration with Visa advances its goal of becoming an institutional-scale settlement bank for stablecoins. Beyond issuing tokens, the company provides digital asset custody and settlement infrastructure.

“Stablecoins have made money move faster, but speed alone won’t bring institutions onchain,” Nathan McCauley, co-founder and CEO of Anchorage Digital, said in a statement. “They need a regulated institution behind the money. With Anchorage Digital select issued stablecoins now being supported on the Visa network, institutions get both: the speed of a stablecoin and the safety of a federally regulated bank behind it.”

For its part, Visa said the integration expands settlement options for its network participants.

“As stablecoin payments grow, we’re focused on providing more choice for our partners in how they settle with Visa,” said Dan Roesbery, vice president of global crypto partnerships and go-to-market at Visa. “Supporting USDPT as a native settlement asset, in partnership with Anchorage, gives them another trusted, institution-grade option backed by a federally chartered bank.”

In addition to Western Union’s USDPT, Anchorage Digital Bank’s federally regulated platform issues several other dollar-pegged stablecoins, including Tether’s USAT, OSL Group’s USDGO, Ethena Labs’ USDtb, Falcon Finance’s fUSD, and Zelle’s ZLUSD. The company said each token is backed 1-to-1 by U.S. dollars and cash equivalents and issued under federal oversight.

Anchorage Digital also operates Atlas, an institutional counterparty settlement network designed to mitigate risk and facilitate off-exchange settlement, collateral management, and cross-border transfers. The company said combining regulated stablecoin issuance with settlement infrastructure is intended to support institutional adoption of ’round-the-clock digital payments.

title: Gemini’s quarterly retail trading volume sinks to 3-year low
summary: Gemini’s third-quarter trading rebound masked a deepening retail slump.
content:
Crypto exchange Gemini has just reported its lowest quarterly retail trading volume in three years, despite an increase in overall crypto trading volume.

Total spot trading volume rose 18% from the second quarter to $4.5 billion, according to Gemini’s Q3 earnings report. Institutional volume climbed 26% to $3.9 billion, while retail volume fell 14% to $600 million, its lowest level since the third quarter of 2023. 

Gemini said the quarterly increase in spot trading volume was “supported by increased institutional Zcash activity and expanded affiliated market-making,” but did not give a specific reason for the decline in retail trading. 

Despite the retail slump, Gemini’s exchange revenue increased 7% from the previous quarter to $13.4 million as institutional revenue more than doubled. Retail traders remained its largest source of exchange revenue, contributing nearly three-quarters of the total.

Crypto exchanges turn to prediction markets for growth 

A number of crypto exchanges also reported softer crypto trading activity in the most recent quarter. 

Coinbase reported softer retail and institutional activity, with consumer spot trading volume falling 9% from the previous quarter to $23.4 billion. Coinbase chief financial officer Alesia Haas said “continued growth in prediction markets helped offset softer crypto trading activity.”

At Robinhood, crypto revenue fell 55% year-on-year to $120 million, offset by a sixfold increase in event-contract revenue to $173 million. 

Related: Strategy stock sheds 5% amid MSCI index removal, Bitcoin sell-off

Gemini also got some help from its own prediction exchange, Gemini Predictions, with revenue from that business unit increasing 52% quarter-on-quarter to $796,000, though it wasn’t significant enough to offset declines elsewhere. 

Gemini looks to expand prediction markets

Gemini reported stronger prediction-market activity heading into the fourth quarter, with average daily traders in October running about 50% above the third-quarter average. 

Nearly a third of new prediction traders were new to Gemini, more than double the proportion in Q3.

The company is also seeking to distribute its event contracts through other platforms. An August nonbinding agreement with Apex Fintech Solutions would make Gemini Titan the exclusive venue for crypto event contracts distributed through Apex’s futures brokerage to its brokerage customers, subject to definitive agreements.

Gemini is set to host a Q3 earnings call on Friday.

title: DOJ Wins Court Authority to Seize $1.2 Billion of North Korea’s Stolen Binance Crypto as Freezes Top $2.7 Billion
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

DOJ Wins Court Authority to Seize $1.2 Billion of North Korea’s Stolen Binance Crypto as Freezes Top $2.7 Billion
The DOJ won court authority to seize $1.2 billion of North Korea's stolen Binance crypto and took down a $400 million deepfake theft scheme.
This post DOJ Wins Court Au...
content:
The DOJ said Thursday it has court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance, part of a freeze of more than $2.7 billion that officials said halted about half of North Korea’s October exchange heist.

In a Thursday announcement, the department said that on or about Oct. 29, members of the North Korean military, referred to by the FBI as TraderTraitor, stole more than $6 billion worth of virtual assets from Binance. That is below the $6.34 billion figure Binance has covered since the attack.

Binance said it had completed coverage of the assets hit in the breach, replacing the tokens from company funds rather than by recovering the stolen coins. Those are separate tracks: the DOJ is trying to interdict what was taken, while the exchange has said users were made whole from its Secure Asset Fund for Users, a portion of its futures insurance fund and its treasury.

Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the DOJ’s Criminal Division said the department and its partners were able to “immediately halt about half of this historic breach” by freezing stolen assets “before they got beyond law enforcement reach.” The freeze of more than $2.7 billion is a joint figure for U.S. government and private-sector efforts. Of that amount, the DOJ said it has already obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion. The underlying court papers were not posted with the announcement.

The $1.2 billion is not newly recovered money but comes out of the roughly $2.85 billion Binance said on Nov. 3 had been frozen or intercepted, and Thursday’s court authorization is the legal step that lets the government move toward taking ownership of those funds through forfeiture, where until now they had simply been frozen at the token issuers.

Even that freeze is not the end of the trail. The DOJ said TraderTraitor actors are still moving the stolen assets through cryptocurrency bridges, mixers and exchanges, and that tracing, seizure and forfeiture work continues. Last week, on Oct. 31, the FBI, with the U.S. Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation, issued a Cyber Alert attributing the theft to North Korea and urging virtual asset service providers to block transactions with or derived from addresses the actors are using. The alert said investigators have seen the stolen assets converted primarily into ether.

A separate $400 million deepfake scheme, and 900 seized videos

Separately from the DOJ and Binance case, the U.S. attorney’s office in the Central District of California and the FBI announced the seizure of cloud-based infrastructure used in a social engineering campaign the FBI is calling FaceStealer. The FBI said the scheme has resulted in the theft of more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over the last 18 months and has also been used in attempts to compromise people who maintain open-source software, a step the bureau said appears calculated to enable supply-chain attacks.

The method is a fake video call. The FBI said North Korean hackers, known publicly under names including APT38 and BlueNoroff, lure targets with meeting invitations sent from accounts stolen from earlier victims. Once a target joins, the hackers play a prerecorded webcam video of a person the target knows, or a deepfake of a well-known figure in the cryptocurrency industry, then introduce a fake technical error and send a “fix” that installs malware. In several cases, the theft came months to more than a year after the first compromise, as the hackers waited for wallet balances to grow.

A Thursday FBI FLASH report said the meetings run on imposter versions of Zoom, Microsoft Teams and Google Meet, with invitations often moving through hijacked Telegram, LinkedIn, Slack or Discord accounts. Pursuant to a federal warrant, the FBI seized more than 900 webcam videos of FaceStealer victims. The bureau has posted a hub for the campaign at fbi.gov/facestealer.

Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General for National Security M. Scott Proctor tied both Thursday’s actions to the same charge: “North Korea’s government bankrolls its rogue regime and illicit weapons program through cryptocurrency theft.”

The Binance recovery is still being run by the FBI’s Los Angeles Field Office, Cyber Division and Virtual Asset Unit, with the Secret Service and IRS-CI. The DOJ did not say how much of the more than $2.7 billion freeze, or of the $1.2 billion under court authority, is bitcoin.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Circle and Global Citizen Plan USDC Vendor Payments for Move Afrika in 2027
summary: Circle and Global Citizen plan to introduce USDC payments for participating Move Afrika vendors in Rwanda in 2027, alongside practical financial education.
content:
TL;DR: Circle and Global Citizen plan USDC vendor payments and training for Move Afrika, starting in Rwanda in 2027.

The businesses behind live concerts are the focus of Circle’s latest stablecoin partnership. A November 10 announcement with Global Citizen outlines plans to offer USDC payments to vendors working on Move Afrika, the touring initiative created by Global Citizen and pgLang.

The programme offers a practical way to judge whether digital-dollar payments improve a business process beyond the initial announcement.

Rwanda is the starting point

The partners say the payments initiative will begin in Rwanda in 2027. Circle also plans to support financial education, technical training and guidance through the Move Afrika Production Alliance.

The combination matters because receiving a token is not the same as being comfortable managing it. For a vendor, the relevant questions may be basic: how to recognise a legitimate payment, keep access to the funds and use the money for the next business expense.

Training would be especially useful if it covers those everyday decisions in the same setting as the payment itself. The partners’ ambitions will ultimately be easier to assess through the experiences of participating businesses than through a broad estimate of the market available to stablecoins.

The concert provides a concrete payment use case

Imagine a local production supplier that needs to pay staff and replace equipment after an event. A faster incoming transfer could be valuable, but only if the supplier can turn that balance into the payments its business needs to make.

A digital-dollar balance may be convenient for one expense and require conversion for another. Availability, fees and the reliability of the withdrawal route can therefore matter as much as the speed of the original transfer. Those are implementation questions for this programme, rather than assumptions that a dollar token resolves automatically.

The same distinction appears in NewsBTC’s coverage of SAT Japan’s stablecoin payment option: customer payment choice and the currency a business ultimately uses can be separate parts of a service.

Circle has explored other African payment routes

The partnership follows Circle’s March collaboration with Sasai Fintech, a Cassava Technologies business. That earlier announcement focused on exploring USDC applications across enterprise payments, cross-border transfers and wallet services.

The two efforts have different routes to users. Sasai brings an existing financial-services platform, while Move Afrika supplies an event-based network of working businesses. Neither announcement establishes the results of the other, and the earlier collaboration should not be presented as evidence that the new vendor programme is already operating.

For Circle, the potential benefit of an event programme is the ability to connect a payment with a recognisable commercial obligation. For participating suppliers, the meaningful outcome would be a useful balance received and recorded with less friction.

Success can be measured in vendor outcomes

The clearest future evidence would include how many vendors choose USDC, whether they use it again and the total cost of receiving and spending or converting it. Feedback about training and payment exceptions would help show where the experience needs improvement.

NewsBTC’s analysis of Bitso Business payment volumes shows why operating evidence matters. For Move Afrika, the useful evidence will come from participating vendors after the planned rollout begins.

Move Afrika gives Circle and Global Citizen an identifiable starting group and a future rollout date. The interesting story now is how that plan becomes a reliable payment experience for the people doing the work behind the stage.

written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $71,200 After a Fresh Session Low as the 10-Year Yield Holds Above 5%
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Trades Near $71,200 After a Fresh Session Low as the 10-Year Yield Holds Above 5%
Bitcoin price traded near $71,200 Thursday evening after slipping to a fresh session low near $71,000, its weakest level since Aug. 20.
This post Bitcoin Price Trades Near $71,200 After ...
content:
Bitcoin price traded near $71,200 on Thursday evening, after slipping to a fresh session low near $71,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. U.S. stocks closed modestly lower and the 10-year Treasury yield held above 5% after Nvidia said CEO Jensen Huang had resigned.

The decline started in the morning. Bitcoin price fell below $72,000 before the opening bell and dropped to about $71,150 shortly after 10 a.m. Eastern. A bounce later faded, and the bitcoin price printed a new session low near $71,000 around 6:23 p.m., its weakest level since Aug. 20. It now stands roughly $30,400 below where it closed one year ago.

Stocks close lower as yields keep pressure on the bitcoin price

The Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.39% to 25,366.09, the S&P 500 lost 0.35% to 7,592.40 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.36% to 52,297.09, Reuters reported. Nvidia shares finished 4.3% lower at $166.19, off the day’s lows, after the company said Huang had resigned as president, chief executive and a board member, effective immediately, and named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO.

Bitcoin-linked stocks had a harder session. Strategy (MSTR), which MSCI is removing from its USA Index at the Nov. 30 close, finished at $114.41, down 6.5%. Shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), which had bled $2 billion over nine straight days of outflows through Wednesday, closed at $40.36, down 4.5%.

The bond market did much of the afternoon work. The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 12 basis points to 5.105% and reached 5.12%, its highest since Oct. 21, after President Donald Trump said the United States does not need a deal with Iran, Reuters reported. The two-year yield, which tracks Federal Reserve expectations most closely, climbed about 14 basis points to 4.867%. Brent crude settled at $95.82 a barrel, up 3.3%, after attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure escalated.

Fed hike bets, a $404 billion deficit and a busy evening of crypto news

Higher yields reflect a market that still expects the Fed to tighten again next month. Fed funds futures are pricing in 29 basis points of hikes in December, a quarter-point move as the base case with only slim odds of a half-point step, Reuters reported. Rising rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and that has weighed on the bitcoin price all week.

The Treasury added a fiscal reminder after the close. The government ran a $404 billion deficit in October, the first month of fiscal 2027, the Treasury Department said, up 42% from $284 billion a year earlier, as receipts fell to $369 billion and outlays rose to $773 billion. Some benefit payments that would normally have been made on Nov. 1, a Sunday, were shifted into October.

The evening also brought a cluster of crypto headlines. The Justice Department said it has court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of cryptocurrency stolen from Binance in October’s North Korea-linked heist, part of a freeze that officials said halted about half the breach. Binance, in a separate announcement, said it has fully covered the $6.34 billion in user losses with company funds. Jane Street’s quarterly 13F showed it had raised its Strategy stake 54% as of Sept. 30, though large options positions point to hedging rather than a straight bet. After the close, Gemini reported third-quarter revenue of $40.9 million, down 19%, as platform trading volume fell 73%; its net loss narrowed 63% to $58.6 million.

Those announcements did not lift the bitcoin price off the session lows. Friday’s Producer Price Index is the next inflation test, and Nvidia is still scheduled to report quarterly results on Nov. 17 under its interim leadership.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $71,200.

Micah Zimmerman

title: Trezor Confirms Spy Implants in 3 Hardware Wallets, Cuts Resellers by 80%
summary: Trezor reported the discovery of three tampered Safe 5 wallets, an approximately 80% reduction in resellers, and a firmware update blocking the identified implants. CryptoBilis buyers should still move funds to new wallets, and purchases from March onward qualify for replacements. Trezor Details Fir...
content:
Trezor reported the discovery of three tampered Safe 5 wallets, an approximately 80% reduction in resellers, and a firmware update blocking the identified implants. CryptoBilis buyers should still move funds to new wallets, and purchases from March onward qualify for replacements.

Key Takeaways

  • Trezor said it received no reports of customer funds lost to the implants.
  • Firmware 2.13.1 cannot secure recovery phrases captured before installation.
  • Replacement eligibility covers CryptoBilis purchases from March onward.

Trezor Details Firmware and Reseller Changes

Hardware wallet maker Trezor said on Nov. 12 that three Safe 5 devices bought from CryptoBilis, a former authorized reseller in Southeast Asia, contained unauthorized hardware implants. Its blog post on the investigation detailed a firmware update and stricter distribution controls. Version 2.13.1, released Nov. 11, prevents the identified implants from capturing information by updating the software that runs the device, the company said.

All three affected devices were bought between Aug. 20 and Sept. 23 through CryptoBilis directly or via its Tokopedia and Shopee stores. Trezor examined the first reported Safe 5 implant in its laboratory and identified two others from owners’ photographs. Forty-eight customers had contacted the company, which was checking their devices in its lab or through internal photographs.

The company stated:

“We have cut our reseller network by about 80%.”

Its reseller reduction plans emerged in October, and Trezor now describes the removed partners as trustworthy and posing no immediate threat. Remaining sellers must meet stricter requirements governing sourcing, storage, and access to devices.

Hidden Boards Captured Wallet Secrets

Inside the Safe 5, the unauthorized implant sits between the screen and main board, the device’s primary circuit board connecting electronic components. It copies displayed information without changing the firmware or Secure Element, a dedicated security chip, according to Trezor’s analysis. The added board records recovery words during wallet creation or restoration, plus displayed passphrases, which are optional extra secrets used to access separate wallets.

The implant encrypts what it captures and sends it over a mobile network to a server run by the attackers. Without a signal, it holds the data and keeps retrying until the transfer goes through. Trezor said the implant works the same way as those found in some Ledger devices. In Ledger’s case, attackers bought genuine devices, modified them, and put them back on sale through resellers in Southeast Asia.

Ledger had confirmed an unauthorized hardware implant in an affected customer’s wallet in October. Trezor’s findings remained limited to Safe 5 devices bought from CryptoBilis. Checks of other regional resellers’ devices found no tampering, and the company reported no confirmed implants in other models.

CryptoBilis Buyers Still Need New Wallets

Although the update blocks capture by the identified implants, previously exposed wallet backups remain compromised. Trezor continued advising CryptoBilis buyers to transfer funds to newly created wallets, since replacing hardware while reusing the same recovery phrase leaves that exposure intact. Owners of suspected tampered devices were instructed to retain them and avoid setup or use pending support guidance.

Replacement eligibility covers every model purchased from CryptoBilis from March onward. Shipping restrictions may require a different model with a refund of the price difference, delivery to another country, or a refund. Customers were asked to arrange replacements through official Trezor Support, with uncertain buyers also encouraged to verify their device’s origin.

Scammers could impersonate staff offering replacements or refunds, Trezor warned, reiterating that it never requests recovery phrases. The company continued working with SEAL 911, the Security Alliance’s emergency response service for cryptocurrency incidents. It also pledged a reward for the customer who first reported the implant.

title: Jane Street Lifts Its Strategy (MSTR) Stake 54% to 4.1 Million Shares
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Jane Street Lifts Its Strategy (MSTR) Stake 54% to 4.1 Million Shares
A 13F filed Thursday shows Jane Street held 4,119,097 Strategy shares as of Sept. 30, up 53.8%.
This post Jane Street Lifts Its Strategy (MSTR) Stake 54% to 4.1 Million Shares first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine a...
content:
Jane Street Group raised its Strategy (MSTR) stake 53.8% in the third quarter, to 4,119,097 shares, a Form 13F filed Thursday shows, a position dated to Sept. 30 that does not capture any trades the firm may have made since then.

Those caveats matter as much as the increase. Jane Street is a trading firm, and one of the largest market makers in stocks, ETFs, and options, and the same filing lists call options covering 13,573,000 Strategy shares and put options covering 13,991,800 shares, each more than three times the size of the common stake. Some of that stock is likely a hedge for the options and market-making book rather than a straight bet on the company. The 13F does not say how much.

The shares were valued at $630.6 million in the filing, using the Sept. 30 price of $153.09. Strategy has fallen about 25% since then. At Thursday’s close of $114.41, the same 4,119,097 shares were worth about $471 million.

The Class A position is up 1,441,475 shares from the 2,677,622 Jane Street reported at June 30, when the same holding was valued at $232.8 million. The firm filed about four days ahead of the Nov. 16 deadline; the SEC accepted the report at 4:04 p.m. Eastern on Thursday.

Call and put positions that dwarf Strategy’s stock

The options lines were already large in the second quarter and grew again. Calls covering 13,573,000 shares were valued at $2.08 billion in the new filing, and puts covering 13,991,800 shares, listed in two rows, were valued at $2.14 billion. Those figures use the same Sept. 30 share price as the common-stock line; a 13F reports the underlying shares the options cover, not the cash premium paid for the contracts.

The report is a holdings filing that folds in positions across seven other included managers, among them Jane Street Capital, Jane Street Options and Jane Street Global Trading, so the Strategy lines can include inventory across the group rather than a single proprietary bet. Authorized Signatory Jeremy Kahn signed the report in New York on Nov. 12. The table lists 14,764 entries valued at $1.19 trillion.

Other early 13Fs so far, with bigger names still to file

Jane Street’s 53.8% increase was the sharpest percentage increase among the large Strategy stakes in Thursday’s early 13F wave. Capital International Investors, a Capital Group unit, raised its stake 4.5% to 36,467,109 shares, worth about $4.17 billion at Thursday’s close. Invesco added 10.9%, to 10,362,698 shares, worth about $1.19 billion. Renaissance Technologies cut its position 41%, to 1,515,560 shares, worth about $173 million, and left the spot bitcoin ETF holdings it had reported at midyear, including BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust.

JPMorgan Chase, in a filing already reported, lifted its Strategy stake 36% to 848,932 shares and held 11.4 million IBIT shares, worth about $460 million at Thursday’s close. Bank of New York Mellon, in another early 13F, raised its stake in Strive (ASST). Those share counts, like Jane Street’s, are as of Sept. 30.

Still to file by the Nov. 16 deadline are the main quarterly 13Fs from Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Millennium and Mubadala. Institutional managers that exercise investment discretion over $100 million or more in 13F securities have 45 days after quarter-end to disclose those holdings. That window ran to Nov. 14, a Saturday, so the deadline is Monday.

The Sept. 30 snapshot also precedes this week’s decision by MSCI to remove Strategy from its USA index, a step that will force index funds to sell by Nov. 30, and it precedes the stock’s slide since quarter-end. Monday’s remaining filings will show where other large holders stood on the same date, not where they stand now.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Maple Finance’s strategy rift sends co-founder, COO to the exits
summary: Maple Finance co-founder Joe Flanagan and COO Ryan O’Shea are leaving over disagreements about the firm’s direction as SYRUP falls despite revenue growth.
content:
Two senior executives are leaving onchain asset manager Maple Finance over disagreements about the firm’s direction as its SYRUP token slid more than 7% Thursday.

Maple co-founder and executive chairman Joe Flanagan said Wednesday he would leave after seven years at the firm, describing a growing divide with fellow co-founder and CEO Sidney Powell.

“Over time, our views on strategy, leadership, and life have moved further apart,” Flanagan wrote. “I believe Maple is best served by one co-founder leading it forward from here.”

Chief operating officer Ryan O’Shea also said in a Thursday post on X that he would leave after nearly five years at Maple. “I’ll be stepping down as COO. I’ve come to a different view on the direction Maple should take, and I’ve decided it’s time to step aside,” he wrote.

SYRUP traded at $0.12 at 10:36 p.m. UTC Thursday, down 7.5% over 24 hours and 12% over the past week, according to CoinGecko. The token had a market capitalization of about $145 million.

Maple and Powell did not respond to Cointelegraph’s requests for comment by publication.

Maple says leadership shakeup will not disrupt anything

In a statement published Wednesday, Maple confirmed that Flanagan was stepping down as chairman and leaving the company. “This is an agreed and orderly transition,” the company said, adding that his responsibilities would move to Powell and Maple’s existing leadership team.

The company did not announce a replacement chairman or specify how the departing executives’ duties would be carried out.

Flanagan said his differences with Powell reached a point where they were no longer constructive. “I am choosing to leave rather than continue supporting a direction I cannot stand behind,” he said. Flanagan added that he would help with the transition through the end of 2026.

O’Shea is stepping down effective Nov. 27. “I’ll have no ongoing role after that,” he wrote.

The departures come as Maple looks to expand beyond crypto-backed lending. In October, Powell said the firm planned to reach more customers through fintech partnerships and lend against a wider range of assets, including payments owed on loans made by fintech companies and securities backed by assets such as mortgages.

Related: Kraken, Maple launch onchain warehouse facility for crypto-backed institutional loans

Revenue growth continues

The announcements come as Maple’s lending business continues to grow, while SYRUP is down 62% year to date and total value locked (TVL) has declined.

According to Token Terminal, Maple’s protocol revenue rose 8% year over year in October, while TVL fell around 11% between the end of September and Nov. 11.

Maple’s latest quarterly results also showed growth, with the company reporting $4.4 million in third-quarter revenue, up 5% from a year earlier. Assets under management rose 18% year over year to $4.7 billion.

Maple has also been using some of its revenue to buy back SYRUP tokens. In September, the company repurchased about 1.37 million tokens, twice as many as in August, according to its October update.
