title: Bottomline Completes First USDC Transfers Inside Its Enterprise Payments Platform
summary: Bottomline says it completed its first live cross-border USDC payments through its Global Payments Hub and Cash Management platform as an intra-company transfer.
content:
TL;DR: Bottomline has completed live USDC transfers inside its enterprise payments platform. The initial transfer was between company entities.

Bottomline disclosed the cross-border transactions in a November 10 announcement, using its Global Payments Hub and Cash Management platform.

The practical point is where the payment fits. A finance team may be more interested in approving, tracking and reconciling a transfer within its existing systems than in opening a separate crypto application to make it happen.

The first transfer was within the company

Bottomline describes the milestone as an intra-company transfer. That establishes that the company used the integration for a live movement of funds; it does not establish that unrelated businesses are already using it at scale.

The release says the aim is to let treasury teams handle stablecoin payments alongside traditional methods, retaining familiar approvals, controls and audit processes. It presents near-real-time settlement for selected scenarios, especially cross-border payments, as part of the attraction.

The company has not supplied a transaction-by-transaction performance dataset in this announcement. Readers therefore cannot use it to calculate an average fee saving or a reliable improvement in end-to-end delivery time.

Treasury software does more than send money

Bottomline’s cash-management product description emphasises connecting treasury, accounting, compliance, banking and enterprise resource planning data. It describes tools for cash visibility, reconciliation and reporting, helping place the USDC announcement within the wider product.

Consider a group with businesses in two countries. Moving value between them is only one part of the job. Staff may also need to identify the correct entities, record the purpose of the transfer, obtain approval and match the completed payment to the accounts.

If a stablecoin route requires those steps to be reconstructed manually outside the normal workflow, a fast blockchain transfer can still leave an expensive administrative task. Integration is useful when it keeps the financial record attached to the movement of money.

NewsBTC explored a related implementation issue in Circle and ACI’s Latin American settlement collaboration, which examined how a digital-dollar option fits within existing payment operations.

A digital dollar is one part of the route

Circle describes USDC as a dollar-redeemable token backed by liquid reserves. That explains the asset being transferred, but a corporate payment can involve more than the onchain movement itself.

A business funding a transfer from a bank account needs an entry route. A recipient that pays suppliers in local currency may need conversion and a bank payout. Each stage can affect the amount received and the time before it can be spent.

For that reason, the useful comparison is between two complete payment routes serving the same need. A low network charge does not settle the comparison if conversion costs are higher, or if an exception requires substantial staff time to resolve.

The next test is repeat business

The next useful disclosures would identify supported use cases, the businesses choosing them and performance over repeated transfers. Clear handling of failures, rejected payments and reconciliation exceptions would be particularly informative.

There is also a difference between a first transaction and a mature operating metric, as NewsBTC’s analysis of Bitso Business payment volumes explains. Neither measure should be mistaken for fee revenue or universal customer availability.

Bottomline has demonstrated a concrete integration step. Its commercial value will come from making a recurring treasury task easier to complete and account for, with enough transparency for finance teams to compare the new route with the options they already trust.

written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: ‘Anthropic IPO Is Going to Rip’: Arthur Hayes Loads Up on Crypto Ahead of Debut
summary: Arthur Hayes said he was increasing crypto exposure ahead of Anthropic’s expected stock market debut next week. His near-term optimism followed earlier warnings about AI spending and a potential government rescue that he believed could benefit crypto. Hayes Builds Crypto Positions Ahead of Anthropic...
content:
Arthur Hayes said he was increasing crypto exposure ahead of Anthropic’s expected stock market debut next week. His near-term optimism followed earlier warnings about AI spending and a potential government rescue that he believed could benefit crypto.

Key Takeaways

  • Hayes said he kept positions small to medium so he could exit quickly.
  • Anthropic’s 825 million-share IPO could raise up to $64.35 billion.
  • Seven technology partners committed to a conditional $26 billion investment.

Hayes Builds Crypto Positions Ahead of Anthropic Debut

Arthur Hayes, co-founder of cryptocurrency derivatives exchange Bitmex and chief investment officer at crypto investment firm Maelstrom, said on X on Nov. 11 that he was adding crypto risk before Anthropic’s anticipated listing the following week.

Discussing his crypto positioning ahead of the IPO, the oft-outspoken Hayes stated:

“The Anthropic IPO is going to rip. I’m loading up on crypto risk between now and next week’s listing date.”

“Keeping size small-to-medium in case I need to quickly close the positions. But I’m mini-bulled up,” he added.

Proposed Offering Includes $26 Billion Partner Investment

Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company behind Claude, an AI assistant, launched its initial public offering (IPO) roadshow Nov. 10. Its proposed share offering comprised 825 million Class A shares at an expected price of $70 to $78 each. The company had applied to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT.

At that range, proposed IPO proceeds would total $57.75 billion to $64.35 billion before underwriting discounts, the fees paid to banks arranging the sale, and other expenses. Anthropic would offer approximately 801.35 million shares, with existing stockholders selling the remainder. The company would receive no proceeds from those stockholders’ sales.

A separate conditional $26 billion private placement involved Google, Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Micron Technology, Microsoft, and TSMC Partners. Those investors agreed to purchase nonvoting Class N shares at the IPO price, with the transaction scheduled to close immediately after the public offering, subject to conditions. In its Nov. 10 announcement, Anthropic said its registration statement had not yet become effective.

AI Spending Risks Accompany Short-Term Optimism

On Nov. 2, Hayes had offered a more cautious bitcoin outlook tied to bank and Fed balance sheets, expecting weakness until the Federal Reserve or commercial banks began expanding their balance sheets. That assessment focused on monetary conditions as a potential driver of demand. His latest trade instead centered on the approaching AI listing.

Monetary expansion remained central to his broader thesis, with global liquidity and money supply providing the backdrop to his longer-term outlook. Commercial bank lending and central bank asset purchases represent different routes through which funding conditions can change. The earlier assessment put both banks and the Fed within his framework for a bitcoin recovery.

In an interview published Oct. 2, he outlined an AI bailout forecast involving trillions of dollars, arguing that financial stress among AI companies and data-center borrowers could prompt government intervention. He expected money creation associated with that rescue to benefit crypto and placed a potential reckoning roughly 12 to 18 months away. That forecast addressed a longer horizon than the listing trade.

Financial disclosures supplied a concrete measure of Anthropic’s growth and spending exposure. Revenue reached $33.2 billion in the first nine months of the year, while its operating loss narrowed to $1.3 billion from $5.2 billion a year earlier. Purchase and lease commitments totaled approximately $900.9 billion, largely for computing and infrastructure, including $70.7 billion due within 12 months after Sept. 30.

title: DOJ’s Operation TorNado Arrests 354 and Seizes $234 Million in Cash and Crypto
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

DOJ’s Operation TorNado Arrests 354 and Seizes $234 Million in Cash and Crypto
The Justice Department said the sweep that ran from May 2025 to October 2026 was the sixth and most extensive JCODE action since 2018, seizing 5.7 metric tons of drugs and 209 firearms, without saying ho...
content:
The Justice Department and Europol said Thursday that Operation TorNado has produced 354 arrests and the seizure of more than $234 million in cash and virtual currencies, in what the FBI called the largest takedown yet of dark web drug vendors and buyers.

The announcement came from the department’s Joint Criminal Opioid and Darknet Enforcement team, or JCODE, an FBI-led group created in 2018. Officials said Operation TorNado is the sixth, and most extensive, internationally coordinated action since then, and that it builds on last year’s Operation RapTor. The sweep ran from May 2025 to October 2026.

Europol, which coordinated work with agencies in 14 countries, published a parallel statement the same day. The operation targeted vendors and buyers who had been active on five dark web markets already seized by law enforcement: Archetyp, Bohemia, Nemesis, Kingdom and Tor2Door. Officials also identified accounts on DrugHub and on forums, single-vendor shops and encrypted messaging services.

The seizures included about 5.7 metric tons of illicit drugs worldwide, among them fentanyl and other opioids, methamphetamine, heroin, cocaine, ecstasy and MDMA, plus 38 pill presses and 209 firearms. Neither the Justice Department nor Europol split the $234 million between cash and cryptocurrency, and neither named bitcoin or any other coin in the official totals.

Europol put the European share at more than €60 million in cash and cryptocurrencies, alongside 950 kilograms of drugs and 57 firearms, and the U.S. share at more than €150 million, or $166 million, in cash and cryptocurrencies, plus more than 4.8 metric tons of drugs and 152 firearms. Those regional money figures still combine cash and crypto. Europol said its forensic and blockchain analysis teams traced illicit transactions as part of the work.

Individual cases point to Monero and bitcoin

The closest official window into how the vendors were paid comes from the cases the Justice Department highlighted and from court papers posted with the announcement.

Alexander Green, 32, of Jacksonville, North Carolina, was arrested in June and charged in the Southern District of Ohio with conspiracy to distribute controlled substances, including fentanyl. The department said he allegedly operated a vendor called STARLABS on DrugHub, which it described as a Monero-only dark web market, and that the group has been linked to two overdose deaths. A criminal complaint says undercover purchases from STARLABS were made “in exchange for cryptocurrency.” If convicted, he faces up to 20 years in prison.

In a separate Florida arrest, brothers Stanislav Chernyshov, 30, and Vladislav Chernyshov, 35, are charged in the Eastern District of Virginia with conspiracy to distribute Schedule I synthetic opioids. Prosecutors say they allegedly ran the vendor “BarbaraWhite,” selling counterfeit oxycodone pills laced with nitazenes and shipping more than 1,000 parcels across 49 states. A search-warrant affidavit describes bitcoin transfers tied to that account and the Nemesis market. They each face up to 20 years if convicted.

132 arrests in the United States, and more work ahead

Operation TorNado led to 132 arrests in the United States, 59 in the United Kingdom, 45 in Hungary and 41 in Germany, along with arrests in France, New Zealand, the Netherlands, Slovenia, Austria, Ireland, Czechia, Australia and Finland. A number of investigations are still ongoing to identify the people behind remaining dark web accounts, the department said.

FBI Director Kash Patel called Operation TorNado “the largest interagency takedown of Dark Web drug vendors and buyers to date.” IRS Criminal Investigation Chief Jarod Koopman, whose agency was part of the JCODE group, put the financial work at the center: “Criminal networks may operate across borders and in the shadows of the Dark Web, but they cannot operate without money.”

Federal prosecutions are underway in more than 20 districts. An indictment or complaint only alleges that crimes were committed, and the defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty.

What the announcement does not settle is how much of the $234 million was cryptocurrency, and how much of that was bitcoin. Officials have not said. The record on Operation TorNado shows a combined cash-and-crypto seizure, a Monero-only market in at least one featured case, and bitcoin transfers in court papers, without a breakdown of the total.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: NK hackers join memecoin trenches, xStocks adds Hong Kong equities: Asia Express
summary: North Korean hackers launch memecoins to launder funds stolen in the Binance hack, while xStocks plans to add hundreds of Hong Kong-listed equities in the coming weeks.
content:
North Korean hackers create memecoins to launder funds 

North Korean hackers created memecoins to launder cryptocurrency stolen in the $6.3 billion Binance hack, according to a report from blockchain analytics firm Elliptic.

Between Nov. 5 and 7, the hackers created at least six tokens on NEAR and used liquidity pools on decentralized exchanges to move $430,000 of stolen funds between wallets, Elliptic said. However, the tokens attracted almost no outside trading and were abandoned shortly after launch.

Elliptic said the same laundering technique was also used following the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in 2025, when North Korean-linked actors moved at least $24 million through a newly created token on the TRON blockchain.

HONG KONG

Hong Kong’s wealthy investors are embracing crypto. (Chi Hung Wong)

xStocks tokenizes 200 stocks in UK and EU, with hundreds from Hong Kong coming soon

Kraken parent Payward’s xStocks platform has added tokenized versions of more than 200 stocks listed in the United Kingdom and European Union. 

Payward said the latest expansion brings xStocks’ offering to more than 1,500 tokenized assets. The company reported more than $45 billion in cumulative transaction volume and over 550,000 unique holders.

Payward said it plans to add hundreds of Hong Kong-listed equities in the coming weeks.

Hong Kong’s forthcoming crypto licensing regime

Deputy Secretary for Financial Services Chan Ho-lim told FinTech Week the region will introduces a new licensing regime for virtual-asset trading, custody, advisory and management, via amendment bills that will be submitted to Legislative Council this year.


More Hong Kong news

Police have arrested 22 people in a cross border money laundering investigation, that allegedly involved a over the counter crypto network that moved more than HKD$150 million (US$18 million) while attempting to obscure the origin of funds. Meanwhile, the US has sanctioned 41 entities allegedly linked to the Cambodia’s Prince Group, including a man named Qiu Yong, who is accused of running Hong Kong companies on behalf of the criminal organization.

SOUTH KOREA

South Korea to permit crypto withdrawal freezes during hacking threats

South Korea’s Financial Services Commission (FSC) plans to allow crypto exchanges to suspend deposits and withdrawals when hacking is suspected, rather than waiting until a breach is confirmed.

The FSC said it would issue a no-action letter permitting preventive suspensions under certain conditions. Current rules prohibit exchanges from blocking withdrawals without legitimate grounds and explicitly allow restrictions only when a hacking incident is clearly established.

The regulator also called for round-the-clock monitoring and incident response, higher cold-wallet holdings, and stronger insurance coverage and reserves.

GOPAX puts everything on ice

South Korean crypto exchange GOPAX announced on November 6 it was suspending trading, deposits and withdrawals and moving all user assets to cold wallets. The firm had received threatening emails that claimed a hack was imminent, and took the drastic step of putting everything on ice on the recommendation of financial authorities.


JAPAN

Nomura explores sale of crypto unit Laser Digital

Japanese financial services giant Nomura Holdings is reportedly weighing a sale of its cryptocurrency subsidiary Laser Digital as Nomura’s European operations continue to post losses.

Nomura has held talks with potential buyers, including Marex Group but is yet to make a final decision and could keep the business.

Nomura’s European businesses posted a pretax loss of 7.4 billion yen ($46.5 million) in the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026, their fourth consecutive quarterly loss. The company posted pretax profits in every other reporting region over the same period.

THAILAND

Thailand is examining new rules for ETFs and ICO investors (Sasint)

Thailand proposes $148K daily cap on stablecoin deposits and withdrawals

Thailand’s securities regulator has proposed capping daily stablecoin deposits and withdrawals at 5 million baht ($148,000) each per customer at regulated crypto operators.

The limit would apply separately to deposits and withdrawals at each operator, Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said in a Thursday announcement. The regulator said the rules aim to curb money laundering, cybercrime and attempts to bypass cross-border money transfer rules.

The draft would bar stablecoin transfers to and from third-party wallets.


More Thailand news

Thailand’s SEC will block access to Bitget from December 5. It has also proposed new tests for retail investors before allowing them to invest in ICOs. The tests would require knowledge of at least six areas including digital tokens and investor rights, blockchain technology, digital-asset wallets and distribution channels. The proposals will be up for comment until November 25. The SEC is also seeking feedback on new rules around margin loans and ETFs, but has ruled out allowing leveraged or crypto ETFs at this stage.

Vietnam

South Korean crypto firm Bithumb Asset, has invested $85 million into a luxury resort project in Hoi An in Vietnam being built by local real estate developer Asia Estate. Da Nang police have issued a warning about scams via “ghost” cryptocurrency projects that are really just ponzi schemes in disguise. They highlighted a fraud ring involving the DRK cryptocurrency project, led by Huynh Duc Van, 33, and seven accomplices, which was recently dealt with by law enforcement.

SINGAPORE

Nomura’s former head of crypto derivatives trading, John Kim, has joined Chicago-based DV Trading in Singapore to lead a new discretionary crypto-trading team. A Singapore woman lost S$78,000 (US$60,391) in a four-month long crypto scam after someone posing as an insurance buyer “helped” her to set up a crypto wallet. She initially believed she was making money, before getting cleared out after she was directed to the little known Qevorinex platform. International bank communication network Swift argued at Singapore FinTech Festival for shared standards to prevent digital assets from fragmenting across incompatible systems.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, Nvidia shares plunged after co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO and left the board. Coinbase’s head of EU policy said tighter DeFi rules could push users toward riskier platforms. Binance’s security chief warned about fake job interviews months before attackers used a similar tactic in the exchange’s $6.3 billion hack.

Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, exits board; shares plunge

Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as president and CEO and stepped down from the company’s board on Thursday, effective immediately. The board named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO.

Kress will retain her role as CFO while Nvidia’s board considers internal and external candidates for the permanent CEO role. The board also appointed Harvey C. Jones its first chair and said it expects Nvidia’s operations to proceed without interruption.

Nvidia shares fell more than 13% shortly after the US market opened on Thursday, trading at $151.00 as of 2:31 p.m. UTC, according to Yahoo Finance. Bitcoin (BTC) fell alongside Nvidia shares, dropping as much as 3.5% to a multimonth low.

The shares later pared losses to trade at $165 at 4:24 p.m. UTC, down 5% on the day. The stock was down more than 26% over the previous month.

EU DeFi proposals could push users to riskier platforms, says Coinbase exec

European Union efforts to tighten oversight of decentralized finance (DeFi) could drive crypto users toward platforms offering fewer investor protections, according to Coinbase’s head of EU policy.

Roeland Van der Stappen told Cointelegraph that regulated crypto platforms could respond by limiting or dropping access to DeFi services.

“Rules designed to protect investors would end up pushing activity towards the places with the least protection,” Van der Stappen said.

In its September response to the European Commission’s consultation on the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), the European Securities and Markets Authority recommended creating a new category of regulated crypto services for firms that give customers access to DeFi protocols.

Binance CSO unwittingly foreshadowed $6.3B hack tactic months before attack

Months before Binance lost $6.3 billion to a hack, its chief security officer described to Cointelegraph how a fake job interview could give attackers a foothold inside the exchange — closely resembling one of the entry methods later used against the exchange.

During a July interview about Binance’s response to rising security threats, Jimmy Su told Cointelegraph that fake job interviews were “something we worry about a lot internally,” explaining how attackers could tailor a job opportunity to an employee before persuading them to run code as part of a technical assessment. 

“And once that gets executed, the device is compromised and then they can start harvesting credentials,” Su said, adding that attackers could then use that to penetrate further into the network.

Su’s detailed warning about malicious coding assessments was not included in Cointelegraph’s July coverage, but takes on new significance following the biggest crypto exchange hack in history.

title: Kalshi ends Donald Trump Jr. advisory role over Polymarket investment: Reuters
summary: The prediction market operator said the decision was mutual and followed 1789 Capital’s investment in rival Polymarket, denying political considerations.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 12, 2026

The prediction market operator said the decision was mutual and followed 1789 Capital’s investment in rival Polymarket, denying political considerations.

Prediction market platform Kalshi has ended its advisory relationship with Donald Trump Jr. after his venture capital firm increased its investment in rival Polymarket, Reuters reported Thursday.

A Kalshi spokesperson told Reuters that talks about ending Trump Jr.’s advisory role began in August, after Trump Jr.’s venture capital firm, 1789 Capital, took the lead on Polymarket’s $1 billion funding round. The round would value the company at $21 billion, with 1789 Capital set to contribute about $300 million.

“We have mutually agreed to end Don’s advisory role after his firm’s significant investment in a competitor this past summer,” the spokesperson said.

Trump Jr. joined Kalshi as a strategic adviser in January 2025 and received an equity stake reportedly worth $300,000 at the time, according to the Financial Times.

Kalshi’s spokesperson said political considerations played no role in the decision. Two people familiar with the matter told Reuters, however, that some within Kalshi had raised concerns about what Democrats’ midterm sweep of both chambers of Congress could mean for the company.

title: Russia Sets November 22 Start for Exchange Crypto Trading, Subject to Approval
summary: Russia’s central bank has set November 22 as the earliest start under new exchange trading rules, with each venue’s rulebook requiring regulatory concurrence.
content:
TL;DR: Russian exchanges may begin cryptocurrency trading from November 22 if their trading rules receive the Bank of Russia’s concurrence. The November 11 announcement sets operating requirements for venues. A separate asset-eligibility ordinance takes effect on November 17, so the two dates describe different regulatory steps.

Russia has added another piece to its regulated crypto market framework, with a new ordinance setting the conditions under which exchanges can start trading digital currencies and digital rights. The Bank of Russia’s November 11 notice identifies November 22 as the earliest start under those rules, subject to the regulator agreeing to a venue’s trading arrangements.

That condition matters. An effective date creates a legal opening; it does not show that every exchange is technically ready or that every prospective customer can place an order on the same morning.

The exchange rulebook comes into focus

Under the announcement, exchanges must register trading participants, maintain records of orders and transactions, and monitor trading. They also have to calculate specified prices and report trading information to the central bank using the procedures applied to other assets.

These requirements address the organisation of a market: who participates, how activity is recorded and what the supervisor can inspect. The notice says the Ministry of Justice has registered the ordinance. It does not name a completed launch at a particular exchange or provide a forecast for trading volumes.

Why November 17 is a different milestone

The central bank’s November 6 asset-eligibility announcement set a November 17 effective date for an ordinance covering Bitcoin, Ether and USDT. That notice deals with which assets non-qualified investors may access and the conditions attached to their purchases.

Non-qualified investors face an annual purchase ceiling of 300,000 rubles through a single intermediary. Qualified investors are not subject to that asset-list and purchase-limit restriction. The central bank says investors in both groups must pass the relevant test and familiarise themselves with crypto investment risks before transacting.

Reading the announcements together avoids a misleading single-date headline. One concerns the eligible assets and investor conditions; the other concerns organised trading requirements. Neither removes the need to check when a particular intermediary actually makes a service available.

Domestic permission and platform access differ

A national regulatory opening can exist alongside changes at individual international exchanges. NewsBTC previously reported KuCoin’s withdrawal from Russia and Belarus, where affected users’ account notices determine their closure deadlines.

Those developments should be assessed separately. A domestic venue’s permission does not change another company’s service terms, and an international exchange exit does not by itself tell us when a domestic alternative will be usable.

For a trader, the practical questions include the identity of the intermediary, the assets it supports, how a purchase is funded and where holdings are kept. For an exchange, reliable records and price calculations become part of delivering a functioning service rather than merely announcing one.

A new route does not measure new demand

The market impact depends on participation after services open. An expanded route into Bitcoin could bring additional buyers, but it could also shift activity from one channel to another. Permission alone cannot distinguish those outcomes or establish how much fresh capital will arrive.

There is a longer institutional backdrop. NewsBTC reported VTB’s conditional plans for direct crypto trading in December 2025. That historical proposal helps explain interest in domestic access, but it is not evidence that the bank has launched a service under the latest rules.

The next meaningful evidence from Russia will be venue-specific launch notices, completed onboarding and observable trading activity. Until those arrive, November 22 is best understood as a conditional regulatory starting point. It is a material step toward an organised market, with implementation still determining what customers can actually do.

written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Strategy stock sheds 5% amid MSCI index removal, Bitcoin sell-off
summary: Strategy shares declined Thursday following MSCI’s decision to remove the company from its indexes, as Bitcoin also fell amid a broader crypto market decline.
content:
Shares of Michael Saylor’s Bitcoin treasury company Strategy fell 6.49% on Thursday, closing at $114.41, a day after MSCI confirmed the company’s removal from its global equity indexes and amid a broader cryptocurrency market sell-off.

On Wednesday, MSCI confirmed that Strategy would be removed from its global equity indexes after the Nov. 30 market close, a move that could trigger selling by funds tracking the benchmarks. JPMorgan previously estimated that the exclusion could result in roughly $2.8 billion in selling pressure.

Source: Yahoo Finance

Ryan Kirkley, CEO of Global Settlement Network, told Cointelegraph that MSCI’s decision could help distinguish Bitcoin treasury companies from traditional operating businesses and limit indirect cryptocurrency exposure for passive investors.

“Index inclusion meant ordinary passive investors, like someone holding a global index fund in their pension, were getting leveraged Bitcoin exposure they never chose. MSCI just fixed that,” he said.

Kirkley added that MSCI’s decision also raises broader questions about whether Bitcoin treasury companies should be classified alongside traditional operating businesses.

MSCI has said publicly what many people in institutional finance have been saying privately for a while: buying an asset and holding it isn’t an operating business. It’s a fund that doesn’t follow fund rules.

In its Aug. 31 response to MSCI’s proposed rules, Strategy argued that the changes were a pretext for targeting digital asset treasury companies. It also downplayed the potential financial impact, saying MSCI-linked funds held approximately 13 million of its shares, representing just 3.1% of its basic shares outstanding.

The stock’s decline coincided with a broader cryptocurrency market sell-off. Bitcoin traded near $71,340 as of 4:08 p.m. ET on Thursday, down 4.3% over the past 24 hours, according to CoinGecko data. The total cryptocurrency market capitalization declined 3% to around $2.49 trillion.

title: Futurebit Bitcoin Mining Rigs Hit Retail Stores as Solo Miners Keep Winning Big
summary: Bitcoin mining hardware is heading to retail store shelves as Futurebit partners with electronics retailer Micro Center to sell its Apollo III home mining machines, opening another avenue for consumers to participate in a network increasingly dominated by industrial-scale operations. Brooklyn-based ...
content:
Bitcoin mining hardware is heading to retail store shelves as Futurebit partners with electronics retailer Micro Center to sell its Apollo III home mining machines, opening another avenue for consumers to participate in a network increasingly dominated by industrial-scale operations.

Key Takeaways

  • Futurebit is bringing home bitcoin mining to retail, partnering with Micro Center to sell its Apollo III machines at four U.S. locations starting Nov. 13.
  • The Apollo III delivers up to 18 TH/s using 3nm ASIC chips, with an integrated Bitcoin full node and solo mining capabilities that let users independently validate transactions and compete for block rewards.
  • Solo miners are increasingly making headlines for beating enormous odds, including 38 documented block discoveries in 2026, though winning remains exceptionally unlikely given Bitcoin’s massive network hashrate.

Brooklyn-based Futurebit announced Thursday that its Apollo III Full Node will be available at four Micro Center locations beginning Friday, Nov. 13. The initial rollout covers stores in Brooklyn, New York; Miami, Florida; Tustin, California; and Austin, Texas, coinciding with the grand opening of Micro Center’s new Austin location. Customers can also reserve the machines online for in-store pickup.

The partnership marks Futurebit’s first entry into physical retail, allowing customers to examine mining hardware and learn about bitcoin mining before purchasing a machine.

“When we started Futurebit, we made weekly trips to the DIY electronics section at the Brooklyn Micro Center to buy parts,” said Futurebit founder John Stefanopoulos, in a statement. He added that customers will now be able to purchase miners designed near that same store.

Futurebit unveiled the Apollo III in February, introducing a desktop-sized mining system powered by American-engineered 3-nanometer ASIC chips. The machine delivers up to 18 terahash per second (TH/s) in Turbo mode, while its lower-power Eco mode offers efficiency of up to 15 joules per terahash.

The device also incorporates a full Bitcoin node, built-in solo mining capabilities, an eight-core ARM processor, 8GB of RAM, and up to 2TB of storage. Its integrated design allows users to independently validate Bitcoin transactions and attempt to mine blocks without relying on an external mining pool.

More Solo Mining Wins to Come?

The retail expansion arrives amid growing attention surrounding solo miners who have successfully discovered Bitcoin blocks despite extraordinarily unfavorable odds.

Bitcoin.com News reported Wednesday that a solo miner operating through CKPool discovered block 975427, collecting a BTC reward worth approximately $230,000. The discovery marked the 38th documented solo-mining victory of 2026.

In late October, a Futurebit Apollo miner was credited with discovering block 973262, marking the fourth documented solo block from the company’s hardware and its first since March 2025. Another independent miner discovered a block the following day using approximately 16.2 TH/s of computing power.

Other successful miners have used considerably smaller devices. In July, a hobbyist operating a palm-sized Bitaxe machine at approximately 1 TH/s discovered a block worth roughly $200,000 at the time after just eight hours of operation.

Such victories remain exceptionally rare. With Bitcoin’s network computing power around 1,000 exahash per second, an individual Apollo III operating at its maximum 18 TH/s represents only a tiny fraction of the total network hashrate. Even continuous operation could mean decades or centuries between statistically expected block discoveries.

For Futurebit, however, the retail push is about more than winning mining rewards. The company argues that making independent mining and node operation accessible to ordinary consumers can help distribute Bitcoin’s infrastructure beyond the industrial mining companies and major pools that currently dominate the network.

title: Combos, Sports and Crypto Drove Prediction Markets’ Record September as Politics Lagged
summary:
Political contracts generated $901 million in September across four prediction-market platforms, a small share of a record trading month even as the US midterm elections approached. 
Sports, crypto, and multi-event contracts drove much more activity, offering trading opportunities beyond election cy...
content:
2026-11-12T23:30:00.000+02:00

Thursday, 12/11/2026 | 21:30 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Sports, crypto and combos generated 94% of September’s $75.5 billion in nominal prediction-market volume.
  • Kalshi captured 71% of third-quarter dollars paid, while its low-priced combos made nominal trading volume look much larger than buyers’ spending.

Political contracts generated $901 million in September across four prediction-market platforms, a small share of a record trading month even as the US midterm elections approached.

Sports, crypto, and multi-event contracts drove much more activity, offering trading opportunities beyond election cycles. Those three categories accounted for 94% of September’s $75.5 billion in nominal volume, according to Prediction Frontier’s third-quarter report.

The research covers Kalshi, Polymarket’s international and US venues, and Novig. The monthly record coincided with the start of the NFL and college football seasons.

Short Contracts Create Repeat Trading Opportunities

Sports provide a continuing calendar of matches, while short-duration crypto contracts let traders take positions on repeated price movements.

Kalshi, for example, offers contracts on whether cryptocurrency prices rise or fall over 15-minute windows. Prediction markets traders can redeploy proceeds after each position settles rather than wait for a distant election result.

Combos work differently. They combine several outcomes into one position, similar to a sportsbook parlay, and some trade for only a few cents. Kalshi offers them across sports and other event categories, so combos should not automatically be counted as sports trading.

Their low prices also affect reported scale. A contract with a maximum $1 payout contributes $1 to nominal volume even if the buyer pays only a few cents. Cheap combos can therefore produce substantial headline turnover from relatively small purchases.

Kalshi’s Lead Looks Different in Dollars Paid

Kalshi combos alone generated $34.2 billion in September nominal volume. Kalshi’s share rose from 69% in July to 73% in August and September, although Novig enters the dataset only from August 4.

Over the same period, Kalshi’s average purchase price per $1 contract fell from 32 cents to 24 cents. The report attributes that decline to combos; Polymarket’s average remained around 50 cents.

The falling purchase price means each dollar spent generated more nominal volume. Politics still mattered to individual venues: Polymarket US handled more than half of September’s political trading.

Across the four platforms, however, sports, crypto and combos supplied 94% of the nominal volume behind the monthly record. The industry reached that high before the final weeks of the midterm campaign, without an election-driven surge.

title: USDC Enters Dual EU Supervision as EBA Oversight Takes Effect
summary: USDC’s joint European supervision begins November 12 under MiCA.
content:
TL;DR: USDC’s European supervision changes on November 12, with the EBA and France’s ACPR sharing responsibilities.

USDC’s European regulatory status moves from an announced designation to an operating supervisory arrangement on November 12. That is the date set in the European Banking Authority’s October decision, which classified Circle’s dollar token as the EU’s first significant e-money token under MiCA.

NewsBTC covered the original significant-token designation last month. The development now is the scheduled transfer of specified responsibilities, making this a practical test of how the EU supervises a widely used stablecoin across agencies.

What changes on November 12

The EBA takes direct responsibility for own funds, reserves, liquidity requirements, and recovery and redemption plans. France’s Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution remains responsible for areas including governance, outsourcing, conflicts of interest and assessments of key personnel.

Circle Internet Financial Europe SAS is the relevant European issuing entity. The arrangement therefore divides duties between supervisors rather than replacing French oversight altogether. For anyone assessing a stablecoin provider, identifying the responsible legal entity remains part of understanding the regulatory framework.

Why significant status adds another layer

The EBA’s explanation of its MiCA role says significant tokens face additional requirements because of the greater risks they may pose. Its framework combines assessments of significance, direct supervisory tasks and cooperation with national authorities.

For significant e-money tokens issued by electronic money institutions, the EBA focuses mainly on the additional liquidity and own-funds requirements. It also establishes and chairs a supervisory college to support cooperation and information sharing. The framework includes ongoing supervision away from the issuer’s premises alongside targeted on-site work.

Those functions address a different question from whether a token traded near one dollar yesterday. Reserves must support redemptions, and operational arrangements must hold up when conditions become less comfortable. A stable market price provides useful information, but it cannot show every weakness in an issuer’s processes.

Supervision is an ongoing process

An earlier EBA procedural decision describes powers that include requesting information, investigating, inspecting premises and taking supervisory measures. It also sets out how responsibility moves between authorities and how supervisory colleges are established.

That makes the milestone more substantial than an extra label. The significance of the transfer will emerge through continuing oversight and the issuer’s compliance with the applicable obligations. It is not a separate promise that every application using USDC will be secure or that every intermediary will process withdrawals without delay.

Consider a business receiving USDC through a payment processor. The issuer’s reserves, the processor’s handling of the transfer and the business’s own wallet controls are different parts of the transaction. Strengthening one part does not automatically validate the others.

Why businesses will follow the implementation

Stablecoins are increasingly being considered within existing payment systems, including the Circle and ACI settlement work covered by NewsBTC. For a prospective user, a clear supervisory structure can make questions about accountability easier to direct.

The useful next questions concern how supervisory coordination works in practice, how the issuer explains its obligations and what public information becomes available about compliance. Businesses still need to assess their own service providers, contractual rights and operational arrangements.

November 12 establishes a defined oversight structure for a significant European stablecoin. Whether that structure delivers confidence over time will depend on its operation, especially when markets or payment systems come under pressure.

written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Donald Trump Jr. Exits Kalshi Role as Democrats Plan to Scrutinize Family Crypto Ties
summary: Donald Trump Jr. is leaving his advisory position at prediction market platform Kalshi following his firm’s major investment in rival Polymarket, as Democrats prepare to investigate the Trump family’s growing financial interests in cryptocurrency and prediction markets.   The departure, first report...
content:
Donald Trump Jr. is leaving his advisory position at prediction market platform Kalshi following his firm’s major investment in rival Polymarket, as Democrats prepare to investigate the Trump family’s growing financial interests in cryptocurrency and prediction markets.

Key Takeaways

  • Donald Trump Jr. is leaving his Kalshi advisory role after his investment firm, 1789 Capital, made a significant investment in rival prediction market Polymarket, where he remains an adviser.
  • The departure comes after Democrats won control of Congress in the midterm elections, setting the stage for investigations into the Trump family’s cryptocurrency businesses and financial ties to prediction markets.
  • Kalshi and Polymarket face growing regulatory scrutiny as state authorities challenge their sports betting contracts, despite the Trump administration’s more permissive federal approach to prediction markets.

The departure, first reported by Bloomberg, ends an arrangement that had attracted political scrutiny because Trump Jr. simultaneously advised two of the industry’s largest competing platforms.

A Kalshi spokesperson said the decision followed a substantial investment in Polymarket by 1789 Capital, the investment firm where Trump Jr. is a partner.

“We have mutually agreed to end Don’s advisory role after his firm’s significant investment in a competitor this past summer,” the spokesperson told Bloomberg. “We are grateful for his contributions in helping us market Kalshi to more customers.”

Trump Jr. joined Kalshi as a strategic adviser in January 2025, shortly before his father’s second inauguration. Kalshi CEO and co-founder Tarek Mansour initially said Trump Jr. would help guide the company’s expansion, although the platform subsequently characterized his responsibilities as focused on marketing rather than regulatory affairs.

Trump Jr. received equity in Kalshi as compensation for the advisory position, according to Bloomberg. He remains connected to Polymarket through both an advisory role and his firm’s investment.

As previously reported by Bitcoin.com News, 1789 Capital pursued an additional $300 million investment in Polymarket in September, following an earlier $200 million commitment. The latest investment was part of a funding round targeting a $21 billion valuation for Polymarket, while Kalshi hit a $40 billion valuation in late October following its latest $1 billion funding round.

Democrats Plan to Ramp Up Trump Family Scrutiny

The departure comes shortly after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the Nov. 3 midterm elections, creating the prospect of investigations into President Donald Trump’s family businesses and their relationships with federally regulated industries.

Rep. Robert Garcia, the leading Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, identified the Trump family’s business activities as a potential investigative priority.

Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Jeff Merkley have also questioned Trump Jr.’s financial and advisory ties to prediction market platforms, demanding answers from the White House by Nov. 23. Their inquiry follows a Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) settlement with a former Trump White House teleprompter operator accused of using advance knowledge of presidential speeches to place bets on Kalshi. The individual was ordered to pay $173,539 in penalties and received a three-year trading ban.

Warren is expected to lead the Senate Banking Committee when Democrats take control in January, potentially expanding scrutiny of prediction markets and Trump family businesses. Congressional Democrats have already questioned whether companies linked to Trump could benefit from preferential treatment by federal regulators.

The political controversy comes as prediction markets face mounting legal challenges over their expanding sports contracts. The Trump administration’s CFTC has generally supported federal oversight of prediction markets, while state regulators argue that sports-related contracts constitute gambling subject to their laws.

As Bitcoin.com News reported, the CFTC issued guidance on Nov. 5 directing federally regulated prediction exchanges to eliminate state-specific trading restrictions within 30 days or explain why they could not comply. The directive followed court orders restricting Kalshi’s activities in certain jurisdictions, intensifying a dispute between federal regulators and state gambling authorities.

The regulatory conflict has also drawn attention from Republican lawmakers, complicating what had previously been a largely partisan dispute over prediction markets.

Trump Jr.’s departure removes one of Kalshi’s most visible connections to the president’s family, but his continued involvement with Polymarket leaves those financial and political relationships under scrutiny as Democrats prepare to assume control of Congress in January.

Challenged on why two or three down years would matter for Bitcoin when gold and the Nasdaq have had similar streaks before recoveries, Peter Schiff says the difference is the backdrop. When a market can’t go up on the best news it has ever had, he argues, that normally indicates that it’s going to go down. He calls Bitcoin “all hype,” with no intrinsic value, income, or dividends, and says much of the supply now sits with ETF investors and Bitcoin treasury companies rather than people who want to use it as money. All of that hot money, he warns, is going to exit, the market will go down faster than it went up, and he expects a massive washout. Even long-term bulls, he says, will have cheaper opportunities after leveraged speculators are cleared out, and he adds that this is not the time to be hodling.

title: Polymarket Cuts Marketing Contractors as It Seeks a $600K Fraud Chief
summary:
Polymarket is reshaping its workforce as it faces pressure to strengthen management and keep pace with rivals.

content:
2026-11-12T22:01:00.000+02:00

Thursday, 12/11/2026 | 20:01 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Polymarket has cut employees and marketing contractors while continuing to recruit senior fraud and financial-crime staff.
  • The open roles would strengthen payment-fraud controls and build sanctions and AML capacity in its US business.

Polymarket is reshaping its workforce as it faces pressure to strengthen management and keep pace with rivals.

Polymarket said the reorganisation had involved “a lot of new hires, changes in personnel and letting some people go.” It did not disclose the number of departures. However, contractors accounted for more than half of those affected, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters.

Marketing Team Reshaped

Polymarket started restructuring its marketing function back in August, with hiring Travis VanderZanden, former Bird founder, as chief growth officer. He effectively replaced chief marketing officer Matthew Modabber, who had built a team of more than 50 people and was fired in October.

Polymarket also changed the marketing team's organisational structure, rewrote its rules for promotional partners, and hired AlixPartners to monitor its content after the scandal over staged creator videos, triggered by a Wall Street Journal investigation.

The latest cuts reduced Polymarket’s use of marketing contractors in particular, according to knowledgeable sources, cited by Front Office Sports.

However, Polymarket continues hiring in the function. Since mid-October, the company’s careers page has added senior roles including head of user acquisition and head of product marketing.

Fraud Controls from Deposits to Withdrawals

At the same time, the company is strengthening its compliance and anti-fraud departments. A New York-based Head of Fraud position with a base salary of $500,000–$600,000, plus equity and benefits, is among the recent job openings posted on Polymarket's career website.

The successful candidate would build a team to prevent and investigate abuse across the customer journey, from account opening to withdrawals.

The remit covers both customers exploiting the platform and criminals targeting its users. Stolen payment methods, account takeovers and abuse of promotional incentives are among the threats identified. The role also requires measuring fraud losses against false alarms and the friction that controls create for legitimate customers.

Polymarket has previously faced payment fraud in its US business. In February, fraudsters attempted to steal at least $10 million by funding accounts with stolen debit cards, placing wagers and trying to withdraw money to accounts they controlled.

The company faced a different threat on its international platform in October. According to Polymarket’s incident report, attackers compromised a third-party monitoring script and used customers’ active sessions to sell positions and move funds out of their wallets.

The platform paused trading and reset active login sessions. It later said it was returning $3.9 million to traders, including compensation for losses tied to the trading pause.

Polymarket US is also recruiting a Sanctions Compliance Officer and a Senior AML Investigator for its financial-crimes function. The sanctions officer would build a dedicated screening team, while the investigator would join a small team handling an existing caseload.

The marketing cuts have taken effect, but these fraud and financial-crime positions remain open. The next step is to fill them: the sanctions officer would have to build a screening team, while the fraud chief would need product and engineering staff to put controls into customer and payment flows.

title: Onramp Launches Business Bitcoin Accounts With Team Withdrawal Approvals
summary: Onramp’s new business account adds named users and withdrawal approvals. Its more expensive Treasury tier introduces a separate multi-institution custody arrangement.
content:
TL;DR: Onramp has launched a business Bitcoin account with named users, role permissions and withdrawal approvals. A separate Treasury tier adds multi-institution custody. The distinction matters because team account controls and the underlying signing arrangement are different parts of security.

For a company buying Bitcoin, the first operational question arrives quickly: who is allowed to move it? A purchase approved by the board still needs a process for everyday access, record keeping and changes in personnel.

Onramp’s new offering addresses that administrative layer. Its significance is practical: making a corporate Bitcoin position something a finance team can govern through defined responsibilities, rather than treating account access as one person’s private task.

What the launch includes

The company’s November 10 announcement says Onramp Business supports up to three named users, role-based permissions, withdrawal approval policies and an audit trail. The entry account has no monthly charge and a stated 0.85% trading fee, with assets held by a qualified custodian.

Those features are intended to separate initiating a payment from authorizing it. In a well-designed company process, the person preparing a transfer need not have unilateral authority to complete it. An audit trail can then help explain who requested and approved an action if it is later questioned.

That does not remove the need for an internal policy. A system can enforce permissions only after the business decides who should have them, which transfers require review and what happens when an employee leaves.

Treasury adds a different custody structure

Onramp’s current product page lists its Treasury tier from $375 a month, with a 0.65% trading fee. It includes vaults in the company’s name and a structure requiring two of three institutions to move Bitcoin. The page labels custom approval rules as forthcoming.

The basic account should therefore not be described as already including every Treasury feature. Likewise, a planned feature should not appear in a list of capabilities customers can use today.

Separating those tiers also makes pricing easier to interpret. A monthly service charge and a trading fee pay for different things; the cost comparison depends on the amount held, transaction frequency and the control arrangements a company actually needs.

More approvals can reduce concentration of control

Bitcoin.org’s wallet-security guidance explains that multisignature arrangements can require several independent signatures before funds move. The general idea is to make compromise of one device or authority insufficient to authorize a transaction.

Operational approvals in an application and cryptographic signatures are not automatically the same safeguard. A finance team needs to understand both: what its own users can approve, and which parties ultimately control the keys needed to spend the assets.

NewsBTC has covered related approaches through Sygnum’s shared-key Bitcoin lending arrangement and AnchorWatch’s custody and insurance offering. Those services address different use cases, but each makes the allocation of control central to the product.

Corporate adoption requires workable recovery

The less visible test is what happens when normal operations break down. A director may leave, an authorized employee may become unavailable, or a service provider may be unable to complete its part. A company considering custody needs a documented recovery process as well as a normal withdrawal process.

Extra checks can introduce friction, so a treasury also needs to distinguish assets reserved for long-term holding from assets it may need to move quickly. Strong controls are most useful when they fit the business’s actual payment and liquidity requirements.

Onramp’s launch offers another route for putting those responsibilities into a managed service. Whether it suits a particular company depends on the contractual terms, key structure, costs and operating requirements, rather than the existence of a Bitcoin account alone.

written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: ‘Shadow Stocks’: Wall Street Watchdog Fights Massive CFTC Stock Perps Push
summary: The amicus curiae brief, filed by Better Markets, former SEC Commissioner Allison Herren Lee, and Harvard Law Professor John C. Coates, argues that single-stock perpetual futures constitute swaps—and, consequently, bypass current Dodd-Frank Act protections for retail investors under the CFTC’s new r...
content:
1. News
  2. Regulation & Legal
  3. 'Shadow Stocks': Wall Street Watchdog Fights Massive CFTC Stock Perps Push

Published:Nov 12, 2026, 2:45 PM EST

The amicus curiae brief, filed by Better Markets, former SEC Commissioner Allison Herren Lee, and Harvard Law Professor John C. Coates, argues that single-stock perpetual futures constitute swaps—and, consequently, bypass current Dodd-Frank Act protections for retail investors under the CFTC’s new rules.

WRITTEN BY

SHARE

Published: Nov 12, 2026, 2:45 PM EST

Key Takeaways

  • Better Markets backed a lawsuit against the CFTC to stop its approval of perpetual U.S. stock derivatives.
  • The group argues these products are security-based swaps lacking fixed dates, requiring SEC regulation.
  • They warn the 6-to-1 leverage and automatic liquidations could quickly wipe out retail investor portfolios.

Better Markets Files Brief to Challenge CFTC’s Approval Of Perpetual Derivatives

The legal battle over the CFTC’s decision to allow perpetual derivatives on individual U.S. stocks is heating up, and third-parties are now raising their voices.

Better Markets, an organization that “fights for a financial system that serves society and supports the productive economy,” has filed a friend-of-the-court (amicus curiae) brief to back the Capital Markets Alliance’s (CMA) challenge to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s (CFTC) approval of perpetual derivatives on individual U.S. stocks.

In the brief, filed by former SEC Acting Chair and Commissioner Allison Herren Lee and former SEC General Counsel and Acting Director of the Division of Corporate Finance John C. Coates, the organization argues that these perpetuals should be classified as security-based swaps and not futures, as they lack a fixed delivery date.

As a consequence of being classified as security-based swaps, these fall under the SEC’s jurisdiction under the Dodd-Frank Act and must not bypass critical protection measures, including registration and the requirement that trading should only be conducted on regulated national securities exchanges.

Furthermore, Better Markets, which has a history of opposing decentralized initiatives, stresses that approving these swaps brings severe risks to retail investors, as they combine high leverage, no expiration date, and automated liquidation features, enticing the formation of a speculative ecosystem.

“These ‘perpetual futures’ are really shadow stocks that are leveraged roughly six-to-one, meaning an investor’s entire portfolio can be zeroed out with just a 16% movement in the market. That level of volatility is common with single stocks and therefore the risk of total loss is real and likely frequent, ruining retail investors while enriching the platform companies,” said Better Markets, warning about the risks of opening these tools to retail investors.

“As we have seen in other nations where these products proliferate, investors can get wiped out in a matter of minutes, including overnight when automatic liquidation thresholds can be triggered,” the organization concluded.

Better Markets’ opinions coincide with those of the CMA, which stressed that the CFTC’s recent approval of a multitude of filings for securities-based products fails to explain why it has long treated perpetual derivatives as swaps, and disregards the impact that this new vision will have on investors and the wider securities market.

The CMA, representing industry heavyweights like Cboe Global Markets, Citadel Securities, and Healthy Markets Association, asks to vacate the approvals of these products and acknowledge that they constitute security-based swaps, effectively barring the CFTC’s purported ability to approve them while the case is pending.

The case is becoming a major battle facing industry incumbents and the CFTC, which is also facing state regulators over prediction markets. The SEC has already filed an amicus brief supporting the CFTC’s new rule changes, contesting CMA’s allegations that it is “going rogue.”

About the author

WRITTEN BYSergio Goschenko

Sergio is a cryptocurrency journalist based in Venezuela with 2,000+ articles published, cited in dozens of papers and reports.

Simon Dixon, CEO and co-founder of BnkToTheFuture, tells BMTV there are only three things that would make him sell all of his Bitcoin and buy gold. Since 2011, he says Bitcoin has done three things incredibly well: you can earn and hold it in self-custody, spend it peer-to-peer without a government in the middle, and rely on a fixed supply of 21 million as a hedge against long-term debasement. If any of those three is ever called into question, he would sell immediately. The real battle, in his view, is not whether Bitcoin gets adopted — he says institutional adoption is on a trajectory we have never seen — but whether custodians, Wall Street-owned miners, and treasury companies end up centralizing the network.

title: Interactive Brokers Adds Vise Long Short Across Four Leverage Levels
summary:
Vise has expanded its
Long Short investment strategy to client accounts held at Interactive Brokers,
giving financial advisors access to four leverage levels.
The expansion adds to
Interactive Brokers' existing services for financial advisors and portfolio
managers. Earlier, the broker also integrat...
content:
2026-11-12T20:15:00.000+02:00

Thursday, 12/11/2026 | 18:15 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • The broker joins Schwab, Fidelity, Goldman Sachs, Raymond James, TradePMR and Altruist as Vise-supported custodians.
  • Vise extends daily tax-loss harvesting and wash-sale screening to long-short accounts held at Interactive Brokers.

Vise has expanded its Long Short investment strategy to client accounts held at Interactive Brokers, giving financial advisors access to four leverage levels.

The expansion adds to Interactive Brokers' existing services for financial advisors and portfolio managers. Earlier, the broker also integrated with third-party investment-management platforms, including robo-advisor Emotomy.

London's trading industry is coming home!

In 2025, Interactive Brokers introduced its Tax Planner, which provides tax-related portfolio insights and supports tax-loss harvesting. Vise's integration adds another investment strategy to the broker's offering for advisors.

Vise Targets Investors with Large Unrealised Gains

The move comes as some large custodians have raised minimum investment requirements or paused new accounts for tax-aware long-short strategies. This has limited access for advisors managing smaller client portfolios.

Vise Long Short extends the company's direct indexing offering. It combines long positions in stocks expected to outperform with short positions in stocks expected to underperform, while maintaining 100% net long market exposure. The strategy aims to generate higher pre-tax returns at market-level risk.

Holding both long and short positions creates opportunities for tax-loss harvesting in different market conditions. Vise applies daily tax-loss harvesting to every account, including during rising markets when long-only portfolios may offer fewer opportunities to realise losses.

Vise Adds IBKR Across Seven Custodian Networks

The strategy targets clients with large unrealised capital gains. These include investors holding concentrated stock positions or proceeds from business sales and real estate disposals.

"Long short has been treated as a product for a select few. The problem it addresses is not," said Samir Vasavada, Co-Founder and Co-Head of Vise.

On Interactive Brokers, advisors can access all four leverage levels. Vise said some large custodians no longer allow new accounts to access the higher leverage options. Onboarding is fully digital, and new advisory firms can typically start using the service within about two weeks.

Interactive Brokers joins Charles Schwab, Fidelity, Goldman Sachs Custody Solutions, Raymond James, TradePMR, and Altruist as a supported custodian. Vise Long Short can run alongside other strategies on the platform. The system also applies wash-sale screening across accounts sharing the same tax identification number.

The top features that make Binance NFT Marketplace stand out include deep integration with the Binance ecosystem, a competitive fee structure, and unique offerings with gamification features.
