Binance NFT Marketplace Review – What Is It? A Detailed Look

Binance NFT Marketplace is a centralized place where you can buy, sell, and create non-fungible tokens (NFTs). You can use the same account to access the NFT marketplace if you already have a Binance account for trading cryptocurrencies. This makes it easy for people who already use Binance to get into the NFT world.

The marketplace supports NFTs that are created on Ethereum and the Binance Smart Chain (now BNB Chain). One of the best things about using the BNB Chain for NFTs is that it usually costs very little to create or “mint” these tokens, often just a few cents, which is much less than on Ethereum. This can be useful for both creators and buyers who want to save on fees.

There are many ways to get NFTs on the exchange. You can buy NFTs right away for a set price, or you can join an auction and bid on them. You can also buy “Mystery Boxes,” which are boxes that give you a random NFT from a collection, with different levels of rarity.

You have to sign up for Binance and complete identity verification process before you can use the Binance NFT Marketplace. Next, you’ll need to deposit some cryptocurrency, like BNB or Ether, into your account. These are the main payment methods for NFTs on the platform. Binance also has “Initial Game Offerings” (IGOs), which are unique NFT assets from the best gaming projects.

Join Binance today and explore one of the world’s largest NFT marketplaces with low fees, top security, and global access to rare digital collectibles.

What Are Binance NFT Marketplace Pros and Cons?

Pros of Binance NFT Marketplace

The pros of the Binance NFT marketplace are low fees, integration with the Binance exchange, high liquidity, low minting costs on the BNB chain, and strong security measures.

  • Low Fees: Perhaps one of the best things about the Binance NFT Marketplace is that it doesn’t cost much to use. It usually has very low fees for transactions, typically only 1% for buying and selling NFTs. Therefore, when you trade, you get to keep more of your money.
  • Integration with the Binance Ecosystem: If you already use the main Binance exchange to trade cryptocurrencies, it’s very easy to start using the NFT marketplace. You can use your current Binance account, which makes it easy to keep track of all your cryptos and NFTs in one place.
  • High Liquidity and A Large User Base: The NFT marketplace has a lot of users and a lot of trading volume because it is backed by Binance, one of the biggest crypto exchanges in the world. This means it’s generally easier to buy and sell NFTs quickly because there are always people looking to trade.
  • Low Minting Costs on BNB Chain: For creators, minting NFTs on the BNB Chain through Binance NFT Marketplace is very cheap, often costing only a few cents. This is a significant advantage compared to networks like Ethereum, where minting fees can be much higher, making Binance more accessible for new artists.
  • Strong Security Measures: Binance is well-known for its robust security systems, which extend to its NFT marketplace as well. The exchange uses various security features like two-factor authentication and a Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to protect user assets and transactions.

Cons of Binance NFT Marketplace

The cons of Binance NFT Marketplace include centralization issues, a less diverse range of NFT collections, and restrictive minting permissions.

  • Centralization Issues: The Binance NFT Marketplace is a centralized platform, which means that just one company, Binance, controls it. Decentralized platforms are preferred by some in the cryptocurrency community, as they are believed to give users more control and reduce the risk of a single point of failure.
  • Less Diverse NFT Collections (Compared to Older Platforms): Since the Binance NFT Marketplace is relatively newer than some other established platforms, it might not always have the absolute rarest or most sought-after NFT collections. While it’s growing, it’s still building up its unique offerings.
  • Minting Permissions Can Be Restrictive: The process of becoming an authorized creator and minting NFTs on the platform can be more stringent than on some other marketplaces, despite the low minting fees. This suggests that not everyone can immediately begin minting their own NFTs.

Is Binance NFT Marketplace Legit and Safe?

Yes, the Binance NFT Marketplace is generally considered legitimate and safe. It is a part of Binance, the biggest cryptocurrency exchange in the world, and it employs the same robust security measures that safeguard their primary trading platform. 

This includes features like real-time monitoring for suspicious activity, cold storage for assets (keeping them offline), and two-factor authentication. Also, in the event of a significant security breach, they have an insurance fund known as SAFU (Secure Asset Fund for Users) that can assist in covering losses.

What Are Binance NFT Marketplace Supported and Restricted Countries?

The Binance NFT Marketplace is generally available in most countries where Binance itself operates, including over 100 countries across Europe, Asia, Africa, and the Americas, such as France, India, Brazil, and South Africa.

However, Binance services, including the NFT marketplace, are limited or unavailable in a number of countries due to a variety of regulatory restrictions and compliance issues. 

Most notably, the US has its own platform called Binance.US with different regulations and restricted availability by state, rather than accessing the global Binance NFT Marketplace. Canada, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, Iran, Cuba, Syria, North Korea, and the Crimean region of Ukraine are among the other nations where the Binance NFT Marketplace is typically restricted.

Can You Use Binance NFT Marketplace in the US?

No, you cannot use the Binance NFT Marketplace in the US because Binance.com is not available for US residents due to regulatory restrictions. Also, Binance has a separate platform called Binance.US, but as of now, it does not support NFTs. Hence, if you try to use a VPN or fake location, your account can be flagged or banned.

What Are the Key Features of Binance NFT Marketplace?

Key features of Binance NFT Marketplace include integration with the Binance ecosystem, a competitive fee structure, unique NFT offerings, high security and trustworthiness, and a user-friendly platform for all devices.

Integration With the Binance Ecosystem

Binance NFT Marketplace integrates with the broader Binance blockchain infrastructure, including their crypto exchange. This implies that you don’t need to create a new wallet just for NFTs or create a separate login if you already have an account with Binance for cryptocurrency trading. 

The entire process is very convenient because you can use your current Binance account. Your money, whether in BNB, BUSD, or ETH, is easily accessible on the same platform, making it simple to switch between trading cryptocurrencies and collecting or selling NFTs. It also leverages Binance’s massive existing user base, creating a large pool of potential buyers and sellers, which is crucial for a liquid marketplace.

Competitive Fee Structure

The Binance NFT Marketplace boasts a highly competitive fee structure, which is a major draw for many users. Binance typically charges a flat platform service fee of only 1% of the sale price when NFTs are bought or sold on the platform.

So, compared to many other NFT marketplaces, which generally charge higher percentages, sometimes ranging from 2.5% to even 7.5% or more, this is significantly lower. A good percentage of the profits from successful sales can be kept by creators and sellers thanks to this small fee. Additionally, for NFTs minted on the BNB Chain through the platform, the gas fees for minting are notably low, often just a few cents, making it very economical for artists and creators to launch their collections without incurring high upfront costs.

Unique Offerings and Gamification

Binance NFT Marketplace provides some interesting and unique ways to get NFTs that go beyond simple direct purchases or auctions. They offer “Mystery Boxes”, which are like digital lucky dips where you can buy a box and get some random NFT from a collection, adding an element of surprise and excitement. 

Also, they heavily feature “Initial Game Offerings” (IGOs), where exclusive NFT assets from popular gaming projects are launched, often involving in-game items or early access passes.

Security, Compliance, and Trust

As an extension of Binance, the NFT Marketplace benefits from the same robust security measures and a strong commitment to regulatory compliance. Here, Binance employs industry-leading security protocols, including advanced two-factor authentication, cold storage for a significant portion of user assets (keeping them offline to protect against hacks), and continuous real-time monitoring for suspicious activities and potential threats.

Additionally, the platform offers a Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), an emergency insurance fund created to safeguard users’ assets in dire situations. Hence, a more secure environment is created by this strong emphasis on security, as well as Binance’s attempts to adhere to international laws and carry out Know Your Customer (KYC) identity verification. Also, the exchange is trusted by over 275 million users globally.

User-Friendly to All Devices

The Binance NFT Marketplace is designed with a strong focus on user-friendliness across various devices. The platform’s interface is user-friendly and intuitive, regardless of whether you prefer to access it on a desktop computer, tablet, or smartphone through the Binance mobile app. 

Even those who are unfamiliar with NFTs can use it because of their simple and uncluttered design. A consistent and enjoyable user experience is ensured by the responsive design, which makes sure the layout adapts fluidly to various screen sizes. Its cross-device compatibility guarantees that you can interact with the marketplace from your preferred device without encountering any technical difficulties. You can easily browse collections, place bids, manage your NFTs, and track sales conveniently, anytime and anywhere.

What Are Binance NFT Marketplace Fees?

The Binance NFT marketplace fee is 1% for successful NFT sales. The types of fees Binance NFT Marketplace charges are platform fees, creator royalty fees, listing fees, burning fees, deposit & withdrawal fees, and minting fees.

Platform Fees

The Binance NFT Marketplace charges a low platform fee of 1% on every successful NFT sale, and this fee is taken from the final sale price of the NFT. So, if an NFT sells for $100, Binance will generally take around $1 as its platform fee.

Creator Royalty Fees

Creator royalty fees are paid to the original NFT creator each time the NFT is resold. Here, Binance allows all the creators to set their own royalty rate, so you can set between 1% and 10%, and this fee is added to the sale price and paid by the seller.

Listing Fees

Binance NFT Marketplace does not charge any fees for listing NFTs for sale. Hence, you can easily list your NFT up for auction or set a fixed price without paying an upfront fee.

Burning Fees

Burning an NFT means sending it to a null address where it can no longer be accessed. Hence, it is effectively removed from circulation. So, if you choose to burn an NFT on a blockchain network supported by Binance NFT Marketplace, you will need to pay a standard network transaction fee (gas fee) for that action, and here, Binance itself does not charge a specific “burning fee,” but the underlying blockchain network does.

Deposit & Withdrawal Fees

Binance generally does not charge deposit fees. However, when you withdraw cryptocurrencies or NFTs, there will be a withdrawal fee, and again, this fee is not set by Binance but is a network transaction fee that goes to the miners or validators of the blockchain network to process your withdrawal.

Minting Fees

Minting an NFT means creating it and putting it on a blockchain. The cost for minting an NFT on the Binance NFT Marketplace depends on the blockchain you choose. 

If you mint an NFT on the BNB Chain, your minting fees are usually very low, often just a few cents. On the Ethereum blockchain, fees can be much higher and fluctuate greatly depending on network activity. In this case, Binance itself does not add a separate minting fee on top of the network’s gas fee.

Register on Binance today and start trade NFTs and other crypto assets with just a few taps.

How to Use Binance NFT Marketplace: Access, Buy & Sell NFTs?

To use the Binance NFT Marketplace to buy and sell NFTs, you must first log in to Binance or join if you don’t have an account. Then verify identity check before buying NFTs. To understand more about Binance requirements for Binance NFT Marketplace and other services, you can read our review. Here is a detailed guide to help you get started:

Step 1: Get Your Binance Account Ready

First, you need a Binance account. Also, you must finish the identity check (KYC). Without it, you can’t trade NFTs or buy crypto. So, if your regular Binance account is already set up and verified, then you are ready for this step. If you are new, you can also use our Binance referral code during registration and get a free $100 crypto welcome rewards.

Step 2: Deposit Crypto in Your Binance Wallet

Next, put some crypto into your Binance Spot Wallet. You need BNB or ETH, because these are the main popular coins for NFTs on Binance. You can buy these using your local currency or send them from another crypto platform. Make sure you have enough BNB to trade NFTs.

Step 3: Go to the NFT Marketplace

Now, find the NFT marketplace on Binance.

  • On Computer: Go to Binance.com. Look at the top of the page. Click on “NFT”.
  • On Mobile App: Open the Binance app. Swipe down from the top to see “Marketplace”, then find “Binance NFT”. Or, tap “More” and look for “Binance NFT”.

Step 4: Find an NFT You Want

Once you are in the NFT marketplace, look for an NFT you like. You can use the search bar or the filters. You can look by kind (like art or games), price, or by collection name. See what’s new or popular.

Step 5: Buy the NFT

When you pick an NFT, you can buy it. There are different ways:

  • Fixed Price: Click “Buy Now”. Confirm the price. If you have enough crypto, it’s yours right away.
  • Auction: Click “Place a Bid”. Put in your offer. If you are the highest when time runs out, you win.
  • Make an Offer: Click “Make Offer”. Type the price you want to pay. The seller can say yes or no.

Step 6: Sell Your NFT

If you want to sell an NFT you own, you can list it for sale. Here, you can choose the same selling methods, fixed price or auction.

Then, set the price, choose your preferred cryptocurrency for payment, and finalize the listing by confirming and posting it. Also, check all the details. There is a small fee (usually 1%) when your NFT sells. Click “Submit”. Binance will review it, and then your NFT will be for sale.

Start buying and selling NFTs on Binance with just a few clicks – fast setup, smooth interface, and full support for BNB and Ethereum blockchains.

title: FSB Pushes Türkiye Toward Dedicated Stablecoin Rules and Tougher Crypto Oversight
summary:
Key Takeaways: FSB commends Türkiye for making meaningful progress in the regulation of cryptos. The watchdog calls for a separate stablecoin framework, more robust enforcement and an institutionalized financial stability
The post FSB Pushes Türkiye Toward Dedicated Stablecoin Rules and Tougher Cryp...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • FSB commends Türkiye for making meaningful progress in the regulation of cryptos.
  • The watchdog calls for a separate stablecoin framework, more robust enforcement and an institutionalized financial stability tracking system.
  • While crypto companies must be registered and licensed, the FSB notes that this process also needs to be improved in terms of cross- border supervision in Türkiye.

Türkiye is being urged by the Financial Stability Board to do more than just exchange license crypto assets, but establish an entire system of regulation.

The FSB has released its most recent peer review report on Nov. 11, indicating that Turkish authorities have made substantial progress in their oversight and regulatory efforts, but remain somewhat distant from the FSB’s global crypto regulatory framework.

  • Türkiye Has Pulled More Crypto Firms Into Regulation
  • Stablecoins Remain the Biggest Regulatory Gap
    • FSB Wants Stronger Enforcement and Cross-Border Coordination

Türkiye Has Pulled More Crypto Firms Into Regulation

Türkiye has already taken the majority of its crypto market on board into the regulatory fold.

In March 2025, the Capital Markets Board issued in-depth provisions on crypto assets service providers which include provisions on establishment and activities and capital requirements. The regulations came in the wake of a legal amendment in 2024 that transferred the regulatory control of crypto service providers to the regulator.

The FSB also noted the measures to limit financial connections between crypto markets and traditional finance.

These are the rule of separating the customer assets held in custody as well as the ban on cryptocurrencies in domestic payments imposed on the Republic of Türkiye. Additionally, a centralized data platform has been established for tracking crypto activity.

Read More: Visa Adds Monad to Stablecoin Settlement Network

Stablecoins Remain the Biggest Regulatory Gap

The clearest gap identified by the FSB is stablecoin regulation. At the time of FSB’s 2025 thematic review, broader crypto regulations were completed in Türkiye, although a framework had not been put in place for stablecoins. This most recent review calls for the establishment of one again.

The FSB also wishes Türkiye to establish a formal crypto market monitoring framework to track crypto markets’ potential impacts on financial markets. That would shift the focus from regulating specific exchanges and custodians to regulating the general exposure, interconnections and potential spillovers on the market into banking and payments.

FSB Wants Stronger Enforcement and Cross-Border Coordination

The review also calls for tougher supervision and enforcement. Domestic laws are not very effective when regulators take a long time to share information with their counterparts abroad, as crypto platforms regularly operate in different jurisdictions.

Therefore, the FSB recommends more robust mutual collaboration and information-sharing measures in addition to Türkiye’s domestic licensing process.

The Capital Markets Board of Türkiye has a list of crypto service providers, which aims to list the people planning to work with this new regime in a provisional manner. The regulator explicitly states that it does not imply a business is fully authorised to be on the list.

The review is part of the FSB’s wider campaign to ensure that all jurisdictions are implementing the 2023 recommendations for cross-border crypto markets and global stablecoin arrangements.

title: Crypto News Today: Bitcoin Loses $72K as $550B Vanishes From Cryptocurrency Market
summary: Bitcoin extended its November decline on Thursday, November 12, briefly falling below $72,000 as heavy liquidations, persistent ETF outflows, and renewed inflation concerns pressured cryptocurrency markets.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Bitcoin extended its November decline on Thursday, November 12, briefly falling below $72,000 as heavy liquidations, persistent ETF outflows, and renewed inflation concerns pressured cryptocurrency markets.

The decline followed a broader deterioration in investor sentiment, with more than $550 billion reportedly erased from the cryptocurrency market since its October highs. Bitcoin’s latest weakness also raised concerns about whether the correction could deepen if institutional demand remains subdued.

Bitcoin Price Breaks Below $72K as Selling Pressure Intensifies

Bitcoin (BTC) fell to approximately $71,548, losing around 2.8% over 24 hours after retreating from an intraday high near $74,695. The decline followed a series of failed attempts to regain the $73,000 level, leaving the market vulnerable to further losses.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Trading activity showed BTC breaking below both $73,000 and $72,000 as sellers gained control. Data from Binance also showed Bitcoin briefly trading below $72,000 on November 12, marking its weakest levels since August, according to market reports.

The cryptocurrency later recovered into the $73,000 range, but the rebound did little to remove concerns about the broader trend. Bitcoin remained under pressure after losing several important short-term price levels.

The decline has also affected the wider digital asset market. Ethereum and other large-cap cryptocurrencies experienced selling pressure as investors reduced exposure to risk-sensitive assets.

Market estimates indicate that more than $550 billion in total cryptocurrency market value has disappeared since October’s highs. Bitcoin has also lost approximately 9% over the past week in the latest reported downturn, reflecting the scale of the correction.

Crypto Liquidations Exceed $650M as Long Traders Take Heavy Losses

Leveraged trading has amplified Bitcoin’s decline, with forced position closures adding to selling pressure across cryptocurrency exchanges.

According to liquidation figures cited in recent market reports, more than $650 million in crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours. One estimate placed total liquidations near $723 million, with approximately 79% involving long positions.

Long liquidations reached $380 million in four hours, contributing to more than $650 million in total crypto liquidations over 24 hours, including $125 million cleared within minutes. Source: @BullTheoryio/X

The pressure intensified during shorter trading windows. WatcherGuru reported that Bitcoin’s drop below $72,000 triggered more than $125 million in long liquidations within 20 minutes. Another report identified approximately $222 million in long positions liquidated over 30 minutes.

Bitcoin futures traders also faced substantial losses. CoinDesk reported that BTC liquidations reached approximately $200.5 million over 24 hours, with 85% involving long positions. Total crypto futures liquidations surged to approximately $725 million during the same period, according to CoinGlass data cited by the publication.

These figures cover different reporting periods and liquidation categories, so they should not be added together.

The mechanism behind these events can accelerate market declines. When leveraged traders fail to maintain sufficient margin, exchanges automatically close their positions. These forced transactions can generate additional selling, pushing prices lower and triggering further liquidations.

The concentration of losses among long traders indicates that many participants were positioned for higher prices before the latest downturn. Their forced exits added pressure to an already weakening market.

Bitcoin ETF Outflows Weaken Institutional Demand

U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds have also contributed to the negative market backdrop. Persistent withdrawals from these investment products have reduced an important source of institutional buying demand.

According to CoinDesk, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $95 million in net outflows on Tuesday, November 10, extending the withdrawal streak to four consecutive trading sessions. The publication reported that BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $78 million of those withdrawals.

A sharp market decline triggered $222 million in crypto long liquidations within just 30 minutes. Source: @WatcherGuru/X

The latest outflows followed withdrawals of approximately $201 million on Monday, $412 million on Friday, and $430 million on Thursday.

Together, these figures highlight sustained selling pressure across the spot ETF market. Other market reports have placed cumulative withdrawals above $1.4 billion over five days, although totals vary depending on the reporting window.

ETF flows matter because these products provide investors with regulated exposure to Bitcoin without requiring direct ownership of the cryptocurrency. Consistent inflows can support market demand, while prolonged withdrawals indicate that some investors are reducing their exposure.

The weakness has also coincided with pressure across technology stocks. Bitcoin’s failure to follow a rebound in Nasdaq-linked assets has raised questions about its near-term demand, particularly as institutional investors reassess their exposure to risk-sensitive markets.

Hotter US Inflation Data Raises Fresh Fed Rate Concerns

Macroeconomic uncertainty has added another challenge for cryptocurrency investors.

The US Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the Consumer Price Index (CPI) increased 0.4% month over month in October, exceeding economists’ expectations of 0.3%. Although the reading was lower than September’s 0.6% increase, it indicated that inflation remained persistent.

Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, increased 0.3% during the month. Shelter costs rose 0.3%, while the food index increased 0.5%.

The hotter-than-expected inflation reading strengthened concerns that the Federal Reserve could maintain restrictive monetary conditions for longer or consider another interest-rate increase.

According to CoinDesk, traders raised the probability of a quarter-point Fed rate hike at the December 8–9 meeting to approximately 90% following the inflation release, based on CME FedWatch data.

Higher interest-rate expectations can weigh on assets such as Bitcoin by increasing the relative appeal of interest-bearing investments and tightening financial conditions. They can also reduce investors’ willingness to maintain leveraged positions in volatile markets.

CoinDesk also reported that stablecoin liquidity had weakened. CryptoQuant data showed that Tether’s USDT market capitalization declined by $6.6 billion over 60 days.

“Stablecoin growth funded every rally this cycle,” CryptoQuant wrote on X, according to CoinDesk.

A contraction in stablecoin supply can indicate reduced purchasing power available within cryptocurrency markets, although it does not independently establish the direction of future prices.

Bitcoin Price Faces $70K Support After Losing $72K

Bitcoin’s latest breakdown has shifted attention toward the $70,000 psychological level as traders assess whether selling pressure will continue.

The recovery above $72,000 offers some evidence that buyers remain active at lower prices. However, sustained trading below the previously established support levels could leave BTC exposed to another downward move.

Losing the $72,000 support level puts Bitcoin at risk of breaking below $70,000. Source: Monolith-Trades/TradingView

The broader market structure also remains under pressure. CoinDesk cited CryptoQuant’s estimate of Bitcoin’s 200-day moving average near $73,200, a level that has become important during the current correction. Its 365-day moving average stood near $76,400, highlighting the distance BTC would need to recover to regain that longer-term benchmark.

ETF flows, derivatives positioning, and macroeconomic developments are likely to remain important indicators of market direction.

For now, Bitcoin’s brief fall below $72,000, substantial long liquidations, and continued institutional fund withdrawals illustrate the challenges facing the cryptocurrency market. A sustained recovery would require stronger buying demand and improved market liquidity, while another loss of support could increase selling pressure toward $70,000.

title: South Korea Gives Crypto Exchanges Power to Freeze Withdrawals on Suspected Hacks
summary:
Key Takeaways: South Korea could temporarily restrict crypto exchange withdrawals during hacks. FSC desires 24/7 monitoring and increased hot-wallet controls. Optimized security checks will be expanded over wallets, blockchains and
The post South Korea Gives Crypto Exchanges Power to Freeze Withdraw...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • South Korea could temporarily restrict crypto exchange withdrawals during hacks.
  • FSC desires 24/7 monitoring and increased hot-wallet controls.
  • Optimized security checks will be expanded over wallets, blockchains and smart contracts.

South Korea is seeking to allow crypto exchanges greater leeway as a suspected hack could result in an actual loss.

The Financial Services Commission said on Nov. 12 that it plans to issue regulatory guidance allowing exchanges to suspend deposits and withdrawals when abnormal activity points to a possible security breach. The move fits into a broader strategy to bring the crypto security standards in line with those for traditional financial institutions.

  • Exchanges Could Freeze Transfers Before a Hack Is Confirmed
  • Cold Wallets and 24/7 Monitoring Move Higher on the Agenda
    • Crypto Security Checks Are Set to Expand

Exchanges Could Freeze Transfers Before a Hack Is Confirmed

Under South Korea’s current Virtual Asset User Protection Act, platforms cannot restrict deposits or withdrawals without a legitimate reason. If a confirmed hacking event occurs, a suspension is warranted but the question had remained unclear of what exchanges could do if suspicious activity occurred before a hack was verified.

The FSC is now looking to fill that void. The regulator will issue a no-action position for preventive restrictions when there is a reason to believe that there is any hacking or unauthorized access. The intent is to evolve the exchanges quickly enough to minimize customer losses, rather than wait until the intrusions are well under way.

The strategy comes amid recent threats to the security of South Korea. GOPAX announced a hacker attack threat on Nov. 6, but deposits, withdrawals and trading were still suspended.

Read More: South Korea Tightens Crypto Exchange Defenses After Binance’s $6.3B Security Breach

Cold Wallets and 24/7 Monitoring Move Higher on the Agenda

The FSC also would like exchanges to keep abreast of continuous monitoring adapted to the 24/7 trading world of crypto.

There should be staff on the platform to identify abnormal transactions and effective controls put in place right away. This leaves exchanges which are incapable of performing continuous monitoring to process deposits and withdrawals at periods where sufficient security personnel are available.

The South Korea government was already pushing for VASPs to store at least 80% of their customers’ virtual assets in cold wallets. FSC said the cold-storage ratio in the industry is already over 95% and the role-players should maintain the hot wallet ratio as little as necessary to facilitate business as usual.

The regulator also advised exchanges to keep their hot wallet money in more than one wallet and have adequate insurance and reserves to pay the users in the event of a breach.

Crypto Security Checks Are Set to Expand

There will also be greater involvement with the Financial Security Institute. The FSC says only five exchanges among 28 virtual asset services have joined the institute in winning its approval. Operators now want to be part of the participation, and authorities are now looking to offer threat intelligence, vulnerability assessments and cybersecurity training to more operators.

The institute is also projected to improve the criteria for transaction checks, wallet access security, integrity of blockchain and smart contract.

The FSC is also developing more comprehensive digital finance laws that would impose cybersecurity requirements akin to those in banking regulations on virtual asset providers. Regulators also want suspected breaches and abnormal external access attempts reported quickly to financial authorities.

我一直说我追求平权，平权意味着抛开性别去评价一个人的成就。女性在职场的机会从不均等，除了适龄女性普遍比男性多生育假期外，确实很多女性对职业生涯秉持“工作不开心还可以嫁人”的心态，导致很多企业管理者在招聘上更倾向于用男性雇员，而职场骚扰也屡见不鲜。所有能跨越重重挑战成长为独当一面的女性leader往往比起其他人花了更多的时间和心力。
女性如果公开露脸为公司做业务，往往在商业竞争中被严重污名化，远的中文主流新闻报道多次引用了友商为币安造的黄谣“币安女团原味内裤，私密小礼物”，还反复贴了我们多位女员工的照片；近期除了Sisi和丫丫在持续被造谣，甚至BNB生态的项目市场负责人，币安合作过的一些KOL，甚至友商的女性员工也被持续的造黄谣；更不用说我丢个身份证被盗用莫名有了黄谣，还有“妈咪”之类的离谱传言。我抗击打能力强，吃得咸鱼抵得渴，但无法想象作为员工，他们的家人朋友反复在新闻媒体看到什么心情。而每一个和币安员工打过交道的人，都会知道这个谣言多无稽，但她们从没有找我抱怨过，只是默默的为用户解决问题，把情绪吞下去，用结果说话。
对那些拿性别搞事、造谣的人型生物账号，这些人应该像蟑螂一样在行业被清理掉，后续我们法务部门将为币安对应的女性员工提供法律保护。欢迎对自己有雄心壮志又能脚踏实地的女性加入币安，我们会为你提供一个公平透明的职场环境。

— Yi He (@heyibinance) November 11, 2026

She cited repeated incidents of employees of Binance who have been sharing their photos with sexual rumors and young women who have been working for projects of the BNB ecosystem and cryptocurrency influencers.

Yi He also stated that female traders at rival companies have also been targeted in similar attacks, beyond Binance.

Her most explicit response was that Binance’s legal side would cover those female staff people who are impacted by claims like this. The statement failed to name any individuals or alleges a lawsuit wouldn’t materialise but said which courts may be involved.

Read More: Binance, Deribit Kill SignalPlus API Keys After $82K Social Engineering Breach

Rumors Have Spread Beyond Binance Staff

According to Yi He, the issue has resulted in a cross-chain effect in the crypto industry.

She stated that despite rumours that incidentally target her position within Binance, some of the female Binance workers have still been active with varying users. She also highlighted women involved in ecosystem-oriented initiatives and business stakeholders who became embroiled in speculations.

She personally had suffered with false accusations when they claimed information about her according to Yi He. But her concern was more about employees whose families and friends might end up facing those allegations online and in the media again and again.

Binance Co-CEO Links the Issue to Workplace Bias

Yi He tied the assaults to larger issues of limitations on women in working places.

She said work is not equal and that when they do get to senior leadership positions, there are additional challenges for women, such as hiring bias and harassment.

If the professional’s performance is assessed without taking into account the gender factor, it is done right by equality, says Yi He.

Yi He is currently listed as a co-CEO and co-founder of Binance, having different responsibilities in the key operational sectors of human resources, marketing communication and customer support.

Her new remarks, then, have an internal office dimension as well as an industry-wide: Binance is claiming that allegations of sexual harassment made against its workers may get treated as a authorized case, as opposed to simply web-based criticism.

Yi He also called for women entrepreneurs to enter Binance in a bid to offer the firm a fair and equitable workplace environment.

summary:

London's trading industry is coming home!

content:
2026-11-12T18:03:10.533+02:00

Thursday, 12/11/2026 | 16:03 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • The firm recently expanded its retail business through Slay Markets and a clearing deal with NinjaTrader.
  • The company, founded in 2024, says it has “paid out more than $440 million to users”.

Tradeify, a US-based futures proprietary trading firm, has signed a multi-year partnership with Inter Miami CF, becoming the football club’s Official Trading Partner.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The agreement follows Tradeify's expansion into retail brokerage, when it launched Slay Markets. The firm established Tradeify Brokerage LLC, a registered introducing broker with the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission and a member of the National Futures Association . It also signed a clearing and technology agreement with NinjaTrader.

Tradeify Adds Fan Activities to Inter Miami Deal

The partnership will include fan-focused activities, content and promotional campaigns. Tradeify will also develop trading challenges for its users, while Inter Miami CF supporters will have access to competitions and other experiences.

Founded in 2024, Tradeify is headquartered in Boca Raton, Florida. The firm said it has “paid out more than $440 million to users” since its launch.

It’s official. 🤝⚽ Tradeify is now the Official Trading Partner of @InterMiamiCF! Two brands. One shared ambition. The future looks exciting. 👀🔥 https://t.co/bjua8svKpJ

— Tradeify (@Tradeify) November 12, 2026

Tradeify Plans Trading Challenges and Fan Activities

The companies said the collaboration would draw on common themes between professional football and trading, including preparation, discipline and decision-making under pressure.

"Tradeify is a strong addition to our growing portfolio of global partners," said Euan Warren, Senior Vice President of Partnerships at Inter Miami CF.

Warren said the agreement would bring together two internationally focused brands through football and fan engagement.

Tradeify Seeks Greater International Exposure

Tradeify CEO Brett Simberkoff said Inter Miami CF's Freedom to Dream philosophy influenced the agreement. He also cited the shared focus on preparation and decision-making.

The deal gives Tradeify access to the club's international fanbase. Financial terms and the specific duration were not disclosed.

title: Bitcoin Core Discloses Tor and Mining Bugs: Who Was Affected and What Was Fixed?
summary: New Bitcoin Core advisories detail three flaws fixed in 2025. The key questions are which nodes were affected, which versions contain fixes and what users need to know.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

New Bitcoin Core advisories detail three flaws fixed in 2025. The key questions are which nodes were affected, which versions contain fixes and what users need to know.

Bitcoin Core developers have disclosed three previously patched security flaws, including a Tor-related permissions mistake that affected thousands of reachable nodes and a high-severity bug that could stop an affected mining node from building blocks until restarted.

The immediate takeaway is practical: operators need to know which software and configuration they run. The advisories describe weaknesses in node software, not evidence that Bitcoin’s supply rules failed or that private keys were stolen.

Bitcoin Core Tor bug crossed a trust boundary

The Tor security advisory explains how incoming Tor connections could inherit permissions intended for trusted computers. Tor traffic reached Bitcoin Core through a local service. If an operator’s whitelist included that service’s address, outside connections could receive the same exemptions as trusted local peers.

Those permissions relax some denial-of-service limits and privacy protections. The consequence was a mismatch between the operator’s intended trust boundary and the connections actually receiving that trust.

The developers said the configuration led to “thousands of reachable mainnet nodes whitelisting all incoming Tor connections.” That describes affected deployments identified in the disclosure; it is not a current census of nodes still running vulnerable software.

Nodes that never enabled the non-default whitelist setting were not affected by this issue. The advisory rates it medium severity and identifies fixes in Bitcoin Core 30.0, 29.2 and 28.3, released in October 2025. The detailed public disclosure followed on November 10, 2026.

A separate flaw could interrupt mining

The high-severity advisory concerns what happens to pending transactions after a chain reorganisation. A reorganisation occurs when a node switches to a competing valid chain with more accumulated work, and transactions from disconnected blocks may return to its pending pool.

Under particular conditions, affected software could restore dependent transactions inconsistently. A mining node could then assemble a candidate block containing transactions whose required inputs were missing. Its own validity checks would reject that candidate, preventing successful block-template creation until a restart restored a consistent pending pool.

This was a failure in an affected node’s ability to prepare a block, not a mechanism for making the wider network accept an invalid one. That distinction explains both the operational seriousness for a miner and the limit of the disclosure’s implications for ordinary holders.

Bitcoin Core rates the issue high severity. The affected versions were 28.0–28.2 and 29.0–29.1. The disclosure credits Niklas Goegge with finding and responsibly reporting it in September 2025. It does not report an attack exploiting the flaw.

The third advisory concerns delayed block processing

A third advisory describes a separate way a malicious peer could delay an affected node’s processing of new blocks. Its severity is medium, and fixes were released in Bitcoin Core 29.2 and 30.0.

The concern is availability: a computer may be running but failing to keep up with the network promptly. For a business relying on its own node, that can complicate transaction monitoring and the timely interpretation of confirmations even without changing the ownership of any coins.

The advisory identifies conditions under which disruption could be repeated. Operators should follow the developers’ published guidance and use maintained software, rather than assume that a visible connection to peers guarantees the node is processing the latest chain correctly.

Why disclose bugs after fixes have been available for a year?

The timing follows Bitcoin Core’s disclosure policy. For medium- and high-severity issues on the standard timetable, detailed disclosure normally comes two weeks after the last affected release reaches end of life. The November advisories identify October 27 as that milestone.

That approach gives operators time to upgrade before a fuller explanation becomes public. It also creates an important distinction for news readers: newly disclosed does not necessarily mean newly introduced or newly fixed. In this case, the repair dates are in October 2025.

The policy now makes a separate provision for easily discoverable vulnerabilities, including flaws that can be found with minimal effort using an AI model. Such issues can receive a patched release and advisory as soon as possible. The three November 10 disclosures followed the longer timetable.

What Bitcoin users should take from the disclosures

For node operators, the relevant questions are version, configuration and operational dependencies. A package supplied by another vendor may bundle Bitcoin Core with additional software and settings, so checking only the name of the application is insufficient. The Tor issue shows why default assumptions about trusted local connections deserve attention.

For holders using a hosted wallet or exchange, these advisories do not instruct them to move funds to a new address. Their service provider manages the underlying infrastructure. The appropriate distinction is between infrastructure maintenance and a wallet-key compromise; the published flaws concern the former.

The subject is also separate from the longer-term cryptographic risks discussed in BNC’s report on Bitcoin public-key exposure and quantum computing. A software patch addresses a specific implementation weakness. Planning for future quantum capabilities involves a different set of protocol and wallet decisions.

The disclosures reinforce a familiar but consequential point: decentralised money still depends on well-maintained software. Readers can take the bugs seriously without mistaking them for evidence that every Bitcoin node was affected, that funds were stolen, or that the network stopped enforcing valid blocks.

Nvidia Shares Plummet as Jensen Huang Resigns After 33 Years at the Helm of the Tech Giant
summary:
Nvidia announced Jensen Huang’s resignation as president, chief executive and board member on November 12, ending the co-founder’s 33-year leadership of the chipmaker. Finance chief Colette Kress takes over as interim CEO while retaining her CFO responsibilities. 
The board will consider internal an...
content:
2026-11-12T17:29:04.078+02:00

Thursday, 12/11/2026 | 15:29 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Nvidia’s shares are down 6.2% amid the leadership crisis.
  • CFO Colette Kress takes over as interim CEO while the board seeks a permanent successor.

Nvidia announced Jensen Huang’s resignation as president, chief executive and board member on November 12, ending the co-founder’s 33-year leadership of the chipmaker. Finance chief Colette Kress takes over as interim CEO while retaining her CFO responsibilities.

The board will consider internal and external candidates for the permanent role. It also appointed Harvey Jones, a former Synopsys CEO, as Nvidia’s first board chair. The company’s announcement did not state a reason for Jensen Huang’s resignation.

Nvidia Stock Tumbling Down

At the open, Nvidia shares tumbled to $159.91, the lowest level since June 2025. By the time of writing, the stock has partially recovered losses and returned to $163.36, though it is still down 6.2% from yesterday's close. Over the last five days, the stock has lost 15%, while its monthly losses exceeded 27%.

The sell-off had already begun before the announcement, with Reuters reporting sharp losses in extended trading amid reports of Huang’s possible departure.

Departure Follows Independent Investigation

Huang’s exit follows reports of a relationship with a woman suspected by US authorities of spying for China. Those allegations had increased pressure on the executive before the leadership change.

In a November 8 letter to employees, Huang acknowledged marital infidelity and pledged to cooperate with an investigation into national-security concerns. He did not identify the woman or admit disclosing confidential information.

That day, Nvidia’s board announced an independent investigation while expressing confidence in Huang and his management team. It said it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets had been compromised.

Four days later, Nvidia publicly announced his departure.

Earnings Are the Next Scheduled

Update Independent directors appointed former acting US Attorney Joon Kim and Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct the investigation on November 10.

For customers and partners, Jones said the board expects operations, customer commitments and the product roadmap to continue without interruption.

Nvidia’s next scheduled financial update remains November 17, when it will publish fiscal third-quarter results and hold its earnings call under the new interim leadership.

title: Anthropic’s Claude AI Blocks Pokémon Fan Games Over Copyright Concerns—What Changed?
summary: Anthropic’s Claude AI has begun rejecting requests to create Pokémon-related game assets, raising new questions for fan developers using generative tools to build unofficial projects.
content:
Skip to content

Anthropic’s Claude AI has begun rejecting requests to create Pokémon-related game assets, raising new questions for fan developers using generative tools to build unofficial projects.

The reported restrictions extend beyond recreating existing games. Claude has also refused requests involving recognizable Pokémon characters, sprites, artwork, and other franchise elements, affecting developers who have incorporated AI into their creative workflows.

Claude Won’t Generate Your Pokémon Slop For You Anymore

The restrictions came to wider attention after Big Kid Nation, the developer behind the unofficial game Pokémon Arena 2D, reported that Claude had started rejecting requests connected to its Pokémon fan project. The developer shared the issue on November 11, 2026, and subsequently showed examples of the AI refusing to work with Pokémon-related assets.

Reports indicate that Claude AI is refusing to generate Pokémon-related content, including fan art and game recreations. Source: AUTOMATON/X

In one reported exchange, Claude declined to use existing Pokémon sprites when helping build a new game. The refusal remained in place even after the developer asked whether moving the files to a different location would change the outcome. This suggests that the restriction is concerned with the content itself rather than simply where the assets are stored.

An examination of Claude’s coding instructions also revealed more specific restrictions covering intellectual property owned by existing game franchises. These include character names, character designs, artwork, music, stages, levels, and recognizable visual appearances.

The reported changes could affect developers who previously used AI tools to generate game code, modify sprites, create artwork, or assemble other elements for unofficial projects. Instead of receiving assistance with those tasks, users may now encounter refusals when their requests involve recognizable copyrighted material.

Big Kid Nation has expressed frustration with the development, particularly because of the time and financial resources invested in Pokémon Arena 2D. The developer described the project as a non-monetized effort, stating that substantial personal expenses had gone toward AI services and development.

The creator has also pushed back against criticism that the project relies entirely on automated production. In comments shared through the project’s Discord community, Big Kid Nation described its workflow as “almost exclusively vibe coded,” while acknowledging that a growing human team is involved.

The developer has reportedly spent up to $2,000 per month on project expenses and dedicated 10 to 14 hours daily to learning and development during much of the year. Big Kid Nation has also appealed to Nintendo to create the ambitious official Pokémon game that fans have been requesting, expressing a willingness to contribute to such an effort without payment.

Despite the new restrictions, the developer has not announced that Pokémon Arena 2D is being abandoned.

This Is Likely An Extension Of Claude’s Recent Video Game Update

The Pokémon-related refusals appear to follow a broader change Anthropic introduced to Claude Code in late October 2026. The earlier update focused on preventing the AI from helping users recreate specific existing video games, including projects presented under different names or described as original.

Anthropic’s Claude AI has begun blocking Pokémon-related content generation, including ROM hack assets, fan-game characters, sprites, and game recreations, citing intellectual property restrictions. Source: Retro Dodo/X

The revised instructions established a distinction between developing original games and reproducing another company’s existing intellectual property. Claude was directed to assist with original concepts, games built around general genres, and projects using designs and assets created by the user.

However, it was instructed not to build a recreation of a specific existing game, even when users attempted to rename the project or describe it as an original creation.

Anthropic technical staff member Addy Osmani acknowledged the change in a public post, explaining that the company wanted to steer Claude away from recreating another developer’s game. Osmani also stated that “using Claude to infringe IP is against our usage policy.”

The original restriction was not intended to prevent all AI-assisted game development. Instead, it addressed requests that could involve copying existing titles and their protected elements. Anthropic indicated that original game concepts and projects based on users’ own designs and assets would remain supported.

The subsequent Pokémon-related refusals suggest that the safeguards have become more specific. In addition to preventing direct game recreations, the reported instructions now identify individual elements that could constitute copying, including characters, artwork, names, music, and level designs.

The move highlights how Pokémon fan-game development has long faced copyright restrictions, with AI now closing a technical workaround that enabled unauthorized recreations. Source: Joseph/X

This distinction is important for fan developers. A project may introduce original gameplay mechanics or a different battle system while still relying on recognizable characters, logos, sprites, and other material from an established franchise. Changing the gameplay format does not automatically resolve intellectual-property concerns associated with those assets.

The developer behind Pokémon Arena 2D describes the project as a real-time arena battler in which players select moves for their creatures during battles. Its visual presentation uses a community-made Pokémon sprite collection, making the relationship between the game’s original mechanics and its use of established franchise assets particularly relevant to Claude’s restrictions.

Final Thoughts

For now, Pokémon Arena 2D remains scheduled for a December 2026 public beta, according to Big Kid Nation’s official website. The project is advertised as a free fan game, with players able to sign up for updates ahead of its public release.

Whether the development team can maintain that schedule while adjusting to Claude’s restrictions remains uncertain. The reported refusals may require changes to its AI-assisted workflow, particularly for tasks involving protected characters and artwork.

The development also highlights a broader challenge for generative AI companies. Tools that make coding, illustration, and game production more accessible must distinguish between helping users create original entertainment and reproducing material owned by established franchises. Anthropic’s latest restrictions show how those boundaries are increasingly being enforced within AI-assisted creative work.

  • Paysafe cut its full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook by 8% and adjusted EPS forecast by 24%.
  • A $203 million non-cash goodwill charge deepened the reported loss.

Paysafe lowered its full-year earnings outlook after third-quarter revenue growth failed to translate into stronger profitability. Adjusted EBITDA margin fell by roughly five percentage points, while operating cash flow more than halved.

The revised forecast cuts expected adjusted EBITDA by about 8% and adjusted earnings per share by 24%, measured at the midpoints of the previous and new ranges.

MetricQ3 2026Q3 2025
Revenue$439.6m$433.8m
Adjusted EBITDA$105.7m$126.6m
Adjusted EBITDA margin*24.0%29.2%
Operating cash flow$30.3m$69.2m

Margin calculated from reported figures. Source: Paysafe’s quarterly results.

Paysafe attributed the EBITDA decline to business mix, continued investment and severance costs. Its Digital Wallets business also faced market softness and regulatory pressure in areas including cryptocurrency and financial trading.

Goodwill Write-Down Deepens Reported Loss

The company reported a net loss of $247.5 million, including a $203.3 million non-cash goodwill impairment. The write-down widened the accounting loss but did not consume cash and was excluded from adjusted EBITDA.

The cash-flow deterioration was caused by lower adjusted EBITDA, refinancing fees and working-capital outflows linked to the timing of receivables, according to the results.

Refinancing Extends Maturities at a Higher Cost

Paysafe’s August refinancing gave it more time to repay part of its borrowings. Replacement dollar and euro term loans mature in June 2030, while the new revolving credit facility runs to August 2031. At the time, management described the transaction as extending debt maturities and supporting investment and deleveraging.

However, higher effective rates following the transaction increased third-quarter interest expense by $7.5 million year on year, adding pressure on adjusted earnings.

Full-year 2026 guidancePreviousRevised
Revenue$1,790m–$1,830m$1,761m–$1,771m
Adjusted EBITDA$449m–$464m$415m–$422m
Adjusted EPS$1.90–$2.03$1.45–$1.54

The previous EPS forecast already incorporated the refinancing’s effect on interest expense. November’s reduction therefore represents a further downgrade to an earnings outlook that had already been revised for the higher financing cost.

  • Tickmill wins Global Most Established Broker 2026 at the Finance Magnates Awards, recognising its established position and continued presence in the online brokerage industry.

Tickmill, an international multi-asset broker, has been named Global Most Established Broker 2026 at the Finance Magnates Awards 2026, held on 6 November in Limassol, Cyprus.

The recognition highlights the broker's established presence in the online trading industry and its continued commitment to providing trading services across multiple asset classes.

Tickmill: An Established Presence in Online Brokerage

Founded in 2014, Tickmill is a multi-regulated, multi-asset broker offering access to financial markets through a range of trading products and services. Its offering covers forex, stock indices, commodities, stocks and cryptocurrencies, with trading available through MetaTrader 4 and MetaTrader 5.

The company has built its brokerage operations around competitive trading conditions, efficient order execution and access to established trading platforms. It also provides educational resources, including webinars, seminars and video tutorials, to support traders in developing their market knowledge.

Alongside its trading services, Tickmill operates through entities subject to different regulatory frameworks, supporting its activities across international markets.

With a focus on maintaining its trading infrastructure and developing its services, Tickmill continues to strengthen its position in the online brokerage sector.

A Celebration of Innovation and Industry Success

The Finance Magnates Awards celebrate the companies and individuals contributing to progress across the financial services sector, with categories covering online trading, fintech, payments and brokerage technology.

Bringing together participants from across the industry, the annual awards provide an opportunity to acknowledge notable contributions and developments in financial markets.

title: MAM/PAMM VS trademakers
summary:
A trading strategy can attract attention through its performance. Building an investment business around that strategy requires considerably more: reliable administration, effective risk oversight, investor onboarding, clear reporting and access to suitable trading infrastructure.
For managers, thes...
content:
A trading strategy can attract attention through its performance. Building an investment business around that strategy requires considerably more: reliable administration, effective risk oversight, investor onboarding, clear reporting and access to suitable trading infrastructure.

For managers, these demands can consume resources that would otherwise support trading and business development. For family offices, high-net-worth investors and professional asset allocators, the quality of that infrastructure can be as important as the strategy itself.

MAM and PAMM arrangements have long helped connect managers with investor capital. trademakers builds on that need with a broader proposition: an integrated environment bringing strategy access, administration, reporting and manager support together.

The comparison therefore extends beyond how trades or profits are allocated. It concerns how effectively a manager can turn a trading operation into an accessible, professionally administered investment offering.

From allocation to investment infrastructure

Multi-Account Manager (MAM) and Percentage Allocation Management Module (PAMM) arrangements generally enable managers to trade across investor accounts or allocate trading results according to agreed rules. Their precise mechanics vary by provider and structure.

Both can be effective. A well-supported MAM or PAMM arrangement may meet a manager’s requirements, particularly where other operational services are already in place. However, allocation technology alone does not necessarily provide strategy evaluation, investor administration, marketing support or consistent performance reporting.

trademakers addresses these wider requirements within one platform. Its proposition combines the practical infrastructure managers need with the information investors require to evaluate their strategies.

Importantly, the trademakers structure is more of a fund-like investment wrapper rather than a fund. Investors participate through a “TM” representing an underlying strategy, with the applicable contractual arrangements defining their investment.

A lower barrier to building a management business

Launching a strategy should not require a manager to recreate an entire operational organisation.

Depending on the individual arrangement, trademakers can provide setup without an upfront charge, together with administration, a dedicated strategy webpage and reporting. Commercial terms are agreed case by case, allowing the service to reflect the manager’s requirements rather than imposing an identical arrangement on every strategy.

The distinction matters: a no-cost setup does not mean that trading or investing carries no charges. Managers and investors should understand the applicable fees within their agreements.

Relatively low initial AUM requirements also create a practical route for emerging managers. A credible trading approach may be ready for professional presentation before its manager has accumulated the assets or resources needed to justify a standalone fund structure.

Established managers can benefit too. Consolidating operational services can free their teams to concentrate on investment decisions, risk control and investor relationships. trademakers’ manager offering emphasises automated processes, client management and support with launching strategies.

Administration, onboarding and market access

Behind every allocation sits a series of operational tasks: onboarding investors, processing subscriptions and redemptions, maintaining records, calculating allocations and producing reports.

trademakers’ asset administration and reporting system brings these activities into a coordinated environment. Managers gain a clearer view of their business, while investors receive information through an established reporting process.

The wider service encompasses onboarding, custody arrangements and direct access to global financial markets through the relevant providers. Instruments and services available depend on the agreed setup and applicable restrictions.

Sterling Gent Trading Ltd, owns and operates trademakers and is the legal counterparty and custodian of client funds. These responsibilities are important when assessing the complete investment arrangement.

Experience beyond the trading screen

Technology becomes more useful when supported by people who understand the business it serves.

The team at trademakers includes professionals with individual careers spanning three to four decades or more across hedge funds, trading desks, proprietary trading, analysis, fund administration and marketing.

That combination brings several perspectives to a manager’s development. Trading expertise helps assess how a strategy operates; administrative experience addresses practical implementation; and marketing knowledge helps communicate the investment proposition clearly.

With representation in 10 countries, trademakers also brings an international network to its work with managers and investors. For a manager seeking to develop a broader business, access to experienced guidance can be particularly valuable when moving beyond an existing circle of clients.

Private or public: a choice shaped by the manager

Managers have different ambitions for distribution. Some want to serve an established investor group discreetly. Others want their strategy to reach a wider audience.

trademakers Private provides a controlled environment accessible to a manager’s introduced clients. This can suit relationship-led businesses, family office connections and managers who value exclusivity over public visibility.

trademakers Public offers broader exposure to eligible investors using the platform. A public profile can help a manager present the strategy, its performance and its characteristics in a consistent format.

The commercial potential differs accordingly. Private arrangements support focused relationship development; public presentation creates opportunities for discovery by investors beyond the manager’s existing network.

Neither route guarantees allocations. The appropriate choice depends on the manager’s objectives, capacity, investor relationships and distribution requirements.

Risk management at the centre

Attractive returns start a conversation. Understanding the risks behind them determines whether that conversation should become an allocation.

trademakers places strategy evaluation and manager assessment at the centre of its proposition. The objective is to understand the approach behind the performance and how the manager controls exposure when conditions become difficult.

For an allocator, meaningful questions extend beyond cumulative returns. How deep have drawdowns been? How quickly have losses developed? What role does leverage play? Can the strategy continue operating effectively as assets grow?

Strategies with similar returns can have substantially different risk characteristics. Clear assessment and ongoing monitoring help investors distinguish between them and judge suitability within a wider portfolio.

trademakers uses JP Fund Services as its investment adviser and risk manager, with responsibility for due diligence on managers and strategies seeking to join the platform.

JP Fund Services is well positioned to provide investors with expert guidance in selecting suitable investment products, ensuring their portfolios are appropriately diversified and aligned with their individual risk profiles and investment objectives.

Live net results and usable data

Professional investors need performance information they can examine, compare and incorporate into their own analysis.

trademakers’ stated approach is to publish live net results, giving investors a record grounded in actual trading rather than presenting hypothetical outcomes as achieved performance. Net reporting also makes the treatment of applicable costs an essential part of understanding the figures.

The reporting proposition includes downloadable daily, weekly, monthly and yearly data. Different observation periods serve different purposes: annual figures provide perspective, while more frequent data can reveal drawdown patterns, variability and the path taken to achieve a return.

For family offices, HNW investors and asset allocators, this supports a more considered assessment of how a strategy might fit alongside existing investments.

Some strategies also have BDO verification of results. Any such verification should be assessed against the specific strategy, period and scope covered. It is distinct from a platform-wide endorsement or a guarantee of future performance; independent auditing is optional and strategy-specific.

A concierge service for managers

Even experienced traders can encounter unfamiliar demands when building an investment offering.

trademakers’ concierge approach provides hands-on support through setup, strategy presentation, administration and reporting. Managers can draw on practical assistance while developing the operational framework around their trading.

For smaller teams, this can fill an important resource gap. For established businesses, it offers a coordinated point of support as requirements develop.

The service is particularly relevant where investment expertise is already strong but internal operational capacity remains limited. Helping managers navigate those demands gives them more time to focus on their strategy and the discipline required to manage it.

A broader proposition for managed money

The choice between MAM/PAMM and trademakers ultimately depends on the services a manager needs and the standards investors expect.

MAM and PAMM arrangements can provide effective allocation mechanisms. trademakers brings a broader combination of administration, reporting, risk assessment, market access and manager support, with private and public routes to investor participation.

For managers seeking to build beyond a trading account, that combination offers a practical foundation for development. For investors, it provides a structured environment in which to examine specialist strategies and their live performance.

For more information contact Sterling Gent Trading to discuss how you can cooperate: Your strategy, its risks, the intended investor base and the infrastructure needed to support it.

title: XRP Ledger Lending Gains Votes—but Seven More Are Needed Before Launch Countdown
summary: XRP Ledger lending is gaining validator support, but approval is still pending. The proposed credit market shifts attention from collateral to underwriting.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XRP

XRP Ledger lending is gaining validator support, but approval is still pending. The proposed credit market shifts attention from collateral to underwriting.

XRP Ledger’s proposed lending system is gaining validator support, but the gap between a promising upgrade and a usable credit market remains significant. The lending amendment has 22 supporting votes against a current requirement of 29, while the vault technology it needs has 23.

The November 12 governance snapshot puts the project closer to approval than in mid-October. It also establishes an important limit on the excitement: lending has not activated, and its two-week approval countdown has not started.

XRP Ledger lending votes climb, but approval is pending

The independent XRPL Dashboard snapshot records 22 of 35 trusted validators supporting LendingProtocol and LendingProtocolV1_1, with 23 supporting SingleAssetVault. CoinDesk’s November 12 report put the earlier October 19 counts at 19 for lending and 21 for vaults.

That is progress, rather than a launch date. The lending proposals still need seven additional supporting votes on that validator set, and the vault amendment needs six. Counts can move in either direction before activation.

The network’s amendment documentation says: “Amendments must maintain two weeks of support from more than 80% of trusted validators to be enabled.” With 35 counted validators, strictly more than 80% means 29 votes. Reaching 28 would leave the proposals short.

The two-week rule prevents a brief burst of support from instantly changing the ledger. It also means that a forecast launch date cannot simply be calculated from today’s vote count. The required majority must first form and then persist.

What the lending system would actually do

The XLS-66 lending specification describes fixed-term loans funded through pooled assets. A broker would arrange credit for borrowers, with the ledger recording the loan and its payments. Borrowers would not need to post the on-chain collateral familiar from many existing crypto lending markets.

That changes where lenders must look for protection. The specification says the design “relies on off-chain underwriting and risk management.” Assessing a borrower’s ability to repay therefore remains a human and institutional task even when the agreement is recorded on a blockchain.

First-loss capital can absorb part of a default loss where provided, but it does not eliminate credit risk. A lender still needs to understand the broker, borrower selection, terms and available loss protection. A transparent record of a loan is valuable; it is not proof that the loan will be repaid.

For institutions, the attraction is the possibility of combining conventional credit assessment with ledger-based origination and servicing. That could reduce some coordination work without turning every borrower into an overcollateralised crypto trader. Whether it produces a commercially useful market will depend on the participants and the terms they offer.

Why the vault amendment matters

The separate single-asset vault specification sets out how depositors can pool one asset and receive shares representing their interest. Lending uses that pool as its source of funds, so approving the loan mechanism without the necessary vault infrastructure would not complete the system.

The vault concept separates the money pool from individual loans. That makes the relationship between deposits, outstanding credit and withdrawals important. Investors should examine how a particular product handles funds committed to loans rather than assuming a vault share is equivalent to immediately available cash.

These are product-design questions, not merely software questions. A ledger can enforce accounting rules while the underlying credit remains illiquid or subject to default. Higher promised returns would need to be assessed against those risks rather than treated as an automatic benefit of moving finance on-chain.

Developers are still refining the design

Work continues alongside the governance process. A public development proposal proposes another lending amendment, LendingProtocolV1_2, addressing transaction sequencing when a loan is opened. It remained an open development proposal when checked for this report, rather than an activated network feature.

That distinction matters because software proposals, released code and enabled amendments represent different stages. A feature can exist in public development without being available for live borrowing. Conversely, a patch to supporting code does not by itself authorise the full lending market to begin operating.

For readers following XRP as an investment, governance progress is a concrete development to monitor. It is more informative than a broad claim that institutional adoption is inevitable. It also supplies no reliable formula for translating a validator vote into a token-price target.

BNC’s coverage of David Schwartz’s personal XRP holdings concerns a separate question about an individual’s portfolio. Protocol adoption should be assessed through implementation and usage evidence rather than inferred from one holder’s buying or selling.

What would turn this into a stronger XRP catalyst?

The next meaningful milestones are a sustained validator majority, activation of the required amendments and actual lending activity. After launch, the quality of borrowers, performance of loans and treatment of defaults would offer a better test of the system than a headline deposit total alone.

The relationship to XRP demand will also need evidence. A credit platform can support ledger activity without every loan necessarily requiring a speculative purchase of XRP. Investors should distinguish network utility, the asset used in a particular vault and the economic benefit that eventually reaches token holders.

For now, the upgrade is an advancing proposal with visible numbers to track. Its strongest promise is a new credit mechanism. Its biggest unanswered question is whether participants can manage ordinary lending risk as carefully as developers manage the ledger rules.
