title: AVA Foundation and Travala Unveil AVA 3.0: A Travala-First Roadmap
summary: Singapore, Singapore, 12th November 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Singapore, Singapore, 12th November 2026, Chainwire

Singapore, Singapore, November 12th, 2026, Chainwire

AVA 3.0 puts Travala at the centre of AVA’s story, with new token-powered initiatives inbound for the real-world travel business.

The AVA Foundation and Travala, the Binance-backed crypto travel booking platform, today announced AVA 3.0, accompanied by a roadmap that reinforces AVA token utility on Travala. As the AVA token’s primary commercial application, Travala is the focus of the new plan, which builds on AVA 2.0 and emphasises real-world travel products, transparent buybacks, and measurable member value.

AVA 3.0 leads with existing products. The AVA Smart Program has more than 180,000 members, who lock AVA to save up to 13% on travel and receive other perks. Members can also pay for discounted travel with AVA and receive AVA rewards through the Travala AI Agent, which is live on BNB Chain in collaboration with Binance Pay.

Backing the program is a monthly buyback. Each month, the AVA Foundation buys back AVA to replenish member giveback rewards, and Travala matches it and locks its share in the AVA Strategic Reserve. The AVA Buyback Multiplier scales Travala’s match between 1x and 3x as AVA givebacks grow, with a total monthly buyback potential of up to 4x AVA givebacks. More bookings generate more givebacks, and more givebacks mean bigger buybacks.

To date, 5,604,414 AVA has been bought back by the Foundation, with 779,691.92 AVA (representing 1.1% of circulating supply) permanently locked in Travala’s AVA Strategic Reserve. 17.5% of AVA’s circulating supply is locked as the ecosystem targets a long-term goal of 30%.

Two launches are next. Increased AVA lock levels for new Smart members are expected in November, while existing members keep their current locks and can use the new Smart Boost feature to increase their AVA locks and potential rewards. AVA+ Partners follows, with the launch expected in Q1 2027. It will allow partner projects to lock AVA for their tokens to be accepted as payment on Travala.

The Foundation is exploring several further ideas for 2027 and beyond, including AI booking agents that recognise Smart membership tiers to apply membership benefits, curated travel specials available exclusively in AVA, and VIP travel concierge access based on AVA holdings.

“Through every market since we started, one thing has held true: AVA is at its best when it’s used,” said Juan Otero, Travala CEO and co-founder, and Steven Hipwell, Travala co-founder and AVA Foundation Lead Contributor. “AVA 3.0 isn’t about grand promises; it’s about evolving what already works.”

The AVA token and all existing memberships, locks, and rewards continue as normal. Partnerships beyond Travala will be assessed where they deliver clear commercial value.

Read the full AVA 3.0 Roadmap that details all upcoming launches and areas of exploration.

Disclaimer

This release contains information about current plans and areas of exploration. Each new product is announced as live only after it has been built and approved. Its mention is not a commitment to launch. Travala and the AVA Foundation are separate organisations with distinct responsibilities. This release is for information only and is not financial advice, or an offer, solicitation, or inducement to acquire, hold, or lock AVA. It is not directed at persons in the United Kingdom, the United Arab Emirates, or any jurisdiction where distribution would be unlawful. References to Travala are to TravelFront and its group companies. See the full AVA utility token disclaimer and the AVA MiCA white paper.

About the AVA Foundation

The AVA Foundation oversees the AVA token ecosystem, including the AVA Smart Program, AVA token, and Travel Tiger NFTs. The AVA token functions as the key to accessing the AVA Smart Program, which provides travel perks and other benefits to Travala customers, such as AVA payment discounts and AVA loyalty rewards. AVA tokenises the concept of loyalty reward programs using blockchain technology, bringing web3 to traditional loyalty models. For more information, visit: www.avafoundation.org.

About Travala

Founded in 2017 and now backed by industry giant Binance, Travala is the leading crypto-native travel booking service, offering 2,200,000+ properties across 230 countries, 600+ airlines, 50,000+ car rental locations, and 400,000+ activities globally. Travala is a champion of cryptocurrency adoption, accepting over 100 leading cryptocurrencies alongside traditional payment methods. For more information, visit: www.travala.com.

title: MSCI Removes Strategy From Indexes: What It Means for MSTR and Bitcoin
summary: MSCI’s index deletion creates a new financing test for Strategy. Here is what passive selling could mean for MSTR and future Bitcoin purchases.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC MSTR

MSCI’s index deletion creates a new financing test for Strategy. Here is what passive selling could mean for MSTR and future Bitcoin purchases.

MSCI is removing Strategy from its global equity indexes, giving Bitcoin investors a new question to confront: what happens to a major corporate buyer when some of the funds holding its shares have to leave?

The index provider’s November review lists Strategy A among deletions from the MSCI USA Index, effective after the close of business on November 30. The decision changes an important source of shareholder demand. It does not remove MSTR from Nasdaq or require Strategy to sell its Bitcoin.

MSCI Strategy removal has a firm effective date

The published review confirms the deletion and its timetable. That makes this a scheduled portfolio event rather than another round of speculation about whether digital asset treasury companies belong in equity benchmarks.

For funds mandated to replicate an index, membership matters regardless of the portfolio manager’s personal view of Bitcoin. Once a constituent leaves, a tracking portfolio normally adjusts its exposure to match. Other investors can still buy the stock, including funds using different benchmarks or discretionary mandates.

That distinction is crucial. An index exit removes one reason to own shares; it does not erase every reason. Nor does the announcement establish the price at which buyers and sellers will meet when portfolios rebalance.

Strategy disputes the case for exclusion

In its consultation response, Strategy said MSCI-linked funds held approximately 13 million shares, representing 3.1% of basic shares outstanding. The company argued that this was less than one day’s trading volume and called the proposal “misguided.”

Those figures describe Strategy’s consultation-era assessment, rather than a fresh measurement of every fund’s position on November 12. Holdings, prices and trading activity can change before implementation. They nevertheless give investors a more concrete starting point than treating every dollar of MSTR’s market value as exposed to compulsory selling.

The company also disputes the classification behind the decision. Its response argues that Bitcoin treasury activity constitutes an operating business. MSCI’s index eligibility decision and Strategy’s accounting position answer different questions: how a benchmark is constructed, and how a company describes its activities.

Why the Bitcoin buying model matters

The larger issue is the connection between share demand and financing. Strategy has raised capital through common stock, preferred securities and debt to support its Bitcoin strategy. Losing a group of benchmark-driven shareholders could make that capital-raising process less favourable if it contributes to a weaker share price.

Consider the economics without assuming an outcome. When investors pay a substantial premium for a company’s underlying assets, issuing new shares can raise more capital relative to the asset exposure represented by those shares. A smaller premium reduces that advantage. The calculation also depends on liabilities, financing terms and the security being issued.

This is why a company holding Bitcoin and a fund holding Bitcoin can produce very different investment results. Shareholders in the company also own its financing decisions, operating activities and corporate obligations. A change in how the equity is valued can matter even when the Bitcoin price is unchanged.

Strategy’s third-quarter results reported $21.23 billion of capital raised year to date as of October 25. That historical figure illustrates the scale of financing in the business; it should not be confused with proceeds guaranteed to remain available after the index decision.

BNC’s earlier report on Strategy’s Bitcoin purchases and preferred-share buybacks showed the competing uses of capital. The index removal adds another consideration to those allocation choices.

Why the impact on Bitcoin remains uncertain

The risks to MSTR and BTC are related, but they are not interchangeable. An investor selling Strategy shares transfers ownership of the company to another buyer. That transaction does not itself instruct Strategy to liquidate coins.

Markus Thielen, founder of 10x Research, told CoinDesk: “We don’t expect any spillover into Bitcoin itself.” His assessment is an analyst opinion, not assurance that market sentiment or future corporate purchases will be unaffected.

The more plausible transmission channel is indirect: weaker equity demand could influence financing terms, which could affect the pace or attractiveness of future purchases. Whether that happens depends on management’s response, other funding sources and investor appetite beyond MSCI-linked portfolios.

It would therefore be premature to equate an estimated amount of stock selling with the same amount of Bitcoin selling. They involve different assets, different decision-makers and potentially different dates. Forecasts built on other index providers also excluding Strategy require those additional decisions to occur.

What investors should watch before November 30

Three developments can make the consequences clearer: disclosures about the actual rebalancing exposure, changes in Strategy’s financing activity, and management’s capital-allocation decisions. Share-price weakness alone cannot identify how much selling came from index funds rather than discretionary investors.

The effective date also matters for interpreting headlines. MSCI announced the change in advance; implementation is scheduled for the November 30 close. Markets can respond before that date, and passive portfolios do not necessarily execute every adjustment in an identical way.

Strategy now faces a test of demand for its corporate Bitcoin model outside one major benchmark family. For BTC holders, the useful question is whether the decision changes the company’s future ability to buy, rather than assuming its existing coins must suddenly come onto the market.

title: Binance SAFU in Crypto Explained: Meaning, Origin, and How It Works
summary:
Binance SAFU (Secure Asset Fund for Users) is an emergency insurance fund established by Binance in July 2018. The fund was created as a means to reimburse victims of security
The post Binance SAFU in Crypto Explained: Meaning, Origin, and How It Works appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Binance SAFU (Secure Asset Fund for Users) is an emergency insurance fund established by Binance in July 2018. The fund was created as a means to reimburse victims of security breaches in the event of unforeseen incidents, such as hacks, security glitches, or system failures.

The benefits of Binance SAFU are increased security, peace of mind for Binance traders, and faster recovery during emergencies. Whether you’re a beginner or an experienced trader, the SAFU is an assurance that Binance will cover your losses if you qualify for reimbursement in case of technical or security glitches.

The Binance SAFU is offered by Binance Global Exchange, the largest cryptocurrency platform by trading volume. Binance offers a range of products for both beginners and advanced traders, including spot and futures trading, staking, crypto loans, and, of course, the SAFU. That said, this article will cover what SAFU means and how to protect your funds and stay SAFU in the crypto space.

  • What Does SAFU Meaning Stand for on Binance?
    • How Does SAFU Work on Binance?
    • What are the Benefits of SAFU?
    • What is the Origin and Purpose of SAFU in Crypto?
    • What Does “funds are SAFU” Mean?
  • How to Protect Your Funds and Stay SAFU in Crypto?
    • What Does Stay SAFU Mean in Crypto?
    • What is the Story Behind the SAFU Meme?

What Does SAFU Meaning Stand for on Binance?

SAFU on Binance stands for “Secure Asset Fund for Users.” It is an emergency insurance reserve established by Binance in July 2018 to protect users’ funds in the event of security glitches or losses resulting from hacks, attacks, or platform vulnerabilities. In simple terms, SAFU doesn’t stop the hack from happening; instead, it helps users recover if one does.

Binance allocates a percentage of trading fees (around 10%) to this fund, which is kept in separate wallets and used exclusively to cover user losses if needed. It is worth noting that Binance only uses this fund to cover losses incurred due to a laxity on their end, so if you give your sensitive information to someone, transfer funds to the wrong wallet, or lose money to market conditions, Binance SAFU will not cover your loss.

How Does SAFU Work on Binance?

SAFU on Binance works by 10% of users’ trading fees into a secure wallet as a dedicated reimbursement fund. So, for every time you trade on Binance, a portion of the trading fee (10%) is automatically deposited into the SAFU to cover losses in case of a security breach.

For example, when Binance experienced a significant hack in 2019 that resulted in the loss of over 7,000 BTC, the SAFU (Secure Asset Fund) was used to cover the losses without impacting users.

This reserve is held in secure, cold wallets, which are offline storage systems that are less vulnerable to hacking attempts than online hot or software wallets. Beyond the SAFU, Binance has an extensive FAQ centre and other means to educate users and ensure that the strong security practices complement the Secure Asset Fund’s protection.

Join Binance today and trade with peace of mind knowing your funds are SAFU.

What are the Benefits of SAFU?

The benefits of SAFU are listed below:

  • Additional Security: Aside from the security measures Binance implements and the account security features for individual traders, the Binance Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) provides an extra layer of protection as funds are stored in offline wallets, thereby reducing the risk of loss or theft.
  • Peace of Mind for Binance Traders: Binance users can have peace of mind knowing that their funds can be recovered in the event of unforeseen events or security glitches. Additionally, this commitment to providing a financial safety net for traders demonstrates the platform’s dedication to protecting users in the event of cyber attacks and technical vulnerabilities.
  • Offers Compensation: While the fund covers only specific losses, in the event of security breaches, the Secure Asset Fund for Users enables the platform to compensate traders affected by the incident. Fortunately, funds are added consistently to maintain a value of approximately $1 billion in USDC and ensure there is enough money to cover losses.

The cons of SAFU are listed below:

  • No Legal Guarantees for Payouts: Binance’s terms of service do not legally obligate the exchange to pay out from the Secure Asset Fund for Users. It is at Binance’s discretion whether and when to use the fund to compensate users, meaning users have no contractual assurance of reimbursement.
  • Not a Full Insurance: The Secure Asset Fund for Users is designed as a cybersecurity self-insurance and emergency reserve for users who lose their funds due to a security vulnerability on Binance’s end. It does not provide comprehensive coverage for all losses or serve as a safeguard against company-wide insolvency..

Despite SAFU, it is advisable to activate strong security practices, like Two Factor Authentication, anti-phishing codes, and withdrawal address whitelisting, as the fund cannot prevent all types of losses or scams.

What is the Origin and Purpose of SAFU in Crypto?

The term SAFU originated from Binance in 2018, following a system maintenance that threatened users’ funds. Binance’s CEO, Changpeng Zhao, tweeted, “Funds are safe,” repeatedly assuring the community that their funds were secure. Then, a YouTuber named Bizonacci later created a parody video titled “Funds are SAFU,” poking fun at the situation by intentionally mispronouncing “safe” as “safu.”

The term caught on quickly within the crypto community due to its humorous yet reassuring tone. So, instead of ignoring the viral video and meme, the platform leaned into it. Shortly afterwards, Binance created the “Secure Asset Fund for Users” (SAFU), an insurance-like fund set up to protect users’ funds in extreme situations, such as major security breaches or system failures.

Register now and get fee discounts on every trade with Binance SAFU as backup.

What Does “funds are SAFU” Mean?

“Funds are SAFU” means that your money is safe and secure. The term “SAFU” originated from the cryptocurrency community and stands for “Secure Asset Fund for Users,” which is an emergency insurance fund that some platforms use to protect users’ assets in the event of hacks or losses. So when someone says “Funds are SAFU,” they mean your funds are protected and you don’t need to worry about losing them.

How to Protect Your Funds and Stay SAFU in Crypto?

Here are practical steps to protect your funds and stay SAFU in the crypto industry.

  1. Choose a Reputable Exchange: Selecting a trustworthy exchange is fundamental. Platforms with proven security protocols minimize the risks of hacks or fraud. Binance is a top choice for many traders worldwide due to its robust security features and extensive range of services. Check out this comprehensive Binance review to get a clear picture of what Binance offers and how it safeguards users’ assets.
  2. Enable All Security Features: Setting up two-factor authentication, withdrawal whitelist, and other security layers is vital. These extra steps prevent unauthorized access even if login details are compromised. Securing your account with these measures reduces the chances of losing funds due to cyber threats.
  3. Use Verified Referral Links: When signing up for exchanges or services, ensure you use verified referral links from trustworthy sources. This helps avoid phishing attempts and ensures you’re interacting with the official platform. This Binance referral code covers all the necessary details you need to unlock new user rewards safely on ht exchange.
  4. Keep Private Keys and Recovery Phrases Offline: Never share your private keys or recovery phrases. Storing them offline, such as in a secure physical location or hardware wallet, adds a strong layer of protection against hacks and scams. Access to these keys means access to your funds, so safeguarding them is paramount.
  5. Stay Informed About Scams and Phishing Attempts: Scammers continuously find new ways to trick users into revealing sensitive information. Educate yourself on common crypto scams and be cautious about unsolicited messages or offers. Binance will never ask for passwords or private keys.
  6. Regularly Review Account Activity: Monitoring your Binance account and wallet activity helps spot suspicious behaviour early. If you notice any unauthorized transactions, take immediate action by contacting support and securing your accounts.

Claim your $100 welcome bonus on Binance today with SAFU as your safety net.

What Does Stay SAFU Mean in Crypto?

“Stay SAFU” in crypto means to stay safe and protect your assets. The phrase became popular after Binance’s CEO assured users their funds were secure during a hack. Today, it reminds crypto users to double-check addresses, use trusted wallets, keep their recovery phrases secure, and remain vigilant at all times.

What is the Story Behind the SAFU Meme?

The story behind the SAFU viral meme originated from Binance Exchange. In 2018, during an unscheduled maintenance, Binance’s CEO, Changpeng Zhao (CZ), tweeted “Funds are safe” to reassure users. Shortly after, a YouTuber named Bizonacci uploaded a parody video where he used the voice of Binance’s CEO, CZ (Changpeng Zhao), saying: “Funds are safu.” This was a mispronunciation of “safe”, which sounded funny and quickly spread in the crypto community.

title: David Schwartz Reveals Massive XRP Sell-Off—Transparency or Warning?
summary: David Schwartz, the co-creator of the XRP Ledger and Ripple's former chief technology officer, has revealed that he sold nearly all his cryptocurrency holdings, reducing his XRP position by approximately 88%.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XRP

David Schwartz, the co-creator of the XRP Ledger and Ripple's former chief technology officer, has revealed that he sold nearly all his cryptocurrency holdings, reducing his XRP position by approximately 88%.

His disclosure has sparked discussion across the XRP community, particularly as the token trades near $1.05 amid an extended market downturn. However, Schwartz attributes his decision to personal risk aversion rather than concerns about XRP’s fundamentals or long-term prospects.

David Schwartz Reveals He Sold 23 Million XRP

Schwartz, who posts under the username JoelKatz on X, disclosed that his XRP holdings have fallen from approximately 26 million tokens to just 2–3 million. The reduction represents a substantial change in his personal exposure to the cryptocurrency he helped develop.

David Schwartz reiterated that he has never concealed his crypto sell-off, responding to a Chainlink advocate who referenced his earlier disclosure of selling most of his digital assets. Source: @JoelKatz/X

His sales extended beyond XRP. Schwartz also reduced his Bitcoin holdings from approximately 1,500 BTC to just one Bitcoin, while his Ethereum position declined from around 40,000 ETH to only six.

The former Ripple CTO explained that he has not purchased XRP in a long time because of his discomfort with investment risk. He has previously indicated that his remaining exposure to Ripple stock is already greater than what he considers comfortable.

Schwartz also revealed that he sold approximately 2.5 million XRP in 2025, resulting in a capital gains tax bill of around $1.7 million. The transaction illustrates the scale of his previous holdings and the financial implications of reducing his cryptocurrency exposure.

Despite the extensive sales, Schwartz has retained millions of XRP tokens. His decision therefore represents a significant reduction rather than a complete departure from the digital asset.

Why Did Ripple’s Former CTO Sell Most of His Crypto?

Schwartz has consistently pointed to personal risk tolerance as the primary reason behind his decisions. His explanation suggests that the reduction reflects his approach to managing wealth rather than a specific judgment about XRP’s future performance.

David Schwartz said he has not purchased XRP in years due to his strong aversion to financial risk, following the sale of nearly all his cryptocurrency holdings. Source: @JoelKatz/X

His remaining Ripple stock exposure is another important factor. Although he has sold most of his digital assets, his continued ownership of Ripple shares leaves him with substantial exposure to the company’s business.

Holding both Ripple equity and XRP could concentrate his financial exposure within the same broader ecosystem. Reducing his cryptocurrency holdings allows him to limit that concentration while maintaining an ownership interest in the company.

His comments also highlight a distinction between technological involvement and investment strategy. Being one of the architects of the XRP Ledger does not necessarily mean that Schwartz wants to maintain a large personal position in XRP.

Importantly, he has not presented his sales as a warning about the cryptocurrency’s fundamentals, payment utility, or long-term development. His explanation has centered on his own financial comfort level.

XRP Community Questions the Sell-Off

Schwartz’s disclosure has drawn questions from community members who believe XRP’s potential utility could justify maintaining greater exposure to the asset.

One commenter, @kevin_myles, challenged the emphasis on risk by pointing to XRP’s expected role in financial transactions and cross-border payments.

XRP supporters challenged Schwartz’s risk concerns, arguing that the token’s anticipated utility and higher prices could improve liquidity and reduce transaction slippage. Source: Kevin Myles/X

The discussion also raised an argument about the relationship between XRP’s market price and its payment efficiency. Higher XRP prices can support greater liquidity and potentially reduce slippage costs when large transactions are executed.

This argument reflects an important aspect of XRP’s intended use within the Ripple ecosystem. The digital asset is designed to facilitate value transfers, with on-demand liquidity allowing financial institutions and payment providers to move funds without maintaining pre-funded accounts in multiple currencies.

However, potential utility does not eliminate investment risk. XRP remains a publicly traded digital asset whose market price can fluctuate considerably, regardless of its underlying payment applications.

The exchange highlights two different ways of evaluating the cryptocurrency. Supporters often focus on its potential role in financial infrastructure, while investors must also consider volatility, liquidity conditions, market demand, and portfolio concentration.

Schwartz’s decision illustrates that distinction. Even someone closely associated with XRP’s development can choose to limit personal exposure despite remaining involved with Ripple.

XRP Price Faces Continued Selling Pressure Near $1.05

Schwartz’s disclosure comes as XRP struggles to recover from a prolonged decline. As of November 12, 2026, XRP/USD is trading near $1.05, with recent sessions largely confined to a narrow range between approximately $1.04 and $1.08.

The cryptocurrency has lost roughly 13% to 20% over the past week, depending on the reference point, while its monthly decline stands near 23% to 25%. XRP is also down more than 55% compared with levels around $2.39 a year earlier.

Its market capitalization currently stands near $66 billion to $67 billion, with approximately 63.5 billion tokens in circulation. Daily trading volume remains substantial at around $1.5 billion, indicating continued market activity despite the downward price trend.

The broader technical picture remains bearish. Aggregated daily indicators lean toward Sell, with moving averages showing particularly strong downward momentum. Shorter timeframes, including the hourly and four-hour charts, also indicate continued selling pressure.

These market conditions provide additional context for the discussion surrounding Schwartz’s disclosure. However, there is no direct evidence that his personal decision to sell cryptocurrency is connected to XRP’s recent price decline.

XRP Technical Analysis: Oversold Conditions Meet Bearish Trend

XRP’s daily moving averages indicate that the prevailing downtrend remains intact. The token is trading below several important averages, suggesting that sellers continue to control the broader market structure.

The 10-day simple moving average (SMA) is positioned around $1.15–$1.17, while the 20-day SMA sits near $1.21–$1.23. The 50-day SMA is approximately $1.34–$1.35.

XRP price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Longer-term moving averages also remain above the current price. This positioning reinforces the bearish outlook and indicates that XRP would need a sustained recovery to begin reversing its downward trend.

Momentum indicators, however, present a different picture.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is hovering around 23.4–23.7 on the daily chart, placing XRP deep in oversold territory. The Stochastic %K is also near 6–7, while the Williams Percent Range is around -94.

These readings suggest that selling pressure has become particularly intense. Historically, deeply oversold conditions can precede short-term relief rallies as bearish momentum begins to weaken.

Nevertheless, oversold conditions do not guarantee an immediate recovery. The Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) remains negative, while other momentum indicators continue to reflect weakness.

The Average Directional Index (ADX), around 24–25, also suggests a moderately established trend, with directional indicators favoring the downside.

Key XRP Support and Resistance Levels

The $1.03–$1.05 region represents an important immediate support area. XRP has recently traded around this zone, making it a key level to watch during the ongoing correction.

A sustained break below this support could expose the psychological $1.00 level, potentially opening the door to further losses if selling pressure accelerates.

On the upside, the first resistance cluster lies between $1.07 and $1.09. A recovery above this region could bring the $1.12–$1.15 range into focus.

However, a stronger reversal would require XRP to reclaim its shorter-term moving averages and establish sustained buying pressure.

For now, the technical structure remains bearish despite the possibility of a temporary bounce from oversold conditions.

Transparency or Warning? What Schwartz’s Disclosure Means for XRP

Schwartz’s decision to reduce his XRP holdings raises questions about how even prominent figures in the cryptocurrency industry approach personal investment risk. His sales are particularly notable given his role in creating the XRP Ledger and his continued financial connection to Ripple.

However, interpreting the disclosure as a bearish signal for XRP would go beyond what he has actually stated. Schwartz has attributed his decisions to extreme risk aversion and his existing exposure to Ripple stock, not to a loss of confidence in the cryptocurrency’s underlying technology.

The community debate also highlights the difference between XRP’s potential utility and its performance as an investment. Greater adoption of cross-border payment infrastructure could support demand for the asset, but it does not guarantee price appreciation or protect holders from market volatility.

Meanwhile, XRP’s technical indicators point to continued weakness, although deeply oversold readings leave room for a short-term recovery.

Ultimately, Schwartz’s disclosure offers a rare look into how one of XRP’s key architects manages his personal wealth. Whether investors view it as transparency or a reason to reassess their own exposure, his explanation remains clear: the sell-off reflects his personal tolerance for risk rather than an explicit warning about XRP’s future.

title: What Is Binance Pay and How to Find Its ID?

Binance Pay is a contactless, secure, and borderless means of sending and receiving crypto payments within the Binance platform. You can pay, receive, and send crypto with no fees at
The post What Is Binance Pay and How to Find Its ID? appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Binance Pay is a contactless, secure, and borderless means of sending and receiving crypto payments within the Binance platform. You can pay, receive, and send crypto with no fees at all, straight from your Binance account. You don’t have to copy lengthy wallet addresses or concern yourself with selecting the correct blockchain network. It all takes place within the Binance app, so crypto transfers are fast and hassle-free.

The benefits of using Binance Pay are simple. It is free to use, with no network fees or gas fees. Transactions are instant, so you don’t have to wait for confirmations. It also works globally, which means you can send and receive crypto from people around the world who use Binance. Plus, it’s safe and backed by Binance’s security system.

This guide will explain what Binance Pay is, how it works, and provide a step-by-step guide on how to use Binance Pay. You’ll learn how to create a Binance account and how to send and receive crypto with Binance Pay.

  • What Is Binance Pay?
    • What Are the Pros and Cons of Binance Pay?
      • Who Can Use Binance Pay?
    • What Is Binance Pay Merchant?
      • What Are the Benefits of a Binance Merchant Account?
  • How Binance Pay Works?
    • What Are the Fees of Binance Pay?
    • Is Binance Pay Safe?
  • How to Use Binance Pay?
    • How to Register a New Account on Binance to Use Binance Pay?
    • How to Send and Receive Crypto With Binance Pay?
      • Can You Pay Someone on Binance?
    • What Is Binance Pay ID?
      • Where to Find Binance Pay ID?
      • Is Binance Pay Legal in India?

What Is Binance Pay?

Binance Pay is a feature that allows you to send and receive crypto instantly and free of charge. You can use it to pay your friends, send money to relatives, or accept payments for your business. It is very easy to use and operates within the Binance app. Binance Pay accepts more than 100 cryptocurrencies for payments, and you can make payments using coins such as Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT, USDC, and BNB. Also, you can select which coin you wish to use first when you are making a payment. Binance Pay also works as a Binance payment gateway that helps businesses accept crypto payments easily.

Currently, Binance Pay has more than 40 million active users, and most of the individuals use it to spend their cryptocurrency at tens of thousands of stores, both online and offline. You can use it to shop, pay for food, book travel, and more. It also works well for sending money across countries, and even it is much faster than a bank transfer and has zero fees.

To use it, first, you require a Binance account, and after logging in, proceed to the Binance Pay option on the app. You can send cryptocurrency by using an individual’s Pay ID, phone number, or email. You can also scan their QR code, and the cryptocurrency will be sent to their Pay wallet immediately.

Start using Binance Pay today to send and receive crypto instantly, securely, and with zero fees – no wallet addresses or networks needed, just smooth and easy payments.

What Are the Pros and Cons of Binance Pay?

Pros of Binance Pay

The pros of using Binance Pay are easy to use, low fees, global transactions, secure payments, and flexible payment features.

  • Easy to Use: Binance Pay makes it easy for you to send or receive cryptocurrency with only a couple of taps on your phone. You can quickly pay merchants or share bills with your friends. It supports more than 100 cryptocurrencies, and that means you have lots of cryptocurrency alternatives.
  • Low or No Charges: The majority of Binance Pay transactions are completely free, and that’s great for keeping costs down. But, for larger transactions, above 140,000 USDT, you need to pay 1 USDT. That’s really not expensive compared to using old-style payment methods. You can also view all the charges before finalizing the transaction.
  • Global Reach: You can send crypto anywhere in the world instantly and with low fees. International transfers from traditional banks take days or even weeks. Binance Pay does it instantly, and it’s best for paying friends or shopping around the world.
  • Secure Payments: Binance Pay has robust security features, such as two-factor authentication and encryption. This protects your funds and information. Also, Binance has a good history of safeguarding users. You can rely on it for daily payments.
  • Flexible Features: You can easily modify the way you spend your crypto or even send crypto gift boxes. It is also capable of mobile top-ups and peer-to-peer transfers.

Cons of Binance Pay

The cons of using Binance Pay are mandatory KYC verification, limited acceptance by merchants, customer support delays, and regulatory risks.

  • Requires KYC Verification: You need to go through extra Binance Know Your Customer procedures to use it. You have to provide personal information, such as your ID and address. Some find this restrictive on privacy grounds.
  • Limited Acceptance by Merchants: Few retailers currently accept Binance Pay. You can use it on Binance’s Marketplace, but there is limited choice. Of course, adoption is increasing, but it’s not quite there yet.
  • Customer Support Problems: Binance’s customer service is not always good. When you encounter issues, such as a failed transaction, it may take some time before you can receive assistance. It can be irritating when you urgently need fixes to be done immediately.
  • Regulatory Risks: As you know, crypto payments are subject to uncertain regulations in certain nations. Binance has experienced legal troubles previously that may influence Binance Pay. So, this creates some risk when using it for the long term.

Who Can Use Binance Pay?

You can use Binance Pay if you want to send payments, a shopper or traveler, a business wishing to accept crypto, an individual who wishes to send gifts, or wishes to handle automated subscriptions.

  • People who want to send payments: Any person with a verified Binance account can easily send crypto to friends or relatives around the globe. All you need is the recipient’s Binance ID, email address, or phone number, or you can scan their QR code too. It’s quick, often free, and supports more than 100 cryptocurrencies.
  • Shoppers and travelers: Binance Pay allows you to purchase items or book travel with cryptocurrency at thousands of online and offline retailers. Here, you can pay for clothes, electronics, or even hotel nights on websites like Travala. It supports more than 100 different cryptocurrencies, so you have many options. So, it’s great for anyone who wants to spend crypto as easily as cash.
  • Businesses wishing to accept crypto: Merchants can accept payments in crypto from users on Binance. They must apply for a merchant account with Binance Pay. They can also process payments and refunds via the Merchant Management Platform.
  • People who want to send gifts: You can use the Binance Pay Red Packet function to send cryptocurrency gifts. You have to select the token, value, and number of recipients. The recipient will receive a random amount until all funds are claimed.
  • People who want to handle subscriptions: Binance Pay supports recurring payments. This is very helpful for individuals who wish to manage subscriptions or pay regularly. You can easily approve repeated payments to merchants.

What Is Binance Pay Merchant?

A Binance Pay merchant is a business or individual who accepts crypto payments from customers using Binance Pay. It is easy to do. You simply need to register, get verified, and use tools such as QR codes or payment links to receive payments. 

Simply, customers have to scan or click to pay with cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin or USDT instantly. You can use stablecoins such as USDT to prevent crypto price fluctuations. It also supports all types of businesses, such as stores, cafes, or online platforms. You can manage everything via the Merchant Management Platform, including monitoring payments, handling refunds, and withdrawing funds.

What Are the Benefits of a Binance Merchant Account?

The benefits of a Binance Merchant Account are low transaction fees, access to a huge customer base, fast and secure payments, and easy setup and management. 

  • Low or No Transaction Fees: You can create a free Binance Merchant Account, and you will also often pay little to no fees for crypto transactions. This is better compared to traditional payment methods like credit cards, which nowadays charge very high fees. It also helps small businesses save money, and you can keep more of your profits. Plus, payments settle instantly, which is great for cash flow as a business.
  • Access to a Huge Customer Base: Binance has over 250 million users worldwide on its centralized crypto exchange, and there are 40 million active Binance Pay users. As a merchant, you can tap into this massive audience and take your chance to attract crypto fans who prefer paying with Bitcoin or USDT. This can boost your sales, and you can reach customers globally without dealing with currency exchange hassles.
  • Fast and Secure Payments: Crypto payments through Binance Pay are quick and safe. Transactions happen instantly, so you don’t have to wait days for your funds. The best part, the blockchain technology keeps things secure and reduces fraud risks. 
  • Easy Setup and Management: Setting up a Binance Merchant Account is super simple. You just need to sign up, get verified, and start accepting payments fast. The Merchant Management Platform also lets you track payments, issue refunds, and withdraw funds easily. You can even integrate it with your website or app without much technical knowledge. Hence, it’s user-friendly even for small businesses.

Try Binance Pay now and enjoy fast, fee-free crypto transfers worldwide – perfect for paying friends, shopping online, or accepting payments with just a tap.

How Binance Pay Works?

Binance Pay works as a contactless and safe method for paying and receiving crypto. It enables you to make payments or transfer currencies without sharing personal information. It is developed within the Binance app itself, therefore, you don’t have to install anything additional apps or extensions.

Here’s how it works. Firstly, you sign up for a Binance account. Next, you need to create your Binance Pay account. From there, you can send and receive crypto. To send, you simply need to use someone’s Binance Pay ID, phone number, email address, or QR code. The recipient will receive it instantly in their Binance Pay account.

Here, the platform is using internal transfers. So, when you transfer using Binance Pay, the transfer does not occur on the blockchain. It occurs within the Binance system. It is therefore instant and charges zero fees. Also, you don’t need to hold crypto in a different Pay wallet. The system will use the amount from your Binance exchange funding wallet.

What Are the Fees of Binance Pay?

Binance Pay is free of charge for individual transfers. It does not cost you any additional fee when you send cryptocurrency directly to an individual with the help of Binance Pay. There is no transaction fee for internal transfers on the platform. Receiving is free of charge as well. If someone pays you using crypto with the use of Binance Pay, you receive your full amount.

Now, there may be fees if you use other Binance Pay services. For instance, if you make a purchase from a vendor and the transaction entails currency conversion, Binance will implement its standard conversion spread. This is not an explicit fee, but the exchange rate you receive may differ slightly from the market rate. This is also called a spread fee.

For merchants, Binance introduced a rule where mini-program merchants need to hit a minimum transaction volume, or they’ll pay a quarterly fee. Also, Binance Payouts have a fee of 0.80% per transaction, capped at $5 or equivalent. All fees are shown upfront before you confirm a payment, so there are no surprises. Refunds, if they happen, go back to your Binance Pay Wallet in USDT.

Is Binance Pay Safe?

Yes, Binance Pay is safe as it is built on Binance Exchange’s secure system. It applies Binance’s robust security measures to safeguard your account and funds. First of all, the platform employs two-factor authentication (2FA). To access Binance Pay, you must enable it. This adds an extra layer of protection, requiring a code from your phone in combination with your password.

It also includes device management. This allows you to view the devices logged into your account. If you find an unknown device logged into your account, you can remove it to protect your account. The platform also uses anti-phishing codes. If you receive an email from Binance, the code is displayed in the email, ensuring you won’t receive a fraudulent email.

Binance Pay operates within the Binance environment. Therefore, it employs the same security tools as the rest of the Binance exchange. These tools include cold storage of user balances, risk monitoring, and smart internal controls.

Additionally, Binance Pay payments are internal transfers. They do not go onto public blockchains, which reduces the risk of external attacks. You also do not reveal your wallet address when making a payment. Binance monitors for suspicious activity using risk systems and artificial intelligence. If something seems wrong, your account is frozen to prevent fraud. Your personal information and payment details are also encrypted. You do not share either your payment history or your personal information with the other individual.

Send and receive crypto anytime, anywhere using Binance Pay – easy to use, no hidden fees, and fully integrated with your Binance wallet for fast payments.

How to Use Binance Pay?

To use Binance Pay, you need a verified Binance account. First, open your Binance app and log in. Tap on the “Pay” icon on the home screen. Now you can send or receive crypto with just a few taps. You can also scan another person’s Binance Pay QR code or share your own.

How to Register a New Account on Binance to Use Binance Pay?

To register a new Binance account, follow these three steps: sign up with your email or phone number, verify your identity (KYC), and activate Binance Pay.

Step 1: Sign Up with Your Email or Phone Number

Go to binance.com or download the Binance app from the App Store or Google Play Store. On the site, click the yellow “Sign Up” button at the top right. In the app, tap the icon at the bottom right and choose “Sign Up.” Enter your email or telephone number and use a secure password (blending letters, numbers, and characters for security). Here, you can also use our Binance referral code to get a $100 welcome bonus. Now, a confirmation code will be sent to your email or phone – check your messages or inbox and enter the code to confirm. This takes only a moment or two and sets up your account.

Join millions of users already using Binance Pay and make instant crypto payments with ease, skip the fees, and enjoy a smooth and secure transaction every time.

To secure your account, turn on 2FA immediately after you create an account. On the website, you must click your account icon and then “Settings.” You can use Google Authenticator, SMS, or email for 2FA. With Google Authenticator, you need to download the app, scan the QR code that Binance gives you, and save the backup key somewhere secure. With SMS or email, you receive codes on your phone or inbox for logins and transactions. It’s a five-minute step, but one that’s well worth it for peace of mind.

Step 2: Complete Identity Verification (KYC)

Binance requires identity verification for compliance purposes and to enable features like Binance Pay. On the website, click your profile icon and go to “Verification.” You will be required to upload an official government-issued document, such as a passport, driver’s license, or national identity card, and an address verification, for example, a bill or bank statement. 

Sometimes, Binance will request a selfie or a rapid face scan using the camera on your device. This is an easy procedure, and Binance will likely have it processed within a few minutes, but it may take a couple of days when it’s during peak hours. This step secures your account and prepares it for most features on Binance Pay.

Step 3: Activate Binance Pay

After your account has been verified, enable Binance Pay. Go to “More” in the primary menu and choose “Pay”. Pick a special nickname for anonymity (like “CryptoNinja” instead of your actual name) and enter a six-digit Pay PIN for secure payments. 

Accept the terms and conditions and click “Activate.” This connects your account to Binance Pay, and you can start sending and receiving crypto immediately. The entire process takes only a minute or two, and you’re live.

How to Send and Receive Crypto With Binance Pay?

To send and receive crypto with Binance Pay, follow these steps: funding your wallet, sending crypto via QR code or contact details, and receiving crypto by sharing your QR code or Binance ID.

Step 1: Fund your Binance Wallet

Before sending cryptocurrency, confirm your Binance Funding Wallet has a balance. Click the “Wallets” icon at the top, then “Overview.” Alternatively, you can buy some if you don’t have cryptocurrency, using a bank transfer, credit card, or P2P trade. 

To purchase, click “Buy Crypto” on the landing page, select your fiat currency (e.g., USD or EUR), and pick a cryptocurrency like Bitcoin or USDT. Follow directions to finalize the purchase, which will take a few minutes. You can also move your cryptocurrency from another wallet or exchange to your Binance Funding Wallet by copying your wallet address (found under “Wallets” > “Overview” > “Deposit”). With funding, your cryptocurrency is now prepared for use through Binance Pay.

Step 2: Send Crypto through QR Code or Contact Information

Launch the Binance app and click the “Pay” icon on the home screen. Click “Send,” then pick how you send, either scan the recipient’s Binance QR code or enter the recipient’s details by email, mobile number, or Binance Pay ID. To scan using the QR code scanner, tap the scan icon on the home screen or long-press the icon on the home screen. 

To enter contact details, enter or paste the recipient’s details and click “Continue.” Pick the cryptocurrency, enter the amount, and add an optional message (e.g., “Lunch money”). Double-check, click “Confirm,” and enter your Pay PIN or complete 2-step verification. The transfer is instantaneous, but double-check it; ultimately, sending to the wrong details is irreversible.

Step 3: Receive Crypto by Sharing QR Code or Binance ID 

To get crypto, navigate to the “Pay” tab within the app and click “Receive.” A QR code will appear; share it by saving the image or sending it through WhatsApp, email, or other apps. For a desired amount of crypto, click “Set Currency/Amount,” select the coin (e.g., BNB or ETH), enter the desired amount, and add a comment if you prefer. Click “Confirm” to create a one-off QR code. 

Alternatively, you can share your Binance account email, phone number, or your Binance ID (in “User Center”). After the payer makes the payment, the crypto ends up directly in your Funding Wallet, and you’ll be notified by email or SMS.

Can You Pay Someone on Binance?

Yes, you can pay someone on Binance using Binance Pay. You just need their Pay ID, email, phone number, or you can scan their Binance Pay QR code. Open the Binance app, tap on “Pay,” choose “Send,” and enter their details. Select the crypto you want to send, enter the amount, and tap “Confirm.” The payment will be sent instantly with no fees. Both you and the person must have Binance accounts to use this feature. You can also read our in-depth Binance review to get full information about the exchange.

What Is Binance Pay ID?

Binance Pay ID is a special numerical code that Binance automatically assigns to your account when you enable Binance Pay. It is an individual code that allows other Binance members to send you cryptocurrency directly into the Binance Pay system. You cannot change or personalize your Pay ID like a username or email address. Your Pay ID is generated by Binance and is tied to your account specifically.

Use Binance Pay to handle all your crypto transfers in one place with no fees, fast delivery, and a smooth experience every time you send or receive funds.

Where to Find Binance Pay ID?

To find your Binance Pay ID, log in to your Binance account via the mobile app or website. Now, you need to navigate to the “Pay” section, where your Pay ID will be displayed along with a corresponding QR code. You can share this Pay ID with others who wish to send you crypto, as this provides a straightforward and secure method for transactions within the Binance ecosystem.

Is Binance Pay Legal in India?

Yes, Binance Pay is legal for use in India as of 2025. Binance has formally registered with the Financial Intelligence Unit of India (FIU-IND), enabling it to operate lawfully by being compliant with local laws, particularly anti-money laundering (AML) regulations. This registration enables Indian users to access Binance services, such as Binance Pay, as long as they undergo the required Know Your Customer (KYC) verification procedure.

content:
Binance margin trading is a trading strategy on Binance that allows traders to borrow crypto to trade with more capital than they currently own. Here, you use the crypto in your account as collateral and borrow extra funds to open larger trades with up to 20x leverage.

Using margin on Binance allows you to increase your trade size, take advantage of price movements, and manage positions without needing to sell your long-term holdings. 

It also gives you more room to hedge or adjust your trades quickly. This means you can earn more from a good setup, but you also carry the risk of losing borrowed funds. For instance, if your margin level drops too low, Binance can forcibly close your trade to recover the loan.

For a better understanding of Binance margin trading, this guide explains how Binance margin trading works, the fees and interest rates of margin trading on Binance, and how it compares to spot and futures trading. You will also learn how to set up your margin account, move funds, and place your first trade.

What is Binance Margin Trading?

Binance Margin Trading is a feature on the Binance cryptocurrency exchange that allows users to borrow funds against their existing holdings to trade with leverage, to potentially increase profits. Maximum leverage varies by trading pair and account type. While Cross Margin can go up to 20x and Isolated up to 10x, many pairs have lower caps based on risk level and liquidity.

While leveraged trading enables traders to amplify profits, it also carries a high risk of potential loss due to leverage and potential liquidation if margin levels fall below thresholds.

To simplify margin trading, Binance offers tools like auto-transfer, auto-borrow, and auto-repay. Auto-transfer automates fund transfers between Spot and Margin wallets, auto-borrow automates borrowing funds when placing margin orders, and auto-repay repays loans with proceeds from closed trades.

Start margin trading on Binance today and earn monetary rewards to boost your trading capital.

What are the Pros and Cons of Margin Trading on Binance?

The pros of margin trading on Binance are listed below:

  • Access to More Capital: You can trade with more than what you have. Once you move assets into your margin account, you get access to borrowed funds. This lets you enter bigger trades with less capital.
  • Wide Range of Trading Pairs and Options: You’re not limited to one or two coins. Binance supports 600+ margin trading pairs, so traders are not stuck waiting for one market to move.
  • Updates Borrowing and Margin Level: The platform updates everything while you trade. You see your margin level, how much you’ve borrowed, and how close you are to liquidation as the price changes. It keeps you informed without needing extra tools.
  • Built-in Risk Management Tools Like Stop Loss (SL) and Take Profit (TP): You can set stop loss and take profit on every margin trade. Stop loss and take profit are limits set on trades (market or pending) so that they are automatically closed at an expected gain or a minimal loss. This helps you manage risk and plan exits.
  • Direct Integration: Margin trading happens right inside the Binance ecosystem. Whether you are trading through the Binance app or website, there is no need to use third-party tools or open multiple tabs. Everything from transferring funds to repaying loans is handled in Binance Exchange.
  • Customer Support: Binance offers 24/7 support through live chat and email. If you need answers to frequently asked questions, you can get help through the live chat or the FAQ section. However, if you need help with more complex issues, you can contact the support team via email.

In addition to these channels, Binance is popular for providing users with extensive learning tools, including articles, videos, tutorials and other educational content through Binance Academy. With these materials, you can easily learn how to trade on the exchange and get answers to your questions at all times.

The cons of margin trading on Binance are listed below:

  • Potential Losses and Risk of Liquidation: When the trade moves against you and your margin level drops, Binance starts to close your position. This can lead to losing more than you expected. Also, if the margin level drops below the set range, Binance can forcibly close (liquidate) your position.
  • Borrowed Funds are Not Free: As long as you keep the position open, interest is added to what you owe. The longer you hold, the more it costs. Nevertheless, this won’t be much of a problem if your trades are profitable.
  • Crypto Markets Move Mast. A sudden dip can bring your margin down before you have time to act. Even if the price recovers later, your position might already be gone.
  • Leverage Goes Both Ways: While it can help grow profits, it also means small mistakes can turn into large losses. So, you need to keep an eye on your trades at all times.

How Does Margin Trading Work in Binance?

Margin trading on Binance works by allowing users to borrow funds to increase their trading capital and amplify potential returns. First, you transfer funds into your margin wallet. That becomes the base Binance uses to calculate how much you can borrow. And the higher the value of your deposit, the more leverage you can access, up to 10x leverage on Isolated Margin and up to 20x on Cross Margin.

Next, you choose the trading pair and open a position. You can go long if you believe the asset will rise, or short if you expect a drop. Now, you’re trading with more than you own; both your original deposit and the borrowed funds are combined in that trade. If the price moves in your favor, you close the trade, repay the borrowed amount with interest, and keep the profit.

However, if the market turns against your position, your margin level starts to fall. If it drops too far, Binance can liquidate your position automatically. This means your assets will be sold off to recover the loan. 

Binance offers different modes for margin trading orders. You can either borrow and repay funds manually or allow the system automatically borrow the required assets based on maximum leverage when placing an order. For the automated repayment, the system automatically uses the proceeds to repay the borrowed amount after closing the trade.

Please note: Borrowed funds accrue interest charged hourly. Additionally, when repaying loans, you must repay the same asset borrowed (e.g., if BTC was borrowed, repayment must be in BTC).

What are the Types of Margin Trading on Binance?

The two types of margin trading on Binance are Cross Margin and Isolated Margin. Here is a rundown of the difference between Cross vs. Isolated Margin.

  1. Cross Margin: In Cross Margin mode, all the balances in your margin account are pooled together as collateral for all your open margin positions. This means that if one position is losing, other assets in your margin account can be used to cover margin requirements, potentially preventing the liquidation of a single position.

However, the risk of Binance Cross Margin trading is that losses in one trade can affect all your margin positions since the collateral is shared across all trades. This mode is suitable for traders who want to maximize the use of their total margin balance and are comfortable with the risk spreading across positions.

  1. Isolated Margin: In Isolated Margin mode, each trading pair has its own separate margin account with a specific amount of collateral allocated to it. Here, only specific cryptocurrencies can be transferred in, held, and borrowed in a specific isolated margin account. For instance, if you want to invest in ETHUSDT isolated margin account, only ETH and USDT are accessible.

If the market moves against a particular trade, only the collateral allocated to that trade is at risk of liquidation, protecting the rest of your margin balance from being affected. Unlike the Cross Margin mode, this mode allows better risk management on individual trades and is suitable for traders who want to limit their risk exposure per position.

What are the Fees and Interest Rates for Binance Margin Trading?

Binance charges two main costs when trading on margin, the regular trading fee and interest on the borrowed funds. The trading fee depends on your VIP level and whether the order is a maker or taker. Most users on a basic account pay around 0.1 percent per trade. That amount can drop with higher trading volume or if there’s enough BNB in the account to qualify for up to 20% BNB holders discount.

However, interest is charged separately and only applies to the amount borrowed. The rate depends on the coin, your VIP level, and can change depending on market activity. Interest starts the moment the loan is active and continues until the balance is fully repaid. The longer the trade stays open, the more interest builds up.

Access a $100 welcome bonus, live interest rates, and flexible borrowing with Binance margin trading.

What Are the Borrowing Limits for Binance Margin Trading?

Borrowing limits in Binance margin trading depend on the asset, the margin mode, and your VIP level. Traders with more trading volume (high VIP status) are eligible for more borrow limits compared to regular users. Below is the loan rate and borrowing limit for regular traders.

Aside from the VIP level, each coin available for margin has a set borrowing cap. Assets that are traded more often and have more liquidity typically allow higher limits, while smaller or less liquid coins cap borrowing at lower levels.

In cross margin, all assets in the margin wallet work together as collateral. That means borrowing power is based on the total value of everything in that wallet. As long as the combined balance holds up, larger positions are possible. However, if one position starts losing, it puts pressure on the entire account.

Now, the isolated margin treats each trade separately. When opening a position, only the funds assigned to that trade back the loan. That keeps risk limited to that one position, but the borrowing room is smaller because it’s tied only to that pair.

The actual borrowing amount also depends on your margin level, the ratio between your assets and what you’ve borrowed plus interest. If your margin level drops near liquidation, Binance may restrict additional borrowing to protect the platform and reduce your exposure. The platform adjusts limits in real time when the market moves sharply.

To know exactly how much you can borrow, the Margin Data page on Binance shows live limits for each asset.

What is the Difference Between Spot and Margin Trading on Binance?

Spot trading on Binance is a straightforward transaction where you buy or sell cryptocurrency using your own funds. When you place a spot order, you exchange one asset for another immediately or when your limit is filled. For example, if you want to buy Bitcoin using USDT, the full amount must already be in your wallet. Once the order is executed, the asset becomes yours without any debt or additional obligations.

Margin trading, on the other hand, involves borrowing funds from Binance to increase your buying power. You still start with your own capital, but the platform allows you to borrow more and open a larger position than your actual balance would allow. This means if your trade goes in the right direction, the gains and losses can be much bigger than in spot trading.

Another key difference is the way positions are managed on spot vs. margin trading. Spot trades do not require monitoring beyond their entry and exit strategy. There’s no debt, no interest, and no liquidation risk. In margin trading, each open position is tied to the loaned funds and is constantly monitored by the system. If the margin level falls too low, Binance can automatically liquidate your position to recover the borrowed amount.

Spot trading is for users who want direct ownership of crypto and less risk. Margin trading is designed for those who are confident in market direction and want to trade with leverage. The risk is higher, but so is the reward.

What is the Difference Between Futures and Margin Trading on Binance?

Margin trading on Binance involves borrowing funds to trade larger amounts than your actual balance allows. You put down a portion of the trade’s value as collateral and borrow the rest from the platform. You are charged interest on the borrowed funds, and your assets serve as security. You still own the assets you buy, and the trades happen on the spot market. That means you’re buying or selling real cryptocurrencies.

Binance Futures trading works differently. You are not trading actual coins. Instead, you are trading contracts that track the price of cryptocurrencies. You don’t own the asset, but you can still profit from its movement. These contracts allow you to bet on future prices of crypto assets.

There’s no interest charged like in margin trading, but there is a funding fee that shifts between buyers and sellers based on market conditions. One similarity you will see in Binance margin or futures, is leverage and liquidation risk. Futures contracts also offer leverage, which is often higher than margin trading (up to 125x), but the risk of liquidation is greater too.

How to Margin Trade Crypto on Binance?

Here is a step-by-step guide on how to margin trade crypto on Binance.

Step 1: Enable Margin Trading on the Binance App or Website

Start by logging in to your Binance account. From the main dashboard, navigate to your wallet and click on the margin section. If you haven’t, you will be prompted to complete identity verification and accept Binance’s margin trading terms.

Step 2: Transfer Funds into Your Margin Wallet

To begin trading, move funds from your spot wallet into your margin wallet. This amount will serve as your collateral. Based on your deposit value, Binance calculates how much you can borrow. The more you fund your wallet, the higher your borrowing power.

Step 3: Borrow and Choose a Trading Pair

With funds in your margin wallet, select the crypto pair you want to trade. Binance allows you to borrow additional assets to increase your position size. You can then decide whether to go long or short depending on the market direction. If you expect the asset to rise in value, you go long. If you expect it to fall, you go short.

Step 4: Place Your Order and Monitor Your Margin Level

After choosing your trading pair and borrowing funds, place your order. Binance gives you the option to use either cross or isolated margin. Cross margin uses all the funds in your margin wallet to protect open trades, while isolated margin limits risk to the specific trade. 

Once your position is open, monitor your margin level closely to avoid liquidation. If it falls below the required threshold, Binance will liquidate your position to recover the borrowed funds.

How to Set Up a Margin Account on Binance?

To use Binance Margin for trading, you need to activate margin trading on your account.  Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to set up a margin account on Binance from scratch.

Step 1: Log In and Complete Identity Verification: Start by signing in to your Binance account. If you don’t have one yet, create an account via the Binance app or official website using a valid email address and a strong password.

Then, complete the KYC verification process. This step is necessary before you can access any margin-related features. If you’re new to the platform, consider checking out a detailed Binance review first to understand how it works and whether it fits your trading goals.

Now is the moment to join Binance and try margin trading.

Step 2: Navigate to the Margin Trading Section: Once your identity has been verified, head to the “Wallet” section at the top of the screen. From there, select “Margin” and you will be taken to the Binance Margin interface. You’ll be required to complete a short quiz about the risks of margin trading before continuing.

Step 3: Enable Margin Trading: After completing the quiz, you can enable your margin wallet. Binance will ask you to confirm that you understand the risks involved. Once you accept the terms, your margin wallet becomes active, and you can start transferring funds into it.

Step 4: Transfer Funds and Begin Trading: Move funds from your spot wallet into your margin wallet to begin trading. Once the funds reflect, you can borrow assets and start margin trading across supported pairs.

If you’re opening your first margin account, Binance occasionally offers exclusive bonuses to new users, including lower trading fees and rewards on your first trades. Check out this Binance referral code article to see how these bonuses work and how to qualify.

How to Qualify for Binance Margin Trading?

Before you can borrow funds or place trades using leverage on Binance, you need to meet a few key requirements. These steps help protect your funds and ensure that you understand the risks involved.

  1. Complete Identity Verification

This is the first and most crucial step. Binance needs to know who is using the platform. You’ll be asked to upload a government-issued ID and a clear photo of yourself. The identity verification process enables Binance to comply with international regulations and provides an additional layer of security for your account.

  1. Pass the Margin Trading Quiz

After your identity has been verified, Binance will prompt you to take a short quiz. The questions focus on how margin trading works, the risks of using borrowed funds, and what can happen when the market turns against you. The purpose of this quiz is to check that you understand the basics before you start trading with leverage. You’ll need to pass this quiz before Binance will unlock margin trading features for your account.

  1. Agree to the Margin Account Terms

Once the quiz is done, you will be shown a set of terms and conditions. This is where Binance outlines how the margin system works, what happens during liquidation, and how interest is calculated on borrowed funds. Accepting these terms means you are aware of your responsibilities and the platform’s policies.

  1. Check for Regional Restrictions

Binance does not offer margin trading in every country. Specific locations are blocked due to legal or regulatory reasons. Even if your identity is verified, you won’t be able to activate margin trading if Binance has restrictions in your region. To avoid confusion, it’s a good idea to check Binance’s list of supported countries before opening a margin trading account.

  1. Keep a Clean Account Record

Binance may withhold margin access if your account has unresolved issues. This could include suspicious activity, incomplete verification, or flagged transactions. If you’ve used the platform for a while, keeping your account history clean can help avoid delays when applying for margin access.

Take advantage of new user rewards and start trading with 10% fee discounts on Binance margin pairs.

How to Transfer Collateral on Binance Margin?

Below is a step-by-step guide on how to transfer collateral on Binance margin 

Step 1. Log in to Your Binance Account: Begin by signing in and navigating to the Wallet section. From the available options, select Margin Wallet. This is where you’ll find your available balance, borrowed funds, and margin level.

Step 2. Click the Transfer Button: Inside your margin wallet, locate and click the Transfer button. This will open a short form that allows you to transfer funds internally from your Spot Wallet to your Margin Wallet.

Step 3. Choose the Crypto You Want to Use: Choose which asset you want to transfer. Binance allows you to use coins like Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT, or BNB as collateral. Your choice here depends on what you already own and what you’re comfortable using.

Step 4. Enter the Amount and Confirm: Type in how much you’d like to transfer. The more you transfer, the more you can borrow, so keep your risk level in mind. After checking everything, confirm the transfer.

Step 5. Wait for Instant Confirmation: Your collateral will reflect in your margin wallet almost right away. Since the funds are being moved within Binance, there’s no fee or delay. Once the transfer is done, you’re ready to borrow and begin margin trading.

What Are the Best Margin Trading Tips for Binance Beginners?

Here are six beginner-friendly tips to help you manage risk and build confidence while margin trading on Binance.

  1. Start Small and Observe: Margin trading offers leverage, which can multiply both profits and losses. That’s why it’s better to begin with a small trade and invest only an amount you’re willing to lose. Use this early stage to observe how price movements affect your borrowed position and how quickly markets can change.
  2. Use Isolated Margin Mode: For new traders, using isolated margin is a safer starting point. It allows you to contain your risk in one position, rather than tying multiple trades together. If things go wrong, you only lose the funds assigned to that trade. That’s different from cross margin, where one bad trade could drain your entire margin account.
  3. Don’t Borrow the Maximum Limit: Just because you can borrow more doesn’t mean you should. Margin gives you access to extra funds, but it’s smart to borrow only what you can manage. Going all-in reduces your cushion and increases your risk of liquidation. Keep your leverage low, especially in the beginning, until you’re more comfortable managing price swings.
  4. Watch Your Margin Level: Your margin level tells you how healthy your position is. If it falls too low, Binance will automatically liquidate your trade to recover the borrowed amount. That’s why it’s essential to monitor your open position often.
  5. Set Clear Stop-Losses: Markets can move fast, and it’s easy to get caught off guard. A stop-loss acts as your safety brake; it closes your trade when prices fall below a certain point. This tool is especially helpful when you’re not watching the charts 24/7. Always plan your exit before you enter the trade.
  6. Reflect on Every Trade: After closing a trade, take time to go back and review it. Ask yourself what worked, what didn’t, and what you would do differently in the future. These small reflections help you spot patterns and avoid repeating mistakes.

Does Binance U.S Offer Margin Trading?

No, Binance US does not offer margin trading. This is mainly due to stricter financial regulations in the United States. Margin trading involves borrowing funds to trade larger amounts, which adds a higher level of risk. US regulators have tighter rules around this kind of trading to protect retail and institutional investors.

Can I Withdraw Margin Money?

No, you cannot withdraw borrowed margin funds on Binance. The money is strictly for trading and stays in your margin account until you repay it. However, any unused funds you personally deposited, not borrowed, can be moved back to your spot wallet and withdrawn.
